_meta.purpose: CPA practice-privilege (mobility) rules, per state, for mobility.ts.
_meta.staged_by_design: Records are added in batches, each with a primary-source citation. A state ABSENT from `records` returns not_verified from the engine, which is the intended behavior, not a gap to fill with guesses. NEVER add a state without a citation just to make coverage look complete -- mobility.ts will refuse to emit a permissive verdict for an uncited row anyway (requireCitationOrDowngrade), so an uncited entry buys nothing and risks a wrong answer.
_meta.evidence_standard: Same as data/cpa_deadlines.json: prefer BOTH the state board's own page (source_url) AND the codified statute/administrative rule (citation + citation_url). `confidence` records which was achieved -- dual_source, single_source, or unverified. Any field that could not be verified is null with an explanatory data_gap_note; null NEVER means 'not required'.
_meta.liability_note: A wrong permissive answer here means a CPA practices without authority. Conservative default is mandatory: when in doubt, leave it null.
_meta.batch_status: Batch 1 research returned. Illinois has a full primary-source record but is IN FLUX (see above) and must ship flagged, not clean. Texas/California/New York/Florida findings were prose-only in that pass and need their records finalised before commit. NOTHING committed yet -- the engine degrades honestly to not_verified for every state meanwhile.
_meta.schema_note_2026_07_30: equivalence_test is REQUIRED and cannot be inferred. Primary-source research found the states are actively diverging on what substantial equivalence even means: Texas abandoned NASBA state-level equivalency for an individual-criteria test (SB 522, eff. 2025-09-01); Illinois adopted NASBA NQAS state-level equivalency (P.A. 104-0228, eff. 2026-01-01); New York moves to individual criteria 2026-11-21. A single boolean 'is the home state substantially equivalent?' encodes the WRONG question for whichever kind a state does not use, so the engine refuses to interpret the user's attestation until this field is set.
_meta.verification_ttl: Rows EXPIRE after MOBILITY_VERIFICATION_TTL_DAYS (180) and expiry downgrades to not_verified rather than merely warning. Four of five priority states changed or will change mobility rules inside a 14-month window (2025-09-01 to 2026-11-21), so treating verification as durable would make this dataset confidently wrong within months. Put known changeover dates in rule_changes_on.
_meta.rule_in_flux: Set true when primary sources DISAGREE or a change is mid-flight, and the engine will decline to answer for that state entirely. Illinois is the live example: enrolled P.A. 104-0228 and the compiled ILCS text state different tests for the same section, and the compiled text cites the very act that contradicts it. Do not resolve such a conflict in the data -- flag it and let the user confirm with the board.

_meta.schema_note_2026_08_08: Roadmap #317 Phase 1 adds home_state_substantially_equivalent (+ its paired home_state_substantially_equivalent_note) to every record -- a HOME-state fact (is a CPA licensed here, in good standing, substantially equivalent under the UAA three-E's test?), independent of equivalence_test above (which is about what a state requires of an INCOMING out-of-state CPA as a TARGET state -- a different question). Source: NASBA's own Substantial Equivalency tracking page (https://nasba.org/licensure/substantialequivalency/, checked 2026-08-08), which states all 55 jurisdictions are currently substantially equivalent, with two carve-outs that keep this field from being a blanket true: (1) 'two-tier' states (AL/CT/HI/IL/KS/NE/OK) whose INITIAL certificates don't qualify, only active licenses/permits -- already covered by the engine's existing licenseInGoodStanding gate (checked before this field is ever read), so those 7 are still marked true here; (2) New York and Ohio's 'Legacy Pathway' carve-out -- an individual licensed post-2012 via either state's alternative pathway is NOT eligible for mobility practice privileges elsewhere, a fact about the INDIVIDUAL this dataset has no way to know from state-level data alone. Those two are left null (unverified) rather than guessed true, with the carve-out explained in their own home_state_substantially_equivalent_note -- consistent with equivalence_test already being 'individual_criteria'-bound for New York's target-state role, not a coincidence: both fields independently land on 'this state needs an individual fact, not a state-level one.'

records.citation: Ala. Code § 34-1-7 (practice privilege; Act 2009-620 scheme); Ala. Code §§ 34-1-6, 34-1-10, 34-1-11, 34-1-16(12) (firm registration/permits, attest exception); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (Mobility); all as amended by HB59, 2026 Reg. Sess. (Pathways to CPA Act), eff. 2026-10-01
records.flux_note: HB59 (2026 Reg. Sess., 'Pathways to CPA Act', Rep. Underwood) passed House 20-Jan-26, Senate 22-Jan-26, signed by Gov. Ivey late Jan 2026. Section 3 states a flat effective date: 'This act shall become effective on October 1, 2026.' -- no supermajority/immediate-effect option, so no vote-count analysis needed. It rewrites 34-1-7(a): current law grants practice privilege to any 'person who is licensed as a certified public accountant in another state' (open CPA=CPA, no equivalency test); from 2026-10-01 the individual must ALSO have 'satisfied the educational requirements adopted by rule of the board' -- i.e., Alabama moves to individual-criteria mobility with the education test delegated to board rule. Board rulemaking defining those educational requirements is pending (secondary sources report proposed pathway rules circulating with an Oct 15, 2026 reference); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (last amended eff. 2009-12-23) and the board's mobility web page still state only the pre-HB59 open-license test -- not a present-day contradiction because HB59 is not yet effective, but both will be stale on 2026-10-01 unless updated. Firm-side rules (no registration for firms with no Alabama office, including for attest via the 34-1-16(12) exception for individuals practicing under 34-1-7) are carried forward substantively unchanged by HB59. UPDATE (verifier): ASBPA Notice of Intended Action amending Ch. 30-X-4 filed with LSA 2026-05-08 (comment period closed 2026-07-10); it does NOT amend 30-X-3-.04 and does NOT yet supply the 34-1-7(a) education rule for out-of-state privilege holders. HB59 signing date confirmed: Gov. Ivey announced signing 2026-01-30 ("I have signed HB59, the Pathways to CPA Act"); act number still unlocated - open question retained.
records.data_gap_note: No stable official per-section URL exists for compiled Ala. Code 34-1-7: the old alisondb.legislature.state.al.us code URLs are dead (DNS failure), the new ALISON Code of Alabama browser (https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/code-of-alabama) is an app without per-section deep links, and Justia returns 403 to plain fetchers. The compiled-statute leg therefore rests on the enrolled HB59 act text on the legislature's site (whose stricken baseline text shows current 34-1-7 verbatim, matching the 2023 compiled code) plus the official Administrative Code (admincode.legislature.state.al.us). HB59's assigned Act number (Act 2026-___) was not located.
records.notes: Current scheme (Act 2009-620, in force until 2026-09-30): pure open-mobility. Any CPA licensed in ANY state with principal place of business outside Alabama gets all practice privileges -- no notice, no fee, no registration, no substantial-equivalency or NASBA state-level test (hence equivalence_test='other': open CPA=CPA; becomes individual_criteria 2026-10-01 under HB59). Firms: Alabama firm registration (34-1-6/34-1-10) and annual permits (34-1-11) apply to firms with Alabama offices; Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04(1) states flatly that no firm or office not located in the state must register, and the board's mobility page agrees. Attest: 34-1-16(12) requires attest services to be performed in a firm holding an Alabama permit EXCEPT for a person/individual practicing pursuant to 34-1-7 -- so out-of-state CPAs/firms without an Alabama office may perform attest for Alabama clients without firm registration. Peer review: conditions renewal of the Alabama firm/individual permit (34-1-11(a)(3) compilation; 34-1-16(13)b), NOT the out-of-state practice privilege -- so false for mobility practice; a firm that opens an Alabama office and registers would face it. Out-of-state practitioners/firms are deemed to consent to board jurisdiction, Alabama law compliance, cease-practice-if-home-license-invalid, and service-of-process agency (34-1-7(b); rule 30-X-3-.04(2)). NOTE: starting hint 'HB 277 (2025)' appears wrong -- no such Alabama CPA bill found; the operative act is HB59, 2026 Regular Session. Board mobility page miscites its own rule as 30-X-7-.13 (actually 'Return of Certificate'); the real mobility rule is 30-X-3-.04. UPDATE (verifier - quote correction): the peer-review quote previously captured included STRICKEN enrolled-act text; the operative amended text (enrolled HB59 p.17) reads: "The board, by rule, shall require as a condition for renewal of a permit that any permit holder who performs compilation services for the public other than through a CPA or PA firm undergo, not more frequently than once every three years, a peer review." Cite as 34-1-11(a)(2) (current, through 2026-09-30) / 34-1-11(a)(3) (as renumbered by HB59 from 2026-10-01). peer_review_required=false for out-of-state privilege firms stands on the corrected reading.

records.citation: AS 08.04.420 (practice privileges); AS 08.04.422 (conditions of practice privileges); AS 08.04.240 (firm permit — subsection (k), the former out-of-state attest-firm permit, repealed by sec. 22, ch. 22, SLA 2025); AS 08.04.565 (attest through a firm); AS 08.04.426 (peer review); 12 AAC 04.245; 12 AAC 04.251; 12 AAC 04.285; 12 AAC 04.600. Amending act: HB 121, ch. 22, SLA 2025 (34th Leg.), eff. Jan. 1, 2026.
records.flux_note: Two things put Alaska in flux. (1) COMPLETED 2025-26 CHANGEOVER: HB 121 (34th Leg.) became law without the governor's signature on 2025-07-23 as CHAPTER 22 SLA 25. Enrolled sec. 24: 'Except as provided in sec. 23 of this Act, this Act takes effect January 1, 2026.' Sec. 23 gave immediate effect under AS 01.10.070(c) only to secs. 14-21 (the private-professional-conservator/probate provisions); ALL accounting provisions (secs. 1-13 and 22) are governed by the fixed Jan. 1, 2026 date, so no supermajority-conditioned immediate-effect analysis applies to them. (Final passage was in any event unanimous and far above two-thirds of members elected: House PASSED Y38 E2 and concurred in the Senate amendment Y40 of 40 elected; Senate PASSED Y20 N- of 20 elected; the legislature's bill history records '(H) EFFECTIVE DATE(S) OF LAW SEE CHAPTER'.) HB 121 sec. 4 struck the entire substantial-equivalency test out of AS 08.04.420(a) (the [BRACKETED CAPITALS] 150-hour / exam / 1-year-experience / individually-substantially-equivalent conditions are deleted language), sec. 5 extended the no-notice/no-fee clause of AS 08.04.420(c) from individuals to firms, sec. 6 added firm mobility at AS 08.04.420(d)-(e), sec. 13 amended AS 08.04.565 to let attest be performed through a firm operating under a practice privilege, and sec. 22 repealed AS 08.04.240(k) (the former out-of-state attest-firm permit). (2) LIVE PRIMARY-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm_registration_attest: the compiled, still-in-force administrative rule 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) (official Alaska Administrative Code at akleg.gov, and reprinted unchanged in the board's own Rev. 1/01/2026 'Statutes and Regulations Public Accountancy') states that a firm 'must obtain a permit issued by the board under this chapter if the firm ... (2) does not have an established and maintained office in the state but provides, or offers to provide, attest functions in the state under AS 08.04.240(k)'. Its operative statutory hook, AS 08.04.240(k), was REPEALED effective 2026-01-01, and AS 08.04.420(d) + AS 08.04.565(2) now authorize attest through an out-of-state no-office firm under a practice privilege. The board's last accountancy rulemaking was adopted 2025-06-05, filed 2025-06-26 and effective 2025-07-26 (Register 255, Oct. 2025) — it predates HB 121's effective date and did not touch 12 AAC 04.245, so the rule has not been conformed. Statute and compiled rule therefore state OPPOSITE answers for firm_registration_attest; per the conservative rule this record carries TRUE, not the permissive value. Note that the board's own current guidance sides with the statute (see notes), so the practical answer is very likely 'no permit required' — but that is not what the codified rule says today.
records.data_gap_note: firm_registration_attest and peer_review_required are recorded at their CONSERVATIVE values because of the 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) / AS 08.04.240(k) conflict described in flux_note; they are NOT clean dual-source affirmatives. Every other field is clean dual-source. Separately, the board's HTML pages on commerce.alaska.gov (including the Board of Public Accountancy landing page and Applications & Forms page) return HTTP 403 to non-browser fetchers, so the board leg here rests on three PDF publications served from the board's own portal directory rather than on its HTML pages; those PDFs were fetched and read in full.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: AS 08.04.420(a) grants a practice privilege to any individual who is not licensed in Alaska, IS licensed to practice public accounting in another state, and whose principal place of business is in that other state. As amended by HB 121 sec. 4 the subsection contains NO equivalency, education, exam or experience condition — the old substantial-equivalency test was struck in its entirety. That is open CPA=CPA mobility, hence equivalence_test = 'other' rather than nasba_state_level or individual_criteria. AS 08.04.420(c) expressly removes any notice, fee or documentation obligation, for firms as well as individuals, and permits practice by mail, telephone, electronic means or in person. AS 08.04.422 imposes the usual non-registration conditions (consent to board jurisdiction and discipline, agreement to comply with AS 08.04 and board regulations, cessation if the home-state license lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process). RESIDUAL EQUIVALENCY HOOK — flag this to users: 12 AAC 04.251(b) still provides that the board 'may request' that someone practicing under AS 08.04.420 verify good standing, that the principal place of business matches the state of licensure, OR that 'substantial equivalency qualifications required under 12 AAC 04.285 have been met'; 12 AAC 04.285 defines substantial equivalency by NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service determination at both the state level (a) and the individual level (b). This reads as a discretionary verification power rather than a precondition on the statutory privilege — the statute grants the privilege unconditionally — but it is an unconformed pre-HB-121 rule (12 AAC 04.251 was last amended effective 2025-07-26, before HB 121 took effect) and a CPA could be asked for NASBA SE evidence. 180-DAY TRAP: 12 AAC 04.251(a) provides that an individual who ESTABLISHES a principal place of business in Alaska may practice without an Alaska license for only 180 days and must then apply for licensure by examination, reciprocity, or temporary military courtesy license. Mobility depends on keeping the PPB out of state. FIRM — TAX/NON-ATTEST: clean false. AS 08.04.420(d) gives a practice privilege to a firm that is more than one-half owned by CPAs in good standing (Alaska or another state), has its PPB in another state, and has no Alaska office. 12 AAC 04.245(a) requires a firm permit in only three cases — an office in the state, attest without an office (the disputed (a)(2)), or use of the CPA/PA title, and the title trigger is expressly excepted for a firm 'operating under the requirements of practice privilege'. AS 08.04.510(2) and 08.04.530(2) likewise let a firm use the CPA/PA designation while practising under a practice privilege. So a purely tax/advisory out-of-state firm with no Alaska office registers nothing. This is exactly the case where attest and tax genuinely diverge in Alaska — do not collapse them. FIRM — ATTEST: recorded TRUE conservatively only because of the unconformed 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2). The statutory position is the opposite and is unambiguous: AS 08.04.240(k) (the old out-of-state attest permit, which itself carried an AS 08.04.426 peer-review condition) was repealed by HB 121 sec. 22, AS 08.04.240(a) now issues permits only to 'a firm with an office in the state', and AS 08.04.565 as amended permits attest through a firm that 'is engaging in the practice of public accounting under a practice privilege'. The BOARD'S OWN CURRENT MATERIALS AGREE WITH THE STATUTE, NOT THE RULE: its December 2025 rule-change flyer says 'Effective January 1, 2026 - AK will have firm mobility for firms with a principal place of business outside of AK and no office in AK' (no attest carve-out), and its CPA Firm Permit Initial Application, Rev. 05/13/2026 — i.e. drafted five months AFTER the change — offers the checkbox 'Principal place of business is outside of Alaska and no office in Alaska - Firm permit is optional.' A product should surface the conflict and the optional-permit route rather than assert either extreme. PEER REVIEW: recorded TRUE as a condition OF THE FIRM PERMIT, not of the practice privilege — this is the distinction the field asks about. AS 08.04.426(f) makes peer review a condition of renewal of a firm permit, and 12 AAC 04.600(a) requires a permit holder that issued audit or review reports in the concluding permit period to certify a peer review within the preceding three years (12 AAC 04.620 exempts permit holders that issued no audit/review reports). The board's out-of-state firm permit application requires the firm to certify it 'will comply with the requirements of AS 08.04.426 (Peer Review)'. Nothing in AS 08.04.420 or AS 08.04.422 conditions the no-registration practice privilege itself on peer review; so if the 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) conflict is resolved in favour of the statute, the correct values for both firm_registration_attest and peer_review_required become FALSE. OTHER: the individual pathway also changed — HB 121 sec. 1 repealed the 150-semester-hour requirement, leaving a baccalaureate with an accounting concentration plus two years of experience (AS 08.04.120(a)). Alaska is a single-tier state for practice purposes: AS 08.04.100 says a certificate alone does not authorise practice without a current license or permit. No other accountancy bill was introduced in the 34th Legislature (2025-2026).

records.citation: A.R.S. § 32-725 (limited reciprocity privilege; individuals and out-of-state firms); A.R.S. § 32-731 (CPA firm registration); as amended by Laws 2026, Ch. 17 (SB 1181, Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026) eff. 2027-01-01
records.flux_note: SB 1181 (Laws 2026, Ch. 17, 'Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026') was signed 2026-04-07 and is enacted but NOT YET EFFECTIVE: the act's own Sec. 18 states 'This act is effective from and after December 31, 2026,' i.e. operative 2027-01-01. This in-act delayed date governs (it is later than the session's general effective date of 2026-09-12 after the 2026-06-13 sine die; no emergency clause, so no supermajority vote-count question arises). The act strikes the current A.R.S. 32-725(B)(4) mobility test (licensing jurisdiction requires 150 semester hours + baccalaureate + passed CPA exam + 1 year verified experience, OR individual meets 32-721(C)) and replaces it with: individual holds an out-of-state CPA license AND either (a) meets the qualifications in 32-721(A) (new pathways: baccalaureate+2yrs experience, baccalaureate+30 extra hours+1yr, or postbaccalaureate+1yr) or 32-4302 (Arizona universal-licensure-recognition statute), or (b) holds a valid active CPA registration/certificate/license from any jurisdiction as of December 31, 2024 (grandfather clause). The no-notice/no-fee provision (32-725(D)) and the out-of-state-firm no-registration provision (32-725(G)) are carried forward unchanged (Ch. 17 also adds out-of-state firms to the 'limited reciprocity privilege' definition). The board's Mobility page currently matches the in-force pre-2027 statute (no stale-page disagreement today), but will need updating at the changeover. UPDATE (verifier): Board Notice of Proposed Expedited Rulemaking (July 2026) implements Laws 2026 Ch. 17 - outlines required accounting/related course hours for certification (which feed the 32-721(A) qualifications the NEW 2027 mobility test cross-references) and reduces reciprocity verifications to one jurisdiction; oral proceeding 2026-08-24, final text pending - recheck after adoption. DIFFLAB WARNING: the board News page headline styles the act '(Effective December 31, 2026)' - that is a paraphrase of the act's 'from and after December 31, 2026' clause; the operative date remains 2027-01-01. Do not let an alert on that phrasing trigger a date change. Board also ran 2025-2026 expedited rule updates on peer review (R4-1-454, May 2025) and CPE (May 2026).
records.data_gap_note: peer_review_required=false means peer review is NOT a condition of the out-of-state mobility privilege: neither the six conditions of A.R.S. 32-725(G) (firm no-registration attest privilege) nor A.R.S. 32-731 (registration, which only reaches firms with 'an office in this state') mentions peer review, and the board's Mobility page lists the same conditions without it. Arizona's peer-review program (board 'Firms > Peer Review' pages / board rules) applies to Arizona-registered firms performing attest/compilation; its rule text was not separately fetched because out-of-state firms without an Arizona office are exempt from registration altogether. UPDATE (verifier): peer_review_required=false rests on the statute's exhaustive 32-725(G) conditions, but A.A.C. R4-1-454 as described on the board's Peer Review page ('All firms performing attest services or compilation services are subject to peer review', no express limitation to Arizona-registered firms) is in facial tension; the rule text itself should be fetched and put on file at next re-verification. Value kept false on the statute; treat as the weakest false in this record.
records.notes: Arizona grants individual mobility via the 'limited reciprocity privilege' (A.R.S. 32-725): a nonresident CPA whose principal place of business is outside Arizona, with no Arizona office and no suspension/revocation/relinquishment, has 'all of the privileges of registrants... without obtaining a registration, certificate or license,' and 'A notice, fee or other submission is not required' (32-725(D)) — so no notice AND no fee. FIRMS: under 32-725(G) an out-of-state firm may practice accounting in Arizona 'including the provision of attest services, without having to register as a firm' if 6 conditions are met (owned by/employs a privilege holder, good standing at home, holder's principal place of business is a recognized firm office, no Arizona office or representation of one, active firm permit in another jurisdiction, work performed by/under direct supervision of a privilege holder). Because 32-725(G) covers the whole 'practice of accounting' and 32-731(A) registration applies '[e]xcept as provided in section 32-725, subsection G' and only to firms that have 'an office in this state,' firm_registration is false for BOTH attest and tax/non-attest for firms without an Arizona office (a firm opening an Arizona office loses the exemption and must register biennially). EQUIVALENCE TEST = 'other': a state-specific codified scheme, not NASBA/NQAS reliance — current in-force test checks whether the LICENSING JURISDICTION requires 150 hrs + baccalaureate + passed uniform CPA exam + 1 yr verified experience (UAA-style '3E' written directly into statute, no NASBA reference), with an individual-criteria fallback (32-721(C)); from 2027-01-01 it becomes individual-criteria (meets 32-721(A) or 32-4302) or a grandfather (valid active license held as of 2024-12-31). Attest/compilation reports must be signed by an Arizona certificate holder or a 32-725(G)-qualified person (32-731(B)). Non-qualifying out-of-state/foreign CPAs may still provide expert-witness services, teaching/lecturing, or other board-approved services (32-725(F)).

records.flux_note: Arkansas completed a two-step mobility rewrite in the 2025-26 wave and it is now fully operative. Step 1: Act 428 of 2025 (SB432, approved 2025-04-03; no emergency/effective-date clause, so effective 2025-08-05, the standard 91st-day date after the 2025 regular session's 2025-05-05 sine die adjournment) struck the entire NASBA-NQAS state-level substantial-equivalency practice-privilege text of Ark. Code § 17-12-311 and replaced it with a delegation authorizing the board to 'determine substantial equivalency requirements' and promulgate rules. Step 2: revised board rules (17 CAR Part 236) approved by Arkansas Legislative Council 2026-02-20, published 2026-02-23, effective 2026-03-05, re-defined substantial equivalency at 17 CAR § 236-501 as INDIVIDUAL-criteria mobility (any-state active license + CPA exam + one of three education/experience pathways at initial licensure + CPE at last renewal), with a grandfather clause preserving privileges of out-of-state CPAs holding a valid active license as of 2025-12-31. Board notice, statute, and codified rules all agree; board's proposed-rule-changes page states no proposals pending as of 2026-07-31.
records.data_gap_note: Attest scope nuance: mandatory firm registration for no-office firms covers only § 17-12-103(a)(2)(A) SAS audits, (a)(2)(C) SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and (a)(2)(D) PCAOB engagements for clients with home office in Arkansas. SSARS reviews ((a)(2)(B)), other SSAE examinations/reviews/AUPs ((a)(2)(E)), and compilations ((a)(5)) may be performed for AR home-office clients WITHOUT registration only if the firm meets § 17-12-401 qualifications, works through a practice-privilege individual, and meets § 17-12-508 peer review (§ 17-12-401(b)(2)); firm_registration_attest=true reflects the audit/PFI-examination/PCAOB core.
records.notes: Individual mobility (17 CAR § 236-501(a), eff. 2026-03-05): out-of-state CPA with principal place of business outside AR and a valid active license in good standing from ANY state has all practice privileges without license, notice, registration, or fee, provided at initial licensure the individual passed the CPA exam and met one of three pathways (post-baccalaureate degree + 1 yr experience; bachelor's + 30 extra hrs (150) + 1 yr; bachelor's + 2 yrs) and met CPE at last renewal — an individual-criteria test replacing the pre-Act-428 NASBA-NQAS state-level test. Grandfather: individuals licensed in any state as of 2025-12-31 who then had AR privileges retain them while their license stays valid. Home-office-client audits (SAS), examinations of prospective financial information (SSAE), and PCAOB engagements may be performed only through a firm registered under § 17-12-401 (rule 236-501(a)(4), (b)(2); statute 17-12-401(b)(1)(B)). Firms with no AR office: no registration, notice, or fee for services other than that list — including tax/non-attest — if performed through a privileged individual and lawful in the home state (§ 17-12-401(b)(3); rule 236-501(b)(1)). Peer review: § 17-12-508(a)(1) requires licensees performing attest services to enroll in board-approved peer review every 3 years (registered out-of-state firms doing attest are licensees), and peer review is an express CONDITION of the no-registration privilege for SSARS/other-SSAE/compilation work (§ 17-12-401(b)(2)(C)); rule 236-1302(g) additionally requires out-of-state licensees performing SSARS engagements for AR clients to have an acceptable peer review or home-state quality review. Practice-privilege holders are subject to board jurisdiction, must cease if home-state license lapses, and face title-disclosure rules (236-502) and disqualifiers (236-503: felony, fraud crimes, discipline, denied applications). STARTING HINT CORRECTION: 'HB 1854 / Act 859' is wrong — Act 859 of 2025 is a reproductive-health act; the accountancy act is Act 428 of 2025 (SB432). Board is ASBPA; live site is labor.arkansas.gov (Dept. of Labor and Licensing). UPDATE (verifier): the aside speculating about Act 859 of 2025's subject matter is WITHDRAWN as unverified; the verified accountancy statute of the 2025 session is Act 428 (SB432, lapsed-license reinstatement). Residual drafting artifact worth monitoring: definitions rule 17 CAR 236-100(28) retains a UAA-style state-level prong in its "substantial equivalency" definition even though operative rule 236-501 applies individual criteria.

records.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 5096-5096.22 (Accountancy Act, Art. 5.1 Practice Privileges), as amended by AB 1175 (Stats. 2025, ch. 293), eff. 2026-01-01; esp. §§ 5096(a)-(b) (individual open mobility, no notice/fee), 5096(c) (attest via registered firm), 5096(h) (7-year discipline pre-notification), 5096.12 (out-of-state firm registration)
records.flux_note: AB 1175 (Stats. 2025, ch. 293, signed 2025-10-03, eff. 2026-01-01) replaced California's substantial-equivalency practice privilege with an 'open mobility' framework: any current-and-active out-of-state license qualifies, no notice/fee, and no equivalency test; the CBA may withdraw a specific state's no-notice privilege (BPC 5096.21/5096.22), in which case that state's licensees must file a notification form and pay fees. HOWEVER, the CBA's own Licensee FAQs (last updated 2026-05-04, AFTER the effective date) and practice-privilege pages STILL describe the pre-2026 regime (license from a substantially equivalent state, 4-of-last-10-years practice, or individually equivalent qualifications) - board guidance and the compiled statute currently disagree; practitioner-facing confusion risk is high until CBA guidance conforms. UPDATE (verifier): the CBA has ACTIVE AB 1175 implementation rulemaking (initiated Nov 2025; 16 CCR amendments incl. sections 5.5 and 19 approved Sept 2025 and reauthorized with corrections; 'accounting concentration' definition on the July 2026 board agenda). Separately, AB 1175's licensure-pathway changes phase in 2027-01-01 (new B&P 5093.2/5093.3 pathway) through 2029-01-01 (150-hr legacy route sunset) - licensure, not mobility, but it will change the inbound-CPA population profile. Monitor for CBA guidance/regulation updates and any state-specific privilege withdrawals under 5096.21.
records.data_gap_note: peer_review_required left null: BPC 5096.12 imposes no peer-review condition on out-of-state firm registration, and the CBA's OFR registration (Form PP-13) and renewal forms contain no peer-review section (and no fee), suggesting peer review is NOT a condition of the OFR - but BPC 5076(a) requires peer review for 'a firm, as defined in Section 5035.1' renewing 'its registration in an active status,' and 5035.1's definition does not expressly exclude out-of-state registrants; no primary source affirmatively states the exemption, so this stays unresolved (verifier concurs null is correct). RESOLVED (verifier): the 7-year disciplinary/criminal pre-notification requirement on the CBA's pp_reporting page DOES retain a statutory basis in the post-AB 1175 compiled Article 5.1, at BPC 5096(h).
records.notes: Individual: BPC 5096(a)-(b) (current text, eff. 2026-01-01) grants a practice privilege to any individual whose principal place of business is outside California holding a current, active license from another state; 'a notice, fee, or other requirement shall not be imposed.' Conditions: no California office (except as employee of a registered firm), report criminal charges within 30 days, cease practice on home-state discipline or SEC/PCAOB bar, and perform BPC 5096(c) attest services (audit/review of financial statements, compilations where third-party use expected and independence not disclaimed, examinations of prospective financial information, for entities headquartered in California) only through a firm registered with the CBA. Per BPC 5096(h) (statutory basis verifier-confirmed) and the CBA's pp_reporting page: individuals with specified disciplinary/criminal events in the previous 7 years must submit a Pre-Notification Form and obtain CBA approval BEFORE practicing - a live exception to the no-notice rule. Firm: an out-of-state firm with no California office may practice through privilege holders WITHOUT registration (5096.12(a)); registration (Form PP-13, no fee, renewable every two years at no fee) is required only to perform 5096(c) attest services for California-headquartered entities (5096.12(c)) - tax and other non-attest services trigger no CBA firm registration (Secretary of State foreign-qualification rules may apply separately for intrastate business, per the CBA form notice). Equivalence test: 'other' = open mobility, no equivalency screening at all (neither NASBA state-level nor individual criteria); board retains state-by-state withdrawal power (5096.21/5096.22). Pre-2026 rules (substantial equivalency; no-notice no-fee since 2013-07-01) remain visible on stale CBA pages.

records.flux_note: SB26-076 (signed 2026-05-04, Ch. 81) rewrites CRS 12-100-117(2)(a)(I): from 2026-08-12 an individual out-of-state CPA licensed in good standing with principal place of business elsewhere has ALL the same practice privileges as Colorado certificate holders if, at initial licensure, their licensing state required passing the Uniform CPA Exam and a baccalaureate degree (individual-criteria/near-CPA=CPA test replacing the current NASBA-substantial-equivalency test in Rule 1.14); CPAs holding CO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31 are grandfathered, and the board is statutorily barred from requiring any notice, fee, or other submission. Effective-date verification: the act uses Colorado's standard referendum-petition clause (no supermajority immediate-effect mechanism exists in CO), so the remainder of the act takes effect the day after the 90-day post-adjournment period (GA adjourned 2026-05-13); leg.colorado.gov's official bill history lists '08/12/2026 - Effective date'; only section 1 (12-100-108 licensure pathways: BA+2yr experience / BA+30hr+1yr / post-bacc+1yr) is delayed to 2027-01-01. SB26-076 § 3 also narrows the firm-registration exception cross-reference in 12-100-114(1) from '12-100-117(2)' to '12-100-117(2)(a)(II)' (firm incident-to exception only). Source-disagreement flags: (1) Board Rule 1.14 (3 CCR 705-1, current version eff. 12/15/2024) still states the superseded NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalency test; conforming board rulemaking is pending (COCPA reports notice-comment-hearing phase next; hearings to post at dpo.colorado.gov/Accountancy_Program_Info, which itself shows stale 2019-2022 content). (2) COCPA (secondary) claims the mobility provisions take effect only when the board adopts implementing rules — the act's own effective-date clause contains no such condition; act text controls.
records.data_gap_note: The firm no-registration exception (CRS 12-100-117(2)(a)(II)) applies only when Colorado work is 'incident to the entity's regular practice outside this state, as defined by the board' — but current rules define 'incident to' only for foreign-country individuals (Rule 1.14.D.3), not U.S. out-of-state firms, so the exemption boundary is undefined; conservative position: a firm with substantial/recurring Colorado engagements (attest OR tax) must register. Board web guidance on mobility is thin: dpo.colorado.gov has no dedicated mobility page found; the Program Info page is visibly stale; several dpo.colorado.gov paths 403 non-browser fetchers.
records.notes: COLORADO IS MID-CHANGEOVER (verified 12 days before switch). CURRENT LAW (through 2026-08-11): individual out-of-state CPAs practice under CRS 12-100-117(2)(a)(I) + Rule 1.14 with NO notice and NO fee, based on NASBA NQAS SE verification — state-level verification (Rule 1.14.B.1.a(2)) with an individual-level NQAS fallback for CPAs from non-SE states (Rule 1.14.B.1.a(3)); hence equivalence_test = nasba_state_level (with individual fallback). NEW LAW (from 2026-08-12): test becomes individual criteria — licensed in good standing + out-of-state principal place of business + licensing state required exam passage and baccalaureate at initial licensure; still no notice/fee (statutorily prohibited). FIRMS: Colorado's firm registration (12-100-114(1)) is NOT attest-scoped — it attaches to being 'engaged in this state in the practice of public accounting', and the rule-defined 'Practice of Public Accounting' expressly includes tax return preparation and tax advice, so firm_registration_attest AND firm_registration_tax are both TRUE for firms engaged in Colorado practice; the sole out-of-state-firm exemption is the incident-to-out-of-state-practice exception (117(2)(a)(II) + Rule 1.14.B.2), which is service-type-neutral. Attest without a certificate or registration is separately prohibited by 12-100-116(1)(a)(II) subject to the 117 exceptions. PEER REVIEW: TRUE as a condition of firm registration RENEWAL for registrants issuing attest or compilation reports (12-100-114(7); Rules 1.11.A, 1.15.D.3) — it is NOT a condition of the individual practice privilege or of the firm incident-to exemption; non-attest/non-compilation registrants are exempt (Rule 1.11.B). Statute hint in tasking (12-100-114 as the mobility cite) was wrong: 12-100-114 is firm registration; mobility is 12-100-117(2). Evidence basis: board division site (dpo.colorado.gov/LegUpdates) + official CCR (coloradosos.gov, version eff. 12/15/2024, ruleVersionId 11720) + official CRS 2024 printout (leg.colorado.gov OLLS) + Final Act (leg.colorado.gov). CRS 2024 edition predates SB26-076; the act text supplies the amended language.

records.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-281n (repealed and replaced by P.A. 25-36, § 4, eff. Oct. 1, 2025); Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 20-281e(g)-(i), 20-281(b)
records.flux_note: P.A. 25-36 (HB 7020, approved 2025-06-10, each section expressly 'Effective October 1, 2025' -- explicit date in act text, no supermajority-contingent immediate-effect clause) repealed the NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalency test in Sec. 20-281n and the statutory definitions of 'NASBA' and 'substantial equivalency', replacing them with an individual-criteria test (out-of-state license in good standing + meets CT education/experience/exam requirements of new Sec. 20-281c(b)-(e)) plus a grandfather clause (exam passed on or before 2025-09-30 and licensed in good standing on 2025-09-30 = privilege without meeting new criteria). Changeover is PAST and operative. Residual flux: (1) the CGA 'current' compiled chapter (cga.ct.gov/current/pub/chap_389.htm) still displays the PRE-act 20-281n text (history ends at P.A. 15-181) with only a header note deferring to a '2026 Supplement, revised to January 1, 2026' that is not posted at any fetchable /current/sup/ URL -- rely on the official act text, not the compiled page; (2) CT Society of CPAs (lead only) reports the Board of Accountancy is still working through implementing regulations and a comprehensive statute/regulation modernization review; the admin regs (Regs. Conn. State Agencies 20-280-1 et seq.) could not be verified as updated post-P.A. 25-36; (3) DCP firm-permit guidance says a permit is triggered by 'any attest or compilation services to Connecticut clients' while statute 20-281e(h) exempts no-office firms' SSARS reviews/compilations if quality-review-qualified and working through a privilege holder -- for compilation-only engagements record the conservative (permit) reading; attest itself is consistent across both. No 2026-session (adjourned 2026-05-06) amendment to ch. 389 mobility sections found; P.A. 25-111 (SB 1357, DCP omnibus) does not touch Secs. 20-279b to 20-281n.
records.data_gap_note: The no-notice/no-fee rule and the new individual-criteria equivalence test rest on the codified act text alone; DCP/board web pages acknowledge the practice privilege and out-of-state firm permit regime but have not been updated to describe the Oct 1, 2025 test (they simply hyperlink to Secs. 20-281n/20-281e, and the linked compiled page still shows pre-act text). Admin regulations (incl. education reg 20-280-23 cross-referenced indirectly by the mobility test via 20-281c 'as determined by the board by regulation') were not independently verified; eregulations.ct.gov document fetch failed (JS portal).
records.notes: Individual privilege (new 20-281n): out-of-state CPA with principal place of business outside CT gets all privileges of CT licensees with NO license, NO notice, NO fee if (A) valid out-of-state CPA license in good standing AND (B) individual meets CT's education/experience/exam requirements under the new three-pathway 20-281c (bachelor's+accounting concentration+2yrs; bachelor's+30hrs+1yr; post-baccalaureate degree+1yr); OR grandfathered (exam passed on or before 9/30/2025 + licensed in good standing on 9/30/2025). Conditions (20-281n(c)): consent to board jurisdiction, comply with CT law, cease practice if home license lapses, home-state board as agent for service. Attest limitation (20-281n(d)): privilege holders performing SAS audits, SSARS reviews, SSAE examinations/reviews/AUP, or PCAOB engagements for an entity with its home office in CT may do so ONLY through a firm holding a 20-281e permit. Firms: 20-281e(g)(3) requires a permit for a no-office out-of-state firm performing attest services of 20-279b(13)(A),(C),(D),(E) (SAS audits, SSAE prospective-financial examinations, PCAOB engagements, other SSAE examination/review/AUP) for a client with home office in CT -- firm_registration_attest=true (DCP publishes a dedicated 'Initial Out-of-State Firm Permit Application'; $150 annual fee, waived for single-licensee firms). 20-281e(h): SSARS financial-statement reviews (13)(B) and compilations (14) for CT-home-office clients are permit-EXEMPT if the firm meets Sec. 20-281 quality-review qualifications and works through a privilege holder. 20-281e(i): all other services (tax, consulting) under the CPA title are permit-exempt through a privilege holder if lawful in the firm's home state -- firm_registration_tax=false. peer_review_required=true in two places: quality review every 3 years as a condition of firm-permit RENEWAL (20-281(b), waivable for firms doing no financial-reporting/attest work), and as a condition of the (h) no-permit review/compilation privilege; board page confirms ('Permit holders, as a condition of renewal, must undergo a peer review'). Board = CT State Board of Accountancy within Dept. of Consumer Protection (portal.ct.gov/dcp). equivalence_test=individual_criteria as of 2025-10-01 (previously nasba_state_level via NASBA NQAS, repealed by P.A. 25-36). UPDATE (verifier): the CT Board February 2026 newsletter (nasba.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/2026_Feb_CT_NL.pdf) is the only found official post-changeover document describing the new individual-criteria test and grandfather clause in prose, and it reinforces the conservative firm reading recorded here: "Connecticut has no firm mobility - every practicing CPA (including solo practitioners) needs a firm permit" (attest or compilation FAQ wording). Add the NASBA CT newsletter series as a DiffLab monitor pattern.

records.citation: 24 Del. C. § 109 (practice privileges); 24 Del. C. § 111(a), (b), (m) (firm permits; peer review); 24 Del. C. § 102(6) (definition of "practice of certified public accountancy"); 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 §§ 8.0, 10.1, 10.3, 10.4, 10.12
records.flux_note: TWO flux drivers. (1) COMPLETED CHANGEOVER: HS 1 for HB 143, 85 Del. Laws c. 112 (approved 2025-07-30), Section 4 rewrote § 109 and Section 5 provides "This Act takes effect on July 1, 2026." No supermajority/immediate-effect option appears in the act, so no vote-count check was needed; the act carries a flat calendar effective date, already operative as of the 2026-07-31 verification date. The act deleted the NASBA-National-Qualification-Appraisal-Service "substantial equivalency" test from § 109(a)(1) (verified against the enrolled PDF with strike/underline conventions expressly stated in the act's amending clause -- the pdftotext extraction shows the NASBA language as STRICKEN old text, not live text, so the apparent statute-vs-act conflict is a formatting artifact only and is NOT a real contradiction). The compiled Delaware Code at delcode.delaware.gov already carries the post-2026-07-01 text with the 85 Del. Laws c. 112 § 4 credit. (2) LIVE SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: the Board's compiled administrative rule, 24 Del. Admin. Code 100 § 8.1.1 (last amended 27 DE Reg. 978, eff. 07/01/2024), STILL conditions the § 109 practice privilege on the individual holding a license from a state that NASBA NQAS "has verified to be in substantial equivalence" with the UAA, or on the individual obtaining an NQAS individual-substantial-equivalency verification. The current statute § 109(a)(1) contains no NASBA/NQAS element at all and instead imposes individual criteria (baccalaureate or higher with accounting concentration + Uniform CPA Exam + 1 year of § 107(f) experience). The rule heading is still "8.0 Substantial Equivalency" while the statutory heading was changed from "Substantial equivalency. Practice privileges." to "Practice privileges." No conforming Board rulemaking has been published (no accountancy item found in the Delaware Register of Regulations for 2025-2026; the compiled rule's latest citation is 27 DE Reg. 978 (06/01/24)). The Board's own web page (dpr.delaware.gov/boards/accountancy/newfirm/) still cross-references "Section 8.0 of the Board's Rules and Regulations" and cites peer-review subsection numbers (10.12.6.3) that were renumbered to 10.12.2.2 in the 2024 amendments -- further evidence of stale board guidance. Practitioners should treat NQAS verification as a possible residual Board expectation until the rule is conformed. UPDATE (verifier - FACTUAL CORRECTION): the record's assertion that "no conforming Board rulemaking has been published" and that no accountancy item appears in the 2025-2026 Delaware Register is FALSE. Two Board of Accountancy entries exist: 29 DE Reg. 757 (PROPOSED, 2026-03-01) and 30 DE Reg. 96 (FINAL, 2026-08-01). The March 2026 Register text reads: "Pursuant to 24 Del.C. 105(a)(1), the Delaware Board of Accountancy has proposed revisions to its regulations... Proposed amendments to section 8.0 clarify and update the requirements for practice privileges for individuals whose principal place of business is [outside Delaware]." SECOND CHANGE DATE: the conformed Rule 8.0 takes effect ~2026-08-11, removing the NQAS substantial-equivalency condition from the administrative rule; rule_changes_on stays 2026-07-01 (the statutory change) and 2026-08-11 is the next changeover. The residual-risk advisory (practitioners treating NQAS verification as a possible Board expectation) is therefore BOUNDED to ~2026-08-11. Third stale board source added: the Board FAQ page (dpr.delaware.gov/boards/accountancy/faqs/) still describes practice privilege as resting on "substantial equivalency" and refers practitioners to NASBA. DiffLab: regulations.delaware.gov exposes real APIs far more monitorable than the SPA shell - GET /api/register/monthlyRegister (issue index with per-issue file ids) and GET /api/CumulativeTable/tabledata.
records.data_gap_note: UPDATE (verifier): peer_review_required=true is SCOPE-QUALIFIED - Delaware peer review (Rule 10.12.2) is a condition of holding a DELAWARE CPA firm permit; no Delaware peer-review obligation attaches to an out-of-state firm relying on the 24 Del. C. 111(b) / 109(c) exemption (which is why firm_registration_attest is false). Rule 10.12.2.1 ("the Board requires all firms offering or rendering such services to be enrolled") is unqualified on its face and is confined to permit holders only by its parent heading 10.12.2 and by 10.12.2.3. Also corrected: the notes' 111(f) reasoning - 102(19) defines "practice of public accountancy" by reference to "a permit holder" and 102(16) makes "permit" cover CPA permits, so the "framed in terms of public accountancy therefore cannot reach CPA firms" step does not hold.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL PRIVILEGE: 24 Del. C. § 109(a)(1) (as amended eff. 2026-07-01) grants an out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is not in Delaware, holding a valid license in good standing from any state, "all the privileges of permit holders of this State without the need to obtain a permit under § 108" -- PROVIDED the individual has (i) a baccalaureate or higher degree with an accounting concentration, (ii) passed the Uniform CPA Examination or successor, and (iii) 1 year of § 107(f) experience. This is an INDIVIDUAL-CRITERIA test, not NASBA state-level substantial equivalency (the NASBA/NQAS language was struck by 85 Del. Laws c. 112 § 4). GRANDFATHER: § 109(a)(2) preserves privileges for an individual who held a valid CPA license from any state as of 2024-12-31 AND had Delaware practice privileges under § 109 as of 2024-12-31 -- those individuals continue without meeting the new (a)(1) criteria. NO NOTICE / NO FEE: § 109(a)(1) and (a)(2) each state "no notice or other submission shall be provided by any such individual"; the Board page confirms application is not required (optional voluntary application only). CONSENT CONDITIONS: § 109(a)(3) imposes automatic consent by BOTH the individual AND the employing firm to Board jurisdiction/discipline, compliance with ch. 1 and Board rules, cessation of practice if the home license lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process. FIRM REGISTRATION: § 111(a) requires a firm permit only of a firm "with an office in this State"; § 111(b) states a firm without a Delaware office "may engage in the practice of certified public accountancy in this State through an individual practicing pursuant to the practice privilege afforded by § 109 ... without obtaining a permit under this section or otherwise notifying the Board"; § 109(c) independently states such practice "shall not obligate a firm that does not maintain an office in this State to obtain a firm permit under § 111." Rule 10.1 and the Board's CPA Firm Permit page both repeat this. ATTEST IS COVERED by that exemption: § 111(i) expressly contemplates that attest and compilation services rendered in Delaware may be under the charge of a person who "qualifies for the practice privilege under § 109"; nothing in ch. 1 imposes a separate out-of-state-firm attest registration. TAX IS COVERED by the same exemption because § 102(6) defines "the practice of certified public accountancy" to include "the preparation of tax returns or the furnishing of advice on tax matters" -- so both attest and tax fall inside the § 111(b) no-permit-no-notice exemption for firms without a Delaware office. Both firm answers are therefore FALSE ONLY for firms with NO Delaware office; ANY firm that opens an office in Delaware must obtain a CPA firm permit regardless of service type. PEER REVIEW recorded as TRUE because it is a condition of the Delaware FIRM PERMIT, not of the no-registration privilege: § 111(m) directs the Board to require, as a condition of firm-permit renewal, that firms providing attest and/or compilation services enroll in a Board-approved peer review program; Rule 10.4 requires enrollment for initial issuance of a CPA firm permit and Rule 10.12.2.1 requires "all firms offering or rendering such services" (attest and compilation) to be enrolled. An out-of-state firm that relies on the § 111(b) exemption and does not hold a Delaware permit is not subject to a Delaware peer-review condition (its home-state obligations still apply). Rule 10.12.2.2 exempts firms whose only service level is SSARS preparation engagements. CAVEAT / UNRESOLVED TENSION: § 111(f) contains an unrepealed sentence -- "any firm which is engaged to practice public accountancy in this State, for even 1 hour, is required to obtain a permit" -- plus an 80-hour/Delaware-client individual-permit trigger for employees of firms headquartered outside Delaware. On its face this could be read to reach out-of-state firms, but it is framed in terms of "public accountancy" and § 110 PA permits (the legacy Public Accountant track, closed to new permits after 2016-12-31 per § 110(e)), and Board Rule 10.5.2 confines the parallel 80-hour rule to "24 Del.C. §110 and this Section" within the PA-firm requirements block (Rule 10.5.1 is expressly about the "firm permit to practice public accountancy"). The CPA-specific provisions (§ 109(c), § 111(b), Rule 10.1, Rule 10.3) and the Board's own published guidance all point the other way, so FALSE is recorded for the CPA firm fields, but a CPA firm sending staff to work >80 hours in Delaware or for Delaware clients should confirm with the Board. Also note Rule 10.5.1.2/10.5.2 would require individual Delaware permits for employees of a PERMIT-HOLDING firm in those circumstances.

records.flux_note:
TWO independent flux drivers, both live as of 2026-07-31.

(1) PENDING LEGISLATION. B26-494, the "Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2025" (Mayor-introduced), passed First Reading 2026-06-30 and Final Reading 2026-07-14 by 12-0 with 1 abstention (13-member Council). It adds a baccalaureate+2-years pathway AND rewrites mobility. The DC Board of Accountancy chairman's own written testimony (dlcp.dc.gov, hearing of 2026-03-26) states the UAA amendment it adopts "replaces the 'substantial equivalent' standard that states had applied with the 'individual-based standard'" -- i.e. DC's equivalence_test is set to move from nasba_state_level to individual_criteria / CPA=CPA. As of 2026-07-31 the bill had NOT yet been transmitted to the Mayor; after signature it must still complete the 30-legislative-day congressional review under D.C. Code § 1-206.02(c)(1) before becoming law. No operative date exists yet, so rule_changes_on is null rather than guessed.

EFFECTIVE-DATE PRECISION NOTE: DC permanent acts have no supermajority immediate-effect option; the operative date is set by congressional review, not by the vote count. DC EMERGENCY acts, by contrast, require a two-thirds vote and take effect IMMEDIATELY on mayoral signature for 90 days with no congressional review.

(2) EMERGENCY ACT ALREADY AT THE MAYOR'S DESK. B26-730, the "Business Licensing Reform and Accountancy Practice Emergency Amendment Act of 2026", passed Final Reading 2026-07-14 by 13-0 (unanimous; 13 of 13 members elected, comfortably above the two-thirds emergency threshold of 9) and was transmitted to the Mayor on 2026-07-29 with a response due 2026-08-12. Its companion Emergency Declaration Resolution was adopted 2026-07-14 as R26-0487. If signed, this emergency act takes effect immediately and could change the mobility rule within days of this verified_date, ahead of the permanent act. I could NOT read B26-730's text (see data_gap_note), so I cannot confirm which accountancy sections it amends. THIS RECORD SHOULD BE RE-VERIFIED AFTER 2026-08-12.

(3) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (statute vs. still-compiled rule) on firm registration for non-attest/tax services -- see notes. Statute § 47-2853.44(a)(4) exempts; unrepealed 2004 rules 17 DCMR 2542.1/2546.1/2546.3 require a permit of every nonresident firm. Conservative value recorded. UPDATE (verifier): add D.C. Law L26-0078, the Revised Business Licensing Reform Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (effective 2025-12-31, EXPIRES 2026-08-13) as the driver explaining B26-730's timing and the 2026-08-12 mayoral deadline; if B26-730 is signed by 2026-08-12, schedule a SECOND re-check ~mid-November 2026 for reversion and search for a companion temporary act then. Effective-date reasoning CONFIRMED as correct and retained verbatim: both the congressional-review analysis for permanent acts and the two-thirds-of-13-elected (=9) emergency threshold analysis check out, and rule_changes_on=null (refusing to guess) was the right call. HIGHEST-RISK MISREADING, preserved: the Board's 2025-12-12 / 2026-01-15 substantial-equivalency advisory does NOT rewrite the 47-2853.49 practice-privilege test (it cites only 47-2853.08 and 17 DCMR 2508). Minor: the Board page links to nasba.org/licensure/mobility2/, not cpamobility.org. DiffLab: drop/de-weight the two lims.dccouncil.gov URLs (JS-only SPA behind a token-gated API - will silently never diff); add the Committee on Public Works and Operations page for B26-494 (heard 2026-03-26).

records.notes:
CURRENT LAW (what an out-of-state CPA may do in DC today, 2026-07-31):

INDIVIDUAL PRACTICE PRIVILEGE -- YES. D.C. Official Code § 47-2853.49(b) presumes an individual whose principal place of business is NOT in DC to be substantially equivalent and gives them "all the privileges of licensees of the District without the need to obtain a license under § 47-2853.42".

EQUIVALENCE TEST -- nasba_state_level. § 47-2853.49(b)(1) is the primary route: a valid unrestricted CPA license from a state the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service (NQAS) "has verified to be in substantial equivalence" with the UAA. § 47-2853.49(b)(2) is a fallback for individuals from non-verified states who obtain INDIVIDUAL NQAS verification, plus a pre-2012 grandfather from the UAA § 5(c)(2) education requirement. Both routes run through NASBA NQAS, so this is not an individual_criteria / CPA=CPA state today. NOTE a separate board policy: on 2025-12-12 the Board voted (announced in a DLCP/Board advisory dated 2026-01-15) to deem RECIPROCITY LICENSURE applicants holding a BA+accounting concentration, 2 years' experience, and a license from an alternative-pathway jurisdiction to have met "substantial equivalency". That vote cites D.C. Official Code § 47-2853.08 and 17 DCMR § 2508 -- the RECIPROCITY LICENSURE authorities -- not § 47-2853.49, so it does NOT by its own terms rewrite the practice-privilege test. Do not conflate the two.

NOTICE -- NOT required. § 47-2853.49(c): the privileged individual "need not provide notice or other submission to any individual." (The DC codification reads "to any individual" where the UAA model reads "to the Board or any other person"; either way it is a no-notice provision.) FEE -- none: the privilege is expressly "without the need to obtain a license," and no fee attaches. Conditions instead attach automatically by consent under § 47-2853.49(d): DC Board jurisdiction, compliance with the Act and Board rules, cessation if the home-state license lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process.

FIRM REGISTRATION -- ATTEST: YES. § 47-2853.44(a)(2)(C) requires registration by "Any firm that does not have an office in the District but performs attest services defined in § 47-2853.41(1) for a client having its home office in the District." "Attest services" under § 47-2853.41(1) covers SAS audits, SSARS reviews, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, PCAOB engagements, and other SSAE examinations/reviews/agreed-upon-procedures. § 47-2853.49(e) reinforces this: a privileged individual performing § 47-2853.41(1) services for a DC-home-office entity "may only perform the services through a firm that has obtained a registration under § 47-2853.44." § 47-2853.49(f) confirms that individual does NOT additionally need a DC license. § 47-2853.44(b)(1) and (b)(5)(A) accommodate out-of-state registrants by letting an individual WITH PRACTICE PRIVILEGES (rather than a DC licensee) satisfy the member/responsible-person requirements for an (a)(2)(C) firm. Note COMPILATIONS are in "practice of certified public accounting" (§ 47-2853.41(7)) but NOT in the § 47-2853.41(1) attest definition, so a compilation-only out-of-state firm is arguably outside (a)(2)(C) -- an unresolved edge (see open_questions).

FIRM REGISTRATION -- TAX / NON-ATTEST: RECORDED AS TRUE UNDER THE CONSERVATIVE RULE, BUT THE STATUTE SAYS OTHERWISE. This is a genuine statute-vs-compiled-rule conflict, not a judgment call:
  * PERMISSIVE (statute): § 47-2853.44(a)(4) says a firm not caught by (a)(2) "may perform other professional services in the practice of certified public accounting in the District and may use the title 'CPA' or 'CPA firm' without registering under this section" provided it works through an individual with § 47-2853.49 practice privileges and is lawfully able to perform the services in that individual's principal-place-of-business state. § 47-2853.44(d) likewise blesses CPA-title use by a firm "exempt from holding a registration under subsection (a)(4)". Read alone, firm_registration_tax would be FALSE.
  * RESTRICTIVE (compiled rule, never conformed): 17 DCMR 2542.1 (adopted 2004, 51 DCR 4401) bars any partnership/corporation from rendering "any professional services requiring licensure under this chapter and the Act, unless it is registered and holds a permit"; 17 DCMR 2546.1 subjects "every nonresident partnership or corporation that engages in the practice of public accountancy in the District of Columbia" to the chapter; and 17 DCMR 2546.3 flatly requires that "A nonresident partnership or corporation seeking to engage in any activity licensed by this chapter and the Act on an incidental or temporary basis shall apply for and obtain a permit from the Board before engaging in the activity," with 2546.4 letting the Board DENY it. 17 DCMR 2541.5 bars holding out or rendering services "unless and until a permit has been issued."
  * The rules are demonstrably stale: 17 DCMR 2546.2's only escape hatch cross-references "D.C. Official Code § 47-2853.03(f)(2) (2001)" for a "temporary or periodic accounting work incidental to a regular practice in another jurisdiction" exemption -- but the live text of § 47-2853.03(f)(2) contains no such exemption (it covers consultation, demonstration, and teaching). The whole 2540-2547 "Partnership and Corporate Practice" series predates DC's 2011 mobility act (D.C. Law 19-43) and the 2017 amendments (D.C. Law 21-276) and was never conformed to them. A court would very likely hold the statute controls, and DLCP in practice administers § 47-2853.44. But per the conflict rule the CONSERVATIVE value is recorded: an out-of-state firm doing tax/non-attest work for DC clients should assume a DC firm permit may be demanded until DLCP repeals or conforms 17 DCMR 2540-2547. Advise clients accordingly; do not present FALSE here.

PEER REVIEW -- YES, and it is a condition of the FIRM REGISTRATION/LICENSE, not of the individual privilege and not of a no-registration attest privilege (DC has no no-registration attest privilege -- attest for DC-home-office clients always requires registration). 17 DCMR 2548.1 requires ALL CPA firms performing audits, reviews, compilations, or SSAE/SAS/SSARS engagements to enroll in and complete an approved peer review program. 17 DCMR 2550.1 makes proof of enrollment, the next report due date, and the most recent peer review report + acceptance letter part of the INITIAL FIRM LICENSE APPLICATION; 2550.2 makes an applicant firm that fails to supply them "ineligible to perform audits, reviews, or compilations." 2550.3/.4 let the Board condition or restrict the license on an adverse/fail/second-successive-modified report. Because an out-of-state firm registering under § 47-2853.44(a)(2)(C) is an "applicant for initial firm licensure," 2550 applies to it. Peer review is rule-based only -- § 47-2853.44 itself never uses the words "peer review" or "quality review." Sole exemption: 17 DCMR 2555/2556 (compiled as "EXEMPTION FROM PEER REVIEW") for a firm whose sole practice is compiled financial statements for management use only under SSARS No. 8.

FEES (board's own page): DLCP lists Company/Firm $175.00 and Permit to Practice $175.00. These are firm/licensee fees, not practice-privilege fees.

MINOR CODIFICATION ODDITY (not material to any field): the May 2012 final rulemaking (59 DCR 5186) as published numbered its sections 2554 EXTENSION, 2555 EXEMPTION FROM PEER REVIEW, 2556 ETHICAL DUTIES OF PEER REVIEWERS, but the DCMR as compiled lists 2555 TYPE OF REVIEW REQUIRED and 2556 EXEMPTION FROM PEER REVIEW, and shows no "ethical duties" section. Cite 2548 and 2550 (which match exactly) rather than 2555/2556.

records.flux_note: HB 148 (Act 87, signed 2025-05-09) rewrote Georgia mobility effective 2026-01-01: term 'substantial equivalency' replaced with 'mobility practice privileges' and the old NASBA-style state-level test (license from a state requiring 150 hrs + exam + 1 yr experience, with individual-equivalence fallback) was replaced by individual criteria (current license in good standing + education/experience 'as the board by rule or regulation may establish' + passed Uniform CPA Exam). SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (stale board materials): the board's compiled rules -- 20-3-.09 (last amended eff. 2015-02-24), 20-8-.01 (2016), 20-8-.02 (2015), all 'current through Rules and Regulations filed through July 20, 2026' on rules.sos.ga.gov -- and the board's Statement of Policy No. 11 (adopted 2015-11-18, still posted on gsba.georgia.gov) still state the superseded regime, including the old condition that the individual hold a license 'in a state which grants similar practice privileges to license holders in this state.' The board published proposed conforming amendments (August 2025 rule synopses: 20-3-.02, 20-3-.05, 20-3-.08, 20-3-.09, 20-7-.01, 20-8-.01, 20-8-.02, each 'to go into effect January 1, 2026'), but the amended texts do NOT yet appear in the compiled GAC as of 2026-07-31 -- final adoption status unresolved. Until the board adopts education/experience criteria under new 43-3-18(b)(1)(A), the operative individual criteria are effectively good-standing license + passed exam. New 43-3-16(b)(1)(C) also added an 'unless such firm meets the requirements of paragraph (2)' escape and added compilations (43-3-2 para. (4)) to the licensure trigger; (b)(2) by its terms only authorizes review/other-examination-AUP/compilation services without a license, so the conservative reading (audit/SSAE-examination/PCAOB work still requires a firm license) is used here. UPDATE (verifier, markup-verified enrolled act): HB 148 ALSO enacted conditional FIRM mobility effective 2026-01-01 - in 43-3-16(b)(1)(C) the phrase 'subparagraph (A), (C), or (D) of' is STRICKEN and in (b)(2) 'subparagraphs (B) and (E) of' is stricken, so a no-office firm meeting 43-3-16(b)(2)(A)-(C) (majority-CPA ownership, peer-review compliance, performance through a Georgia-licensed or mobility-privileged individual) may perform ALL 43-3-2(2) attest services (audit, prospective-financial examination, PCAOB engagements) plus (4) compilations WITHOUT a Georgia firm license; old 43-3-16(b)(3) (no-office firms/other services under CPA title) is stricken in its entirety. HOWEVER the compiled board rules as served by rules.sos.ga.gov (current through rules filed 2026-07-20) DIRECTLY CONFLICT: Rule 20-8-.01(1) still flatly mandates biennial licensure for any no-office firm performing audit/SSAE-examination/PCAOB work directed into Georgia, with no (b)(2) exemption, and Rule 20-3-.09/20-8-.02 plus the GSBA 2015 Statement of Policy and FAQ pages still describe the superseded substantial-equivalency regime. Statute and still-compiled rule state OPPOSITE answers for the same firm - a live primary-source conflict, NOT resolved here per the contradiction rule: firm_registration_attest is kept at the CONSERVATIVE true (register) and rule_in_flux stays true until the board's conforming amendments land.

records.notes: INDIVIDUAL (43-3-18(b), eff. 2026-01-01): An out-of-state CPA whose office-location designation is in another state is presumed substantially equivalent, has all privileges of Georgia license holders, and may practice in Georgia with NO license, NO notice, and NO fee, if the individual holds a current license in good standing from any other state (and remains licensed while practicing), has attained education/experience the board establishes by rule for mobility privileges, and has passed the Uniform CPA Examination. Conditions (43-3-18(b)(3)): automatic consent to board jurisdiction, compliance, cease-practice-if-home-license-lapses, and service-of-process agency. Retained limiter (43-3-18(c)): privilege applies only if the home state grants similar reciprocity to Georgia license holders. Individuals performing audit/SSAE-examination/PCAOB services for Georgia-directed clients may only do so through a firm meeting 43-3-16 requirements (43-3-18(b)(4)). FIRM-ATTEST: A firm with no physical Georgia office performing any audit (43-3-2(2)(A)), examination of prospective financial information (2)(C), or PCAOB engagement (2)(D) directed to a Georgia client must obtain a biennial Georgia firm license (43-3-16(b)(1)(C); Rule 20-8-.01(1); $150 fee; NASBA processes initial firm applications). Reviews, other SSAE examination/review/AUP engagements, and compilations ((2)(B), (2)(E), para. (4)) may be performed WITHOUT a firm license if the firm meets majority-CPA ownership, complies with peer review rules, and performs through an individual licensed in Georgia or holding mobility privileges (43-3-16(b)(2); Rule 20-8-.02(1)). FIRM-TAX/NON-ATTEST: no firm registration required -- a no-office firm may perform other professional services and use the title 'CPA'/'CPA firm' without a Georgia license if it performs them through an individual with practice privileges and can lawfully perform them in its home state (43-3-16(b)(3); Rule 20-8-.02(2)). PEER REVIEW: required as a condition of firm-license RENEWAL for licensed firms that issued an attest or compilation report in the prior 24 months (43-3-17(a); Rule 20-8-.01(5),(9) -- AICPA-standard peer review within 36 months), AND separately required as a condition of the no-registration review/compilation privilege for unlicensed out-of-state firms (43-3-16(b)(2)(B); Rule 20-8-.02(1)(b)). Legislative history: HB 148 passed House 172-0 (2025-02-19), Senate 52-0 (2025-04-02), signed 2025-05-09 (Act 87), effective 2026-01-01 per Section 3-1 of the act and the legislature's published bill-history 'Effective Date' line. UPDATE (verifier): the FIRM-ATTEST sentence (biennial Georgia firm license, $150 fee) carries the enacted qualifier 'unless such firm meets the requirements of paragraph (2) of this subsection' - i.e. qualifying no-office firms are statutorily exempt from 2026-01-01, though the compiled board rule still demands licensure (see flux_note conflict).

records.citation: 22 GCA § 35122 (Substantial Equivalency), Guam Accountancy Act of 2003; firm permits at 22 GCA § 35107; implementing rules at 25 GAR §§ 2103(d), 2106, 2112
records.flux_note: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on notice_required and fee_required (no pending legislation). (1) The codified statute, 22 GCA § 35122(a)(1) and (a)(2), states the privilege is automatic and that 'no notice or other submission shall be provided by any such individual.' (2) The Board's own official form, 'Notice of Intent to Practice Public Accountancy in Guam under Substantial Equivalency Provisions of 22 GCA §35122 and 25 GAR §2112' (https://www.guamboa.org/pdf/GU_SE.pdf, HTTP Last-Modified 2019-12-07, i.e. republished THREE YEARS AFTER the no-notice language was enacted), is a notarized filing requiring submission 'within 30 days after accepting an engagement.' (3) The compiled administrative rule 25 GAR § 2103(d)(2) prescribes fees expressly keyed to '22 GCA, § 35122': Initial $225.00, Renewal (annually) $175.00, Reactivation/Reinstatement $275.00, Provisional $175.00. A per-registrant annual renewal fee is only coherent if a registration/notice exists. Both the no-notice statutory language AND the substantial-equivalency fee schedule were enacted by the SAME act, P.L. 33-193 (Dec. 15, 2016), which repealed and reenacted both 22 GCA ch. 35 and 25 GAR ch. 2 — so this is an unresolved internal conflict within enacted Guam law, not a stale rule lagging a new statute. Per the conservative-value rule, notice_required and fee_required are recorded TRUE (the reading requiring more of the practitioner). A secondary, lesser divergence: the Board FAQ Q7 describes an open 'Individual Mobility' privilege for a CPA licensed 'in any other of the 54 U.S. jurisdictions,' which is broader than the statute's NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalence test; currently harmless because all jurisdictions are NQAS substantially equivalent, but it would diverge if any jurisdiction lost that status. No changeover date applies: Guam has enacted no accountancy amendment since 2016.
records.flux_summary: Guam's statute says practice privilege is automatic, with no notice required. But the Board's own official form demands a notarized filing within 30 days, and a separate rule sets real registration fees -- both enacted by the same 2016 law, so this is an unresolved conflict within Guam's own law, not an outdated rule catching up to a new one. We recorded the stricter reading (notice and fee required). Confirm directly with the Guam Board before relying on this.

records.notes:
STATUTORY BASIS. 22 GCA ch. 35 (Guam Accountancy Act of 2003), § 35122 'Substantial Equivalency'. Current text is as amended by P.L. 33-193 (Dec. 15, 2016). VERIFIED CURRENT: the Guam Compiler of Laws' official Tables of Code Sections Affected for the 34th, 35th, 36th, 37th and 38th Guam Legislatures (the 38th table running through P.L. 38-133, June 4, 2026) contain NO entry for any section 35101-35125 of Title 22 — no amendment since 2016. Independently, a full scan of all 354 bills of the 38th Guam Legislature (bills pages 1-4 plus special) and the 38th public-laws list found zero bills mentioning accountancy, CPAs, or Title 22 ch. 35. Guam has therefore NOT joined the 2025-26 national pathways/mobility wave, by statute or by board rulemaking (notices.guam.gov shows only board-meeting notices for the GBA, no rulemaking notices). The Board is active — meeting agendas are posted through July 16, 2026 — and its 2025-26 agenda packets discuss the mobility wave only in NASBA national-report attachments about OTHER jurisdictions.

EQUIVALENCE TEST. nasba_state_level: § 35122(a)(1) grants the privilege to a CPA whose principal place of business is not in Guam and who holds a valid license from any State 'which the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service has verified to be in substantial equivalence' with the UAA. § 35122(a)(2) adds an INDIVIDUAL-level fallback for CPAs from non-verified states, who must obtain individual NQAS verification (with a pre-2012 licensure exemption from the § 35105(c)(2) education requirement). The Board's SE form mirrors both routes with two checkboxes. The primary/default test is state-level, hence nasba_state_level rather than individual_criteria.

FIRM — ATTEST (true). 22 GCA § 35107(a)(1)(C): a firm with NO office in Guam MUST hold a Guam firm permit to perform attest services described in § 35103(b)(1), (3), (4) or (5) — i.e. SAS audits, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, PCAOB engagements, and other SSAE examination/review/AUP engagements — for a client having its home office in Guam. § 35107(a)(1)(A)-(B) additionally require a permit of any firm WITH an office in Guam that performs attest services or uses the 'CPA'/'CPA firm' title. § 35122(a)(4) reinforces this at the individual level: a practice-privilege holder may perform attest only through a firm meeting § 35107(a)(1)(C) or holding a § 35107 permit. Board FAQ Q7 states the same. Firm permit fee is $275 initial / $225 annual renewal (25 GAR § 2103(d)(3)).

IMPORTANT CARVE-OUT (do not read as blanket attest exemption). § 35107(a)(2) lets a firm with no Guam office perform SSARS REVIEWS (§ 35103(b)(2) — which Guam's definition classes as ATTEST) and COMPILATIONS (§ 35103(f)) for a Guam-home-office client, and use the CPA title, WITHOUT a permit, but ONLY if (A) it has the qualifications described in § 35107(d) AND § 35107(i), and (B) it performs the services through an individual with § 35122 practice privileges. Subsection (i) is the PEER REVIEW subsection — so Guam conditions this no-registration attest privilege on peer review, in addition to conditioning firm-permit renewal on it.

FIRM — TAX / NON-ATTEST (false). § 35107(a)(3): a firm not subject to (a)(1)(C) or (a)(2) may perform other professional services in Guam while using the 'CPA'/'CPA firm' title WITHOUT a Guam permit, but only if (A) it performs them through an individual holding § 35122 practice privileges and (B) it may lawfully do so in that individual's principal-place-of-business State. This is a conditional exemption, not an unconditional one. Note the boundary: this applies to firms with NO office in Guam; § 35107(a)(1)(B) requires a permit of ANY firm with an office in Guam that uses the CPA or CPA firm title, regardless of service type. Board FAQ Q7 agrees that an out-of-jurisdiction CPA 'may practice public accountancy in Guam, other than performing any type of Attest service.'

PEER REVIEW (true) — TWO DISTINCT HOOKS. (1) Condition of FIRM PERMIT RENEWAL: 22 GCA § 35107(i) directs the Board to require by rule that applicants undergo peer review no more frequently than once every three years; implemented at 25 GAR § 2106(c) ('Successful Completion of an Approved Compliance Assurance Program (Peer Review) as a Condition for Renewal of Permit'), which requires all CPA firms offering or rendering attest services to be enrolled in a Board-approved compliance assurance program (AICPA peer review accepted as substantially equivalent). The Board's firm application asks 'Has this CPA firm had a Peer Review in the last three (3) years?' (2) Condition of the NO-REGISTRATION review/compilation privilege under § 35107(a)(2)(A), via its cross-reference to § 35107(i).

INDIVIDUAL CONDITIONS (regardless of the notice/fee conflict). § 35122(a)(3): exercising the privilege is deemed simultaneous consent by the individual AND the employing firm to (A) the Board's personal and subject-matter jurisdiction and disciplinary authority, (B) compliance with ch. 35 and Board rules, (C) ceasing practice if the home-state license lapses, and (D) appointment of the issuing State Board as agent for service of process. 25 GAR § 2112(a) additionally requires a privilege holder engaging clients via a website to disclose on that website the State of principal place of business, license number, and a contact address. 25 GAR § 2112(c)(1) requires notice to the Board within 30 days of moral-character events under 25 GAR § 2107(a)(1)-(2). 25 GAR § 2112(d) deems home-state CPE compliance to satisfy Guam CPE.
