records.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. ch. 466, esp. §§ 466-3 (definitions), 466-5(a), 466-7(a), (c), (d), 466-34; Haw. Admin. R. §§ 16-71-8, 16-71-24, 16-71-27. Former Haw. Rev. Stat. § 466-5.5 repealed by 2025 Haw. Sess. Laws Act 14, § 3 (education section, not mobility).
records.flux_note: Hawaii's 2025-wave act (SB1291 SD1 = Act 14, SLH 2025, approved and effective 2025-04-10) changed ONLY the licensure pathway (bachelor's + 30 hours OR bachelor's + 12 extra months of public-accounting experience; two years of experience) and repealed HRS 466-5.5. Verified from the act's own text that 466-5.5 was 'Educational requirements for licensure effective December 31, 2000' -- an EDUCATION section, NOT a practice-privilege section. Act 14 did NOT touch mobility, temporary permits, or firm permits. Independently verified NO 2026 accountancy legislation: the legislature's complete 2026 Acts report (266 records, Acts 1-307) contains zero occurrences of 'accountan'; the only accountancy measure in the entire 2025-2026 biennium bill lists besides SB1291 is HB983 HD1 (the SB1291 companion, dead since 3/6/2025, also pathway-only). Method validated by confirming the same reports surface SB1291/Act 14 in the 2025 Acts report. No accountancy item appears on DCCA's proposed-rulemaking page and no rulemaking item appears on the Board's March 13, 2026 agenda/minutes (the Board's only 2026 policy item is 'NASBA Tracking of Applicants Using the Alternative Pathway'). Statute, compiled rules, and board forms/announcements all agree on every field recorded here, so no source disagreement. Recorded as NOT in flux.
records.data_gap_note: Two interpretive gaps, both resolved conservatively rather than guessed. (1) TAX-ONLY OUT-OF-STATE FIRMS: HRS 466-7(d) says 'All firms shall obtain a permit to practice' with no attest/non-attest split, and HRS 466-3 defines 'practice of public accountancy' to include 'the preparation of tax returns or the furnishing of advice on tax matters' -- but that definition is qualified by 'by a person or firm holding itself out to the public as a licensee.' Neither HAR 16-71 nor any board publication interprets the 'holding out' qualifier, so it is not documented whether an out-of-state firm doing purely tax work for a Hawaii client while not holding out as a CPA firm in Hawaii falls outside the permit requirement. firm_registration_tax is recorded TRUE (conservative; the rule requiring more of the practitioner). (2) TEMPORARY PERMITS FOR NON-ATTEST WORK: HAR 16-71-8 defines the statutory 'incidental' test only by audit examples; board practice on granting temporary permits for tax-only engagements is undocumented. Also: the Board's May 29, 2026 meeting minutes were not yet posted as of 2026-07-31 (most recent posted minutes are 3.13.26), so that meeting was not reviewable.
records.notes:
HAWAII GRANTS NO PRACTICE PRIVILEGE / NO SUBSTANTIAL EQUIVALENCY -- it remains a hard non-mobility jurisdiction, and the starting hint that HRS 466-5.5 was a practice-privilege section is WRONG (it was an education section, now repealed). There is no practice-privilege provision anywhere in HRS ch. 466 or HAR 16-71; the words 'privilege', 'substantial equivalency' and 'mobility' do not appear in the compiled rules at all. HRS 466-5(a) and 466-7(a) both require a Hawaii license AND permit to practice public accountancy.

INDIVIDUAL ROUTE: the ONLY route short of full Hawaii licensure is a discretionary TEMPORARY PERMIT under HRS 466-7(c) -- board-granted, effective 'for a period not exceeding three months', and available only where the work is 'Incidental to the person's practice in such other state or country.' HAR 16-71-8 defines 'incidental' as 'services rendered in this State by a non-licensee for work performed for a client outside the State' (e.g., auditing a Hawaii subsidiary of an out-of-state parent). Board form CPA-13 makes the consequence explicit: 'Is the work that you will be temporarily doing in Hawaii for a client that is located outside the State of Hawaii? ... (If "NO", you do not qualify for a temporary permit to practice).' PRACTICAL UPSHOT: an out-of-state CPA generally CANNOT serve a Hawaii-domiciled client at all without full Hawaii licensure plus a Hawaii firm permit.

notice_required / fee_required = TRUE describe this permit requirement, NOT a privilege notification (no privilege exists). HAR 16-71-27 and form CPA-13 require the application to be filed 'not later than sixty days prior to the commencement of the period covered by the application', and CPA-13 charges a total fee of $269 ($25 application + $194 permit + $50 Compliance Resolution Fund). Each 90-day period needs a new application. CPE rules do not apply to temporary permits (HAR 16-71-48).

FIRM REGISTRATION (attest AND tax both TRUE): HRS 466-7(d) 'All firms shall obtain a permit to practice.' HAR 16-71-24(b)(1)(C) provides 'The Hawaii business operations of a foreign or multi-state firm shall constitute a "firm" for purposes of the firm permit to practice under section 466-7, HRS,' and (b)(4) requires every foreign/multi-state firm engaged in public accounting practice in Hawaii to have at least one Hawaii-licensed CPA/PA principal holding a current individual permit. There is NO attest/non-attest exemption anywhere in the statute, the rules, or the board's forms. The firm must also supply a Hawaii general excise tax license number or attest it will have no Hawaii gross income (HAR 16-71-24(b)(2)). Firm permit fees: $89-$121 sole proprietorship, $230-$345 partnership/LLP/corporation/LLC. Notably, a firm permit is a PRECONDITION to an individual temporary permit -- CPA-13 instruction 3: 'Pursuant to Hawaii Revised Statutes section 466-7, your CPA firm must hold a current Hawaii firm permit to practice.'

PEER REVIEW = a condition of the FIRM PERMIT (not of any no-registration privilege, since none exists). HRS 466-34(a) requires every firm required to obtain a firm permit -- 'including the Hawaii offices and Hawaii engagements of foreign or multistate firms' -- to undergo peer review every three years, and (i) states 'An out-of-state firm performing Hawaii attest work shall comply with this part.' IMPORTANT CARVE-OUT: HRS 466-34(d) -- 'A firm that does not perform Hawaii attest work shall be exempt from the peer review process.' So a tax-only out-of-state firm still needs the FIRM PERMIT but is exempt from PEER REVIEW. Separately, HRS 466-7(b)(5) conditions renewal of an INDIVIDUAL permit on proof of having undergone the peer review process. 'Hawaii attest work' is itself a defined term in HRS 466-3 keyed to Hawaii-resident/Hawaii-domiciled clients and Hawaii subsidiaries with stand-alone financial statements.

equivalence_test = 'other': Hawaii applies NO substantial-equivalency test (neither NASBA state-level nor an individual-criteria privilege test) because it grants no privilege. Its scheme is a discretionary board-approved temporary permit conditioned on (i) a valid CPA/PA license from another state or a recognized foreign qualification, (ii) age 18+ and a history of competence/trustworthiness/fair dealing, (iii) the engagement being incidental to out-of-state practice, and (iv) the firm holding a Hawaii firm permit. A separate ten-year/five-year experience waiver of the education requirement for full licensure exists at HRS 466-5(c)(2) -- that is a reciprocity-style licensure path, not mobility.

STALE SECONDARY GOVERNMENT ARTIFACTS (disclosed, but they do NOT contradict any recorded field): (a) the DCCA-hosted HRS 466 PDF at files.hawaii.gov/dcca/pvl/pvl/hrs/hrs_pvl_466.pdf still prints the pre-Act-14 text of 466-5 and the full repealed § 466-5.5 -- do not cite it; (b) HAR 16-71 (compiled 11/27/2021, and the board labels its posted copy 'Unofficial Version') still cross-references repealed § 466-5.5 in three places. Both defects concern EDUCATION requirements only; neither touches mobility, temporary permits, firm permits, or peer review, so this is not a mobility-field source disagreement. The board's own statute/rules page correctly links to the live capitol.hawaii.gov HRS ch. 466.

records.citation: Idaho Code sec. 54-227 (Practice Privileges), repealed and re-enacted by 2026 Idaho Sess. Laws ch. 48, secs. 5-6 (H0563), eff. July 1, 2026; firm side: Idaho Code secs. 54-214 (Firm Registration -- Peer Review), 54-220(4) (Use of Title), 54-212 (General Fees); board rules: IDAPA 24.30.01 (Idaho Accountancy Rules), esp. Rules 109, 110, 207, 208, 211, 400
records.flux_note: Idaho IS part of the 2025-26 wave and changed on 2026-07-01 -- 30 days before the verification date. H0563 (2026 Sess. Laws ch. 48, signed by Gov. 2026-03-18) REPEALED the old Idaho Code 54-227 (titled by the bill's relating clause as 'RELATING TO SUBSTANTIAL EQUIVALENCY REQUIREMENTS', bill SECTION 5) and ADDED an entirely new 54-227 (bill SECTION 6). Idaho therefore MOVED OFF a substantial-equivalency test and ONTO an individual-criteria test: the out-of-state CPA must personally meet the minimum education (54-207) and experience (54-209) requirements. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED: bill SECTION 7 is a fixed-date emergency clause -- 'An emergency existing therefor, which emergency is hereby declared to exist, this act shall be in full force and effect on and after July 1, 2026.' Idaho Const. art. III sec. 22 requires only a simple-majority emergency declaration (no supermajority threshold), and the clause names an explicit date rather than immediate effect, so no vote-count arithmetic can change the answer; final passage was nevertheless overwhelming (House 67-0-3 on 02/24; Senate 35-0-0 on 03/12) and the legislature's own bill page publishes 'Effective Date: July 1, 2026'. SECOND FLUX VECTOR (board rulemaking): IDAPA 24.30.01 has an OPEN negotiated rulemaking, Docket No. 24-3001-2601, Notice of Intent to Promulgate Rules published in the Idaho Administrative Bulletin Vol. 26-5 (May 6, 2026), first public meeting June 1, 2026, whose stated purpose is to '(1) facilitate[] a new pathway to licensure for candidates and make[] minor adjustments to accommodate for statutory changes in line with HB 563 from 2026; (2) remove[] outdated language'. DOPL's rulemaking page lists Accountancy as 'In Progress, 2026-2027', i.e. targeted at the 2027 Legislative Session, and the currently compiled 24.30.01 (PDF regenerated 2026-06-12) still carries pre-H0563 section dates (mostly 3-28-23) and still describes the old 150-semester-hour framework. No SOURCE DISAGREEMENT was found on the mobility fields themselves: the compiled rule's NASBA/NQAS substantial-equivalence language survives only in Rule 110.01 'Interstate Reciprocity', which is the RECIPROCAL LICENSURE fallback that applies expressly 'If the practice privilege standard set out in Section 54-227, Idaho Code, is not applicable' -- it is not the practice-privilege test, so no conservative-value override was triggered.
records.data_gap_note: The Idaho board publishes NO dedicated mobility/practice-privilege guidance page. Its 'Statutes, Rules and Guidance' page carries only statute/rule links and its Guidance section reads 'To be updated.' The board leg of the dual-source test is therefore the board's OWN PROMULGATED RULES (IDAPA 24.30.01, a copy of which is hosted on the board's site at dopl.idaho.gov), the board's Firm Registration & Peer Review Program page, and the board's published fee schedule -- not narrative board guidance. Consequence: equivalence_test = 'individual_criteria' rests primarily on the statute; the compiled board rules predate H0563 and have not yet been conformed, so no board text independently restates the new individual-criteria test. fee_required = false is proved by ABSENCE (no practice-privilege fee anywhere in the exhaustive 54-212 fee cap list or in Rule 400's fee schedule) plus 54-227(2)'s 'no notice or other submission' language; note that Idaho's clause omits the word 'fee' that the UAA model clause contains. firm_registration_tax = false is a textual reading of an enumerated trigger list and is materially qualified by the TITLE trigger -- see notes.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL SIDE. Idaho grants practice privilege by statute with NO notice, NO registration and NO fee, but it is NOT open CPA=CPA: 54-227(1) conditions the privilege on the individual personally meeting Idaho's minimum education and experience requirements in 54-207 and 54-209. Post-H0563 those are three educational pathways -- (a) postbaccalaureate degree with accounting concentration, (b) baccalaureate plus 30 additional semester credit hours, or (c) baccalaureate alone -- paired with 1 year of verified experience for pathways (a)/(b) and 2 years for pathway (c) (54-209(1)(a)-(b)). Hence equivalence_test = 'individual_criteria', NOT 'nasba_state_level'. GRANDFATHER: 54-227(4) preserves privileges for any out-of-state CPA who, as of December 31, 2024, held and continues to hold a valid active license and had Idaho practice privileges under the prior version of 54-227 -- those CPAs keep the privilege without meeting 54-207/54-209. CONSENT CONDITIONS: 54-227(3) makes both the individual AND the firm employing that licensee deemed to consent to board jurisdiction and discipline, to compliance with the chapter and board rules, to ceasing practice if the home-state license lapses, and to service of process on the home-state board. ONE NON-BOARD DISCLOSURE OBLIGATION: IDAPA 24.30.01.109 requires a non-Idaho licensee who enters an engagement to provide professional services via a website under Idaho practice privileges to disclose principal state of licensure, license number, address, and a regulator/public contact route ON THEIR WEBSITE. This is a website-disclosure duty, not a filing with the board, so it does not make notice_required true -- but a compliance product must surface it. FIRM SIDE -- THE IMPORTANT ONE. Idaho has NO firm-mobility provision. Title 54 ch. 2 contains no UAA sec. 7(a)(1)-style exemption letting an out-of-state firm perform attest for Idaho clients without registering, and H0563 did not touch 54-214 (last amended 2008). 54-214(1) states flatly that 'A firm must be registered with the board in order to provide attest services or compilation reports' with no geographic qualifier, and 54-220(4) independently bars ANY business entity from providing attest services or compilation reports unless it is a firm registered under the chapter with conforming ownership. Registration is annual (rule 211.01, due September 30; note the board began transitioning to BIENNIAL licensure on 2026-05-01, and Rule 400 already prints biennial firm-registration amounts of $40 firm plus $10 per licensee up to $400). Fee is $20 firm plus $5 per licensee up to $200 (annual). TAX / NON-ATTEST -- READ THIS CAREFULLY. The registration triggers in 54-214(1) and 54-220(4) are (i) providing attest services or compilation reports, OR (ii) assuming or using the titles 'CPAs', 'CPA firm', 'LPAs', 'LPA firm' or 'certified public accountants'. Rendering TAX services is not itself a trigger, and Rule 211.01 requires a firm registration form only from 'All firms performing any of the peer reviewable services in Rule 207.' That is why firm_registration_tax is recorded false. BUT the title prong is a real trap: an out-of-state firm that holds itself out in Idaho as a CPA firm must register EVEN IF IT DOES ONLY TAX WORK. Since most out-of-state CPA firms carry 'CPA'/'CPAs' in their name or branding, the practical answer for a large share of tax-only engagements is that registration IS required. Note also that Idaho's exemption clause 54-226(1) ('shall not be construed to prevent any person from rendering tax services...') does NOT help firms: 54-206(19) defines 'person' as 'any natural living person', so 54-226(1) shelters individuals, not entities. PEER REVIEW. Peer review is a condition of FIRM REGISTRATION RENEWAL, not of an attest privilege -- 54-214(6) directs the board by rule to require firms to comply with peer review as a condition of registration renewal; Rules 207-215 implement it (AICPA standards, once every three years, administered by a board-approved administering organization, reports filed within 30 days). Rule 208.01 exempts a registered firm that performs none of the Rule 207 services. For INDIVIDUALS practicing under Idaho practice privileges, Rule 207.02 defers entirely to the home state: they 'are to comply with the peer review requirements in the state of their principal place of business.' Rule 209.07 allows the Peer Review Oversight Committee to accept a multi-state firm's review based solely on work performed outside Idaho if done to equivalent standards. ADMIN-CODE HISTORY (relevant to stale links): the board's rules were redesignated from IDAPA 01.01.01 to IDAPA 24.30.01 effective July 1, 2020 when the board was folded under the Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses; the hint's 'IDAPA 01' is the dead numbering and old IDAPA 01 URLs/mirrors (e.g. Cornell LII's 'IDAPA 01 - Accountancy, Board of') are stale.

records.flux_note: P.A. 104-0228 (HB2459, signed 2025-08-15, eff. 2026-01-01) retitled 225 ILCS 450/5.2 from 'Substantial equivalency' to 'Enhanced mobility' and REPLACED the NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test with: (1) issuing state's licensure requirements equivalent to the criteria in Section 14, or (2) individual petition to the Public Accountant Registration and Licensure Committee for an equivalency determination of education, exam, and experience. NOTE: the prior-research claim that IL 'adopted NASBA NQAS state-level equivalency' is BACKWARDS - the enrolled act DELETES the NQAS language (shown stricken in the act). The prior-research claim that the enrolled act and compiled ILCS state DIFFERENT tests could not be reproduced: researcher AND independent adversarial verifier each fetched the enrolled act's raw HTML with strike/underline markup preserved and the compiled ILCS text; both state the SAME new Section-14-equivalence/petition test (compiled source line: 'P.A. 103-309, eff. 1-1-24; 104-228, eff. 1-1-26'). The apparent contradiction arises when the act's STRICKEN NQAS text loses strikethrough formatting during text extraction and reads as live text - both versions are reproduced verbatim in the evidence quotes; human review of the enrolled act PDF should confirm. Still genuinely in flux: (a) Section 14 licensure criteria - the referent of the 5.2(a)(1) equivalence test - gain two new pathways on 2027-01-01 (bachelor's in accounting + 2 yrs experience; master's or bachelor's + 30 accounting hrs + 1 yr), which will shift which states are 'equivalent'; (b) IDFPR's administrative rules (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1420) contain no mobility/practice-privilege section and have not been updated for P.A. 104-0228 (1420.35 Temporary Practice is repealed) - rulemaking is likely; (c) the entire Public Accounting Act is scheduled to be repealed 2029-01-01 (sunset).
records.data_gap_note: notice_required=false and fee_required=false reflect the automatic privilege path (5.2(a)(1) plus 5.2(b): 'no notice or other submission'). For CPAs from states NOT equivalent to Section 14, the 5.2(a)(2) petition to the Committee is itself a pre-condition submission, and whether a fee attaches to that petition is not resolved (statute silent; 68 IAC 1420.40 fee schedule not yet updated for the new petition). No published list of 'equivalent' states exists yet - out-of-state CPAs cannot currently self-verify path (1) eligibility from official sources. firm_registration_attest=false is CONDITIONAL: an out-of-state firm avoids licensure only if it complies with Sections 14.4 (ownership) and 16 (peer review) through its home state; a firm with an Illinois office, or one without an Illinois office that fails 5.2 privilege requirements and performs 5.2(e) audit/attest engagements for an Illinois-headquartered client, MUST hold an Illinois CPA firm license (Section 13). Record-level confidence set to single_source (minimum across answered fields): individual_practice_privilege and equivalence_test are effectively dual-sourced (IDFPR OLA page + compiled ILCS + enrolled act), but notice/fee, firm registration, and peer review fields rest on statute and administrative rule only - no IDFPR page states their substance.
records.notes: Scheme as of 2026-07-31: Illinois grants automatic practice privilege - no license, notice, or fee - to an individual CPA whose principal place of business is out of state if the issuing state's requirements are equivalent to 225 ILCS 450/14; otherwise the individual must first obtain a Committee equivalency determination. Firm mobility: an out-of-state CPA firm has full privileges without license or notice if it complies with Sections 14.4 and 16 (including peer review) through enhanced mobility of its licensed state (5.2(a-5)); this covers attest and non-attest alike, but audits/attestation engagements for Illinois-headquartered entities may only be performed through a licensed or privileged CPA firm (5.2(d)-(e)). Tax/non-attest by an out-of-state firm with no Illinois office triggers none of the Section 13 licensure prongs. Peer review (3-year cycle, Section 16; 68 IAC 1420.75) is a condition of firm license renewal for firms performing 8.05(a)(1) attest activities and is incorporated into firm mobility via the Section 16 compliance condition. Caution: an IDFPR reinstatement form states 'The firm cannot advertise or offer any professional services in Illinois without a valid CPA Firm license' - in context it addresses lapsed Illinois firm licenses, not privileged out-of-state firms, but the tension is logged in the evidence open_questions.

records.citation: Ind. Code § 25-2.1-4-10 (individual practice privilege, no notice); Ind. Code §§ 25-2.1-12-5 and 25-2.1-12-2 (firm permit required for attest services/CPA title use); Ind. Code § 25-2.1-5-8 and 872 IAC 1-6-9 (peer review as condition of firm permit renewal)
records.flux_note: HEA 1143 (P.L. 85-2025, signed 2025-04-16) amends IC 25-2.1-3-2 to add a bachelor's-degree + 2-years-experience licensure pathway, effective 2027-01-01 (the board's own Nonrule Policy Document 25-467 states 'this language will not take effect until January 1, 2027'). The mobility statute IC 25-2.1-4-10 itself was NOT amended (last amended P.L.190-2007). To bridge the gap, the Board adopted Nonrule Policy Document 25-467 'Substantial Equivalency Clarification' (adopted 2025-09-12 by 3-2-0 vote, effective on Indiana Register publication 2025-10-01): out-of-state CPAs serving Indiana-based clients and reciprocal applicants are deemed substantially equivalent if they passed the Uniform CPA Exam and licensed via any of three pathways (post-bacc + 1 yr; 150-hr bacc + 1 yr; bacc <150 hrs + 2 yrs). The policy is expressly non-binding guidance ('if it conflicts with these rules or laws, the rules or laws shall control'). Implementing rulemaking LSA #26-18 (amends/repeals portions of 872 IAC 1-1, 'Pathways to certified public accountant licensure') is mid-flight: authorized 2026-01-12, comment period closed 2026-02-27, public hearing 2026-03-13; final adoption not confirmed as of 2026-07-31. records.notes: Indiana is a UAA-pattern no-notice mobility state, unchanged in statute since 2007: IC 25-2.1-4-10 gives an individual whose principal place of business is outside Indiana all privileges of an Indiana CPA certificate holder, with substantial equivalency determined at the STATE level by 'the board or its designee' (NASBA/NQAS pattern) or, as fallback, via the individual's own qualifications — hence equivalence_test=nasba_state_level with an individual-criteria fallback; the 2025 non-rule policy overlays pathway-based individual criteria (exam + one of three education/experience pathways) for both mobility and reciprocity. Privilege conditions (IC 25-2.1-4-10(c)): consent to board jurisdiction, compliance with IC 25-2.1 and 872 IAC, cease practice if home license lapses, home-state board as agent for service of process. Firms: no firm mobility; firm permit (IC 25-2.1-5, $30 fee per board packet, 3-year cycle expiring June 30, 2027 this cycle) required for any firm providing attest services or using the CPA title (IC 25-2.1-12-5); peer review not more than once every 3 years is a statutory condition of permit renewal (IC 25-2.1-5-8) implemented by 872 IAC 1-6-9 (renewal certification; amended version filed 2025-03-21); board: all firms performing ANY attest functions (audits, reviews, compilations, AUPs) must have peer review every 3 years — peer review attaches to the firm permit, not to any no-registration privilege. Board = Indiana Board of Accountancy (Indiana Professional Licensing Agency, PLA).

records.flux_note: H.F. 778 (2025 Iowa Acts ch. 40, approved 2025-05-01) took effect 2026-07-01 by its own explicit effective-date section (Sec. 9) — no immediate-effect/supermajority clause, so no vote-count issue. It struck the substantial-equivalency test from 542.20: subsection (1) now reads 'without licensure under this chapter, paying a fee, or providing notice to the board' and drops 'substantially equivalent to a comparable license issued in Iowa'; subsection (6)(a) now requires only that the individual 'meet the criteria set forth in subsections 7 and 8' (license in good standing in principal place of business + consent-to-jurisdiction conditions). Strike/underline markup verified by rendering the official Acts PDF to images. CONFLICT: the board's compiled rule IAC 193A—20.2(2) (ARC 7695C, eff. 4/10/24; agency compilation through 5/13/2026 unchanged) still conditions the individual privilege on 'substantial equivalency reciprocity, as provided in Iowa Code section 542.19(1)(a),(b), or (c) and rule 193A—9.5'; the compiled Iowa Code 2026 likewise still prints pre-amendment text with editor notes pointing to 2025 Acts ch. 40 (editorial lag, not a conflict). No board rulemaking implementing H.F. 778 found as of 2026-07-31. CONSERVATIVE READING: until 193A ch. 20 is amended, an out-of-state CPA who does not meet former 542.19(1)(a)-(c) substantial-equivalency criteria faces residual exposure under the stale rule even though the amended statute controls; firm rule 193A—21.2(2) similarly retains a 'substantially equivalent to a permit' condition the amended statute no longer states. No 2026-session ch. 542 legislation found. UPDATE (verifier - citation corrected): all Iowa Admin. Code 193A accountancy rules were editorially TRANSFERRED to Inspections and Appeals [481] chapters 1021-1040 by IAC Supplement 2026-06-10 pursuant to 2023 Iowa Acts SF 514 - the old 193A chapter PDFs are now transfer-notice stubs. records.notes: equivalence_test='other': as of 2026-07-01 Iowa is effectively CPA=CPA — the only individual test is a valid, unexpired license in good standing in the state of principal place of business, licensed there for all services rendered in Iowa (542.20(1)), plus the 542.20(7)-(8) conduct/consent conditions (new (7)(e): comply with chapter and board rules); no NASBA state-level or individual equivalency determination remains in the statute. (The pre-2026-07-01 scheme, still echoed in stale rule 193A—20.2(2), was a disjunctive 542.19(1)(a) state-standards / (b) individual-qualifications / (c) 4-of-10-years test — also not cleanly 'nasba_state_level'.) FIRMS: a permit under 542.7 is required ONLY if the firm has an office in Iowa using the CPA title (542.7(1)(a)); a no-Iowa-office firm practices attest AND tax/non-attest under 542.20(5) with no firm license, no notice, no fee (rule 193A—21.6(1) same), so firm_registration_attest and firm_registration_tax are both false. peer_review_required=true attaches to the NO-REGISTRATION PRIVILEGE, not to a registration: 542.20(5)(e) requires privilege firms to 'comply with the ownership and peer review requirements of section 542.7', and rule 193A—21.5 repeats it for attest/compilation; for Iowa-licensed firms peer review is a permit-renewal condition (542.7(8)). Individuals performing attest in Iowa or for a client with an Iowa home office must practice through a 542.7-licensed firm or an out-of-state firm meeting 542.7 ownership/peer-review (542.20(6)(c), unchanged by H.F. 778); compilations per 542.20(6)(d). CPA-title use: privilege individual may not have an Iowa office using the title except through a permitted/exempt firm office (542.20(6)(b)). State agencies/clients may still demand Iowa licensure for certain engagements (542.20(2), e.g. Iowa Code ch. 11 audits). Accounting Today's 'House Bill 177' bill number is wrong — the act is H.F. 778.

records.flux_note: Kansas joined the 2025-26 wave: HB 2573 (signed 2026-04-09, published and EFFECTIVE 2026-04-23 via Kansas Register Vol. 45 No. 17; passed unanimously; effective-date clause is unconditional Register publication, no supermajority check needed) rewrote K.S.A. 1-322 from a substantial-equivalency test (NASBA/designee-verified state OR individual 150hr+exam+1yr criteria, permissive 'may be granted') to a mandatory grant ('shall be granted') for any out-of-state CPA with an active license in good standing whose initial licensure required passing the uniform CPA exam plus one of three degree/experience pathways (bachelor's+2yrs; bachelor's+30hrs+1yr; post-baccalaureate+1yr), expressly with no permit, registration, or fee; prior privilege holders as of 2025-12-31 are grandfathered. RESIDUAL LAG, not a substantive conflict: as of 2026-07-31 the compiled statutes at ksrevisor.gov still display the pre-amendment 2016 text (history ends 'L. 2016, ch. 19' -- annual compilation lag; the board site and the Kansas Register carry the current text), and K.A.R. Article 74 (eff. 2024-04-26) still frames mobility in 'substantial equivalency' terms pending conforming rulemaking. Old and new texts agree on all recorded booleans (privilege yes; no notice; no fee; attest firm registration; nonattest exemption; peer review), so no conservative/permissive divergence -- only the equivalence test changed, recorded per the enacted current law. Firm statutes 1-308/1-501 were NOT amended by HB 2573.

records.notes: Kansas is historically two-tier (certificate under 1-302 + permit to practice under 1-310) but this does NOT burden inbound mobility: new 1-322(a) grants out-of-state CPAs 'all the privileges of permit holders' with no permit/registration/fee, and 1-308(d) confirms a practice-privilege individual performing services requiring firm registration still needs no Kansas certificate or permit. Two-tier machinery matters only for relocation: an individual moving their principal place of business to Kansas must request both certificate and permit BEFORE relocating (1-302b(d)). ATTEST: an out-of-state firm with no Kansas office must register (1-308(b)(2)) before performing SAS audits, Kansas municipal audit guide audits, SSARS reviews, SSAE engagements (except compilations), or PCAOB engagements for a Kansas client, and the privileged individual may perform those only through a registered firm (1-322(c)); registration renews annually by December 31, and a (b)(2) firm may designate an out-of-state licensee meeting 1-322(a) as its responsible party (1-308(g)). TAX/NONATTEST (incl. compilations, which are outside the 1-321(d) attest definition): no firm registration needed under 1-308(c) IF the performing individuals meet 1-302b(b)-(c) competency qualifications, services flow through a practice-privilege individual, and the services are lawful in the home state. PEER REVIEW: condition of firm-registration RENEWAL for firms providing attest services (1-501 'may require' implemented mandatorily by K.A.R. 74-11-7: every renewal application shall include a peer-review completion/in-process letter or board waiver form; review at least every 3 years, firm bears cost; 1-501 waivers available). Fee note: HB 2573 also struck the old 1-301(b)(7) $150 practice-privilege 'notification' fee item, confirming the no-fee reading; the notification requirement itself had already been removed from 1-322 by L. 2016 ch. 19. Consent-to-jurisdiction conditions (1-322(b)) attach automatically -- no filing.

records.citation: KRS 325.282 (practice privilege) and KRS 325.301 (firm licensure/exemption), Ky. Rev. Stat. ch. 325; KRS 325.282 as amended by 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 21, sec. 2 (HB 45), effective July 15, 2026
records.flux_note: THREE distinct flux/conflict elements. (1) RECENT CHANGEOVER, ALREADY OPERATIVE: 2026 HB 45 (2026 Ky. Acts ch. 21, signed by Gov. Beshear 2026-04-03) rewrote the mobility test in KRS 325.282(1) and took effect 2026-07-15 -- only 16 days before this verification. HB 45 struck the old requirement that the CPA hold a license 'from any state that the board has determined to have licensure requirements substantially equivalent to those found in this chapter' (STATE-level substantial equivalency) and replaced it with a test on the INDIVIDUAL: at initial licensure the person must have been required to show evidence of (a) passing a board-approved exam and (b) attaining the education and experience requirements of KRS 325.261(3) and (5). HB 45 also added a new grandfather subsection KRS 325.282(2) preserving privileges for anyone who, as of June 30, 2025, held a CPA license from any state and had KY practice privileges. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED: HB 45 contains NO emergency clause and no effective-date section (full GA text is Sections 1-4 only); Kentucky requires an express emergency declaration under Ky. Const. sec. 55 for immediate effect -- there is no supermajority-triggered immediate-effect mechanism, so the vote margins (House 93-0 with 7 not voting of 100 members; Senate 38-0 with 0 not voting of 38 members) do NOT accelerate the date. Default 90-days-after-sine-die (session adjourned 2026-04-15) applies. Confirmed on BOTH legs: LRC compiled statute prints 'Effective: July 15, 2026' and the Board homepage says 'Beginning July 15, 2026'. (Secondary press reporting of 'July 16, 2026' is wrong; do not use.) (2) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT -- STALE BOARD PAGE on equivalence_test: the Board's Reciprocal License page still describes the pre-HB-45 test, requiring that the CPA's home state 'is considered to have licensing requirements substantially equivalent to those of Kentucky' (state-level). That directly contradicts the now-operative individual-criteria test in KRS 325.282(1). The statute controls; equivalence_test is recorded as individual_criteria (which is also the more demanding value for the practitioner, since it requires the individual to have personally met KY's education/experience/exam criteria rather than merely holding a license from an SE state). (3) INTERNAL STATUTORY TENSION on firm_registration_attest: KRS 325.282(6) (renumbered from (5) by HB 45, text carried forward unamended from 2008) says a privileged individual performing an SAS audit, an SSAE examination of prospective financial statements, or a PCAOB engagement for a KY-home-office client 'shall perform the service or services through a firm which has obtained a license issued under KRS 325.301' -- while KRS 325.301(2) (added by 2018 Ky. Acts ch. 24) expressly says an out-of-state firm with no KY office 'shall not be required to obtain a license.' The Board's own published guidance resolves this in favor of firm mobility (no license required), and the chapter's own definition of 'Firm' in KRS 325.220(3) includes an entity that 'is exempt from having to obtain a license pursuant to KRS 325.301.' Recorded as false accordingly, but the 282(6) cross-reference was never conformed and is an unresolved drafting artifact. Separately, compiled 201 KAR 1:050 Sec. 1(2)(d) still requires a transcript verifying 'the 150-hour requirement of KRS 325.261' -- a stale rule now that HB 45 repealed the 150-hour subsection; that stale rule affects LICENSURE, not the mobility test, but signals the Board has not yet run conforming rulemaking. No pending 201 KAR ch. 1 amendment on mobility or firm registration was found in the Administrative Register as of 2026-07-31. UPDATE (verifier): HB 45 sec. 3 ALSO amended KRS 325.280 (reciprocity) effective the same 2026-07-15 date, so the reciprocal-license path this record routes office-opening CPAs into changed simultaneously with the mobility test. The 2025-2026 KRS ch. 325 enactment scan is documented COMPLETE: 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 5 (2025 HB 262) amended KRS 325.380 effective 2025-06-27 (firm-name and deceased/retired-partner rules only, no mobility impact). CONTRADICTION-OF-FORM, not of law: the official catchline of KRS 325.282 still reads "...meeting substantially equivalent licensure requirements" and was not conformed by HB 45 - catchlines are not law under KRS 446.140, so equivalence_test=individual_criteria stands. Correction to the researcher's claim that the Board "has not yet run conforming rulemaking": more precisely, no SUBSTANTIVE conforming amendment is on file, though 201 KAR 1:160 carries a certification effective 2026-03-30.
records.data_gap_note: No field left null. Caveat on firm_registration_attest: the 'no firm registration' answer is CONDITIONAL, not unconditional -- KRS 325.301(2) exempts an out-of-state firm only if (a) CPAs hold 51%+ of ownership/voting rights (KRS 325.301(3)(a)) AND the firm complies with the peer review requirement of KRS 325.301(10); (b) ALL services provided by the firm are performed by individuals holding a KRS 325.282 practice privilege; and (c) the firm can legally provide the services in the state where the privileged individual has his or her principal place of business. A firm that fails any of these conditions is not covered by the exemption, and the statute does not spell out what it must then do (KRS 325.301(1) on its face only mandates a license for firms WITH a Kentucky office). Also unresolved: the KRS 325.282(6) / KRS 325.301(2) tension described in flux_note. UPDATE (verifier - CONDITIONALITY THAT MUST REACH THE PRODUCT SURFACE): firm_registration_attest=false is the GENERAL-CASE answer only. KRS 325.282(6) commands the opposite for SAS audits, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and PCAOB engagements performed for a client whose home office is in Kentucky - those require a firm holding a Kentucky firm license under KRS 325.301. Do not render this field as an unqualified "no registration needed". Authority correction: the lead citation for the general-case exemption should be KRS 325.380(4) (which expressly permits attest work through the exempt route), NOT KRS 325.220(3), which merely defines "Firm" to include an exempt entity and does not answer 325.282(6)'s demand for a firm that "has obtained" a license. AFFIRMATIVE NEGATIVE PROOF now available for notice_required=false and fee_required=false: 201 KAR 1:170 was REPEALED (by repealer 201 KAR 1:171), so those two fields no longer rest on absence-of-provision reasoning alone. RESIDUAL EDGE: KRS 325.282(3)(a)'s no-notice provision is written to cover only persons satisfying subsection (1), leaving the new subsection (2) grandfather cohort textually uncovered - notice_required=false is airtight for the (1) cohort and inferential for the (2) cohort. peer_review_required=true binds only firms performing attest or compilation services; an out-of-state firm doing tax-only work in Kentucky has no Kentucky peer-review duty.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: KRS 325.282(1) grants an out-of-state CPA with no KY office and a valid license in good standing from any state 'all the practice privileges granted to the holder of a license issued under this chapter without having to obtain a license from the board,' conditioned on the individual having met, at initial licensure, (a) a board-approved exam and (b) the education and experience requirements of KRS 325.261(3) and (5). KRS 325.282(3)(a) makes no-notice explicit. No fee provision attaches (no license = no application/renewal fee under KRS 325.301(4)-(5) or 201 KAR 1:050). The privilege carries automatic consent to KY board jurisdiction, appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process, a duty to notify the board BEFORE opening any KY office (and then apply for a reciprocal license under KRS 325.280), and a duty to notify the board immediately if the home-state license goes inactive/lapses/is disciplined (KRS 325.282(4)(a)-(f)) -- these are ongoing conditions, not a pre-practice notice. KRS 325.282(7) lets the board REVOKE practice privileges for CPAs of an entire state whose licensing standards the board finds unacceptable; individuals from a revoked state can still qualify individually. TRIGGER FOR KY LICENSURE: the board's line is the OFFICE / employment. If the CPA is employed by or owns a business with a Kentucky office and uses the CPA title there, a KY reciprocal license ($100 under 201 KAR 1:050 Sec. 1(2)(a)) is required. FIRM: KRS 325.301(1) mandates a firm license only for a firm WITH an office in this state that performs attest services or uses the 'CPA' title. KRS 325.301(2) is the firm-mobility exemption for out-of-state firms (added 2018) and covers ALL services described in KRS 325.220 -- which includes both 'Attest service' (325.220(1)) and 'Regulated activities' (325.220(9), expressly including 'the preparation of tax returns or the furnishing of advice on tax matters'). So both attest and tax answer FALSE, and the tax answer is NOT inferred from the attest answer: it rests on the same subsection's own 'services described in KRS 325.220' scope plus KRS 325.301(1) limiting the licensing mandate to firms with a KY office. PEER REVIEW: this is a condition of the NO-REGISTRATION attest privilege, not a condition of a permit the firm must hold -- KRS 325.301(2)(a) requires the exempt out-of-state firm to comply with KRS 325.301(10), which requires all firms performing attest OR COMPILATION services to enroll in and complete peer review in an AICPA-equivalent-or-better program and to allow the sponsoring organization to give the board access via FSBA or similar. The board page states this the same way ('if applicable complies with the peer review requirements [KRS 325.301(10)] of this state'). SEPARATE NARROW EXEMPTION: KRS 325.301(11) additionally lets any out-of-state CPA or firm enter Kentucky without a license solely to (a) conduct a peer review of a firm, or (b) perform attestation work incidental to an engagement initiated with an out-of-state client that extended into Kentucky via common ownership/subsidiary/assets/operations. The board cites 325.301(11) (rather than the broader 325.301(2)) on its CPA Firms overview page as the authority for out-of-state firms not needing a license -- an imprecision in board drafting; the conclusion is the same. EQUIVALENCE TEST: 'individual_criteria.' Note that 'Substantial equivalency' remains DEFINED in KRS 325.220(13) (in both its state-level and individual-level forms), but after HB 45 that definition is no longer the operative test in KRS 325.282; the operative test is the individual showing under 325.282(1)(a)-(b).

records.flux_note: Act 653 of 2026 (HB 548, Rep. Beaullieu), signed 2026-06-02, took effect 2026-08-01: R.S. 37:94 retitled from 'Substantial equivalency' to 'Mobility practice privileges'; the board/designee state-level substantial-equivalence test (NASBA-style) is STRICKEN and replaced with individual criteria -- a valid active CPA license in good standing from any state qualifies, with no license, notice, registration, or fee, if at initial licensure the individual passed the Uniform CPA Exam and met one of three pathways: (a) baccalaureate + 30 additional semester hours + 1 year experience, (b) post-baccalaureate degree + 1 year experience, or (c) baccalaureate + 2 years experience. New 37:94(A)(2) grandfathers any individual licensed as of 2024-12-31 who had Louisiana practice privileges on that date. The no-notice/no-fee outcome is now statutory (previously rested on board rule LAC 46:XIX.1105.E.2). Firm statute R.S. 37:77 is NOT amended by Act 653. Board rules LAC 46:XIX.1105(E) and the board's substantially-equivalent-states framework have not yet been conformed to the Act -- watch the Louisiana Register. rule_in_flux stays true solely on that conforming-rulemaking gap, not on any remaining statutory ambiguity. Re-verified 2026-08-01 (day of effect): equivalence_test confirmed flipped to individual_criteria; zero other coded values refuted.
records.flux_summary: A new law (Act 653) took effect August 1, 2026, replacing Louisiana's old state-level mobility test with one based on the individual CPA's own credentials -- a license from any state now qualifies with no notice or fee if the person met certain education/exam/experience pathways at initial licensure, or is grandfathered under a 2024-12-31 cutoff. The statute itself is clear; we're holding this as unverified only because the Board's own rules haven't been updated to match the new law yet. Confirm directly with the Louisiana Board before relying on this.
records.data_gap_note: firm_registration_tax=false rests on (a) R.S. 37:77(A)'s permit trigger reaching only firms with a Louisiana office and no-office firms providing ATTEST services (no statutory permit trigger for no-office firms performing only non-attest/tax work), plus (b) board rule LAC 46:XIX.1501(B) and the board's Firm Mobility page, which extend the no-permit privilege to 'professional services' generally and CPA-title use ONLY IF the firm meets ownership, peer/quality-review-within-3-years, and licensed/privileged-individual conditions — a no-office firm failing those conditions 'must apply for a permit' under the rule. There is no unconditional statutory sentence exempting non-attest firms, so treat the false as conditional. Also note R.S. 37:83 (unlawful acts) title-use restrictions were not fully analyzed. UPDATE (verifier): LAC 46:XIX.1107(A) imposes a 30-day address/practice-status change-notification duty on substantial-equivalency privilege holders - notice_required=false means no PRE-PRACTICE notice, not zero board-facing obligations.
records.notes: CURRENT LAW (through 2026-07-31): R.S. 37:94(A)(1) grants full practice privileges (no Louisiana license) to individuals whose principal place of business is outside Louisiana holding a valid active license from a state the board or its designee has verified as substantially equivalent (the board publishes an equivalent-states list per LAC 46:XIX.1105.E.4.a; its CPA Reciprocity page states all 54 jurisdictions are substantially equivalent). A(2) provides an individual-verification fallback (per 1105.E.4.b: exam + 150 semester hours + 1 year supervised experience in last 4 years, OR 4 years practice experience in last 10). The statute's default notice+fee sentence is superseded in practice by board rule LAC 46:XIX.1105.E.2 (adopted under the statute's express 'Notwithstanding any other provision of law' authorization), which grants privileges 'without the necessity of giving notice to the board or paying a fee'; the board's site confirms no notice form or fee. Attest under the privilege may be performed 'only through a firm which meets the requirements of this Part' (37:94(A)(4)). FIRMS: a firm with a Louisiana office must hold a permit for attest services or CPA-title use (37:77(A)). A no-office firm providing attest in Louisiana is exempt from the permit only if it meets ALL of: ownership qualifications (37:77(C), simple-majority CPA ownership), peer review compliance (37:77(G)), performs through 37:94-privileged individuals, and can lawfully perform the services in its home state. For non-attest/tax, no statutory permit trigger reaches no-office firms; LAC 46:XIX.1501(B) confirms no-permit practice plus CPA-title use for 'professional services' generally under the same conditions (peer/quality review completed within last 3 years, privileged/licensed individuals, home-state lawful), else the firm must apply for a permit. PEER REVIEW: true = condition of the no-permit firm privilege — statutorily for attest (37:77(A)(2) requires compliance with 37:77(G): board-approved peer review program, PCAOB-only firms exempt) and by rule 1501(B)(1) for the broader professional-services/title privilege; it is also a permit condition for registered firms. Firm permit fees if registration is chosen/required: $150 initial, $50+ annual renewal. Individual privilege: no notice, no fee.
