records.flux_note: FLUX IS A SOURCE DISAGREEMENT, NOT A PENDING LAW CHANGE. (1) Board web guidance vs. statute on FIRM registration: 32 M.R.S. § 12252(1)(A)(3), as amended by PL 2021, c. 68, § 2, requires a firm license for an out-of-state firm performing § 12201(3-A)(A),(C),(D) attest work for a Maine home-office client 'unless: (a) It qualifies for a firm license pursuant to subsections 3 and 8 and it performs such services through an individual with practice privileges under section 12232; or (b) It meets the requirements of section 12253.' The Board's OWN pages (Licensing - Accountancy Firm and Accountancy Branch, and the firm FAQ answering the question 'Substantial Equivalency?') still publish the PRE-2021 unqualified trigger with the 'unless' carve-outs omitted entirely and with no mention of § 12253. That is stale board guidance reading MORE restrictively than current law. The codified BOARD RULE (02-280 ch. 6 § 1(A)) does NOT conflict: it incorporates the statute by reference ('when licensure is required by 32 M.R.S. §12252(1)(A)'), so statute and compiled rule agree; only the informational board webpage is out of date. Recorded firm_registration_attest=false per the statute + compiled rule, but a firm relying on the exemption should confirm with the Board, whose published guidance would tell it to register. (2) rule_changes_on = 2021-10-18 is the operative changeover on which the current firm-mobility scheme took effect: PL 2021, c. 68 ('An Act To Enable Out-of-state Certified Public Accountancy Firms To Provide Services in Maine on the Basis of Substantial Equivalency', H.P. 124 / L.D. 171), approved by the Governor May 25, 2021, contains NO emergency preamble and NO separate effective-date section (confirmed against the enrolled act PDF 130LR0636(03)), so it took effect 90 days after the 130th Legislature's First Special Session adjourned sine die on July 19, 2021, i.e. October 18, 2021 (Me. Const. art. IV, pt. 3, § 16; corroborated by the Revisor's note at 18-B M.R.S. § 1229 that PL 2021, c. 235 'takes effect October 1, 2021' but the actual effective date was October 18, 2021, 90 days after adjournment of the First Special Session of the 130th Legislature). (3) NO 2025-26 mobility change in Maine — Maine is an outlier in the national wave. I scanned all 2,153 LD titles of the 132nd Legislature (2025-2026, LD 1 through LD 2245, adjourned sine die): exactly ONE accountancy bill exists, LD 1789 / H.P. 1200 'An Act to Amend the Education Requirements in the Certified Public Accountant Licensure Laws', enacted and signed June 12, 2025 as PL 2025, c. 297, which amends ONLY 32 M.R.S. § 12228(3) (120-hour exam-sitting eligibility). Its pathways/mobility provisions were stripped by Committee Amendment C-A (H-533) before passage. Sections 12232, 12252 and 12253 were untouched by the 2025 and 2026 sessions. No board rulemaking on mobility either: the 02-280 2025-2026 Regulatory Agenda lists only conformance reviews plus expected rulemaking 'to implement legislation governing licensure by endorsement and provisional licensure' (10 M.R.S. § 8003-H) — that is LICENSURE by endorsement, not practice privilege. A future mobility bill in the 133rd Legislature (convenes Dec 2026) is plausible given the stripped 2025 attempt, but nothing is pending now.
records.data_gap_note: (a) The compiled statute pages and the chapter 113 PDF carry the Revisor stamp 'Data for this page extracted on 10/20/2025' / 'Generated 10.20.2025', i.e. current only through the 2025 First Regular Session; I closed that gap independently by scanning the full 132nd Legislature bill directory (LD 1-2245) and the 02-280 regulatory agenda and found no 2026 accountancy enactment or rulemaking, but a very late 2026 enactment not yet in the bill directory cannot be excluded from these sources alone. (b) 32 M.R.S. § 12253(1)(A) conditions firm mobility on the firm holding a license 'from a state that the board has verified to be in substantial equivalence' with NASBA/AICPA CPA-FIRM licensure requirements; unlike the individual side (where the Board's page points to the NASBA NQAS substantially-equivalent-states list and CredentialNet), the Board publishes NO list of firm-level substantially-equivalent states and no firm verification procedure, so the practical scope of the firm privilege is not determinable from published sources. (c) Whether peer review is a condition of the § 12253 firm privilege is not stated in § 12253 (see notes). (d) I could not retrieve the official Laws of Maine 2021 front-matter effective-date page (legislature.maine.gov/doc/2368 downloaded truncated/corrupt), so the 2021-10-18 date rests on the act's lack of an emergency clause plus the Revisor's corroborating note at 18-B § 1229.
records.notes:
INDIVIDUALS (32 M.R.S. § 12232): Maine grants a full no-notice, no-registration, no-fee practice privilege to an out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is outside Maine. § 12232(2) is emphatic: 'no notice or other submission may be required of any such individual.' Conditions are consent-based only, not filing-based: § 12232(3) requires the individual AND the employing firm to consent to the Board's personal and subject-matter jurisdiction and disciplinary authority, to comply with ch. 113 and board rules, and to cease practice if the home-state license lapses. Note the interlock at § 12232(4): an individual with the privilege may perform § 12201(3-A) ATTEST services for a Maine home-office entity only THROUGH a firm that either holds a § 12252 license or is exempt under § 12252(1)(A)(3) or (1)(B) — i.e. the individual privilege alone does not authorize attest work; the firm-side gate must also be cleared.

EQUIVALENCE TEST: recorded 'nasba_state_level' because the primary test in § 12232(1)(A) is whether the CPA's licensing STATE has been verified by the Board to be in substantial equivalence with NASBA/AICPA (UAA) requirements, and the Board's own page operationalizes this by pointing to the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service list of substantially equivalent states. There is a genuine INDIVIDUAL-criteria fallback in § 12232(1)(B) for CPAs licensed in a non-SE state, which the Board routes through NASBA CredentialNet; § 12232(1)(B) also lets the Board exempt a CPA who passed the Uniform CPA Exam and held a valid license from any other state before January 1, 2012 from the § 12228(3)(B) education requirement. Maine has NOT moved to CPA=CPA / individual-criteria mobility — it kept the classic state-level SE model, which is now a minority position after the 2025-26 wave.

FIRMS - ATTEST: recorded false (no registration/permit required) on the statute + compiled rule, but READ THE CONDITIONS. An out-of-state firm with NO Maine office performing § 12201(3-A) paragraph A (SAS audits), C (SSAE prospective financial information) or D (PCAOB engagements) for a client with its home office in Maine escapes the § 12252 license ONLY via one of two routes: (a) § 12252(1)(A)(3)(a) — the firm must itself qualify for a Maine firm license under § 12252(3) (simple-majority CPA ownership) AND § 12252(8) (peer review) and must perform through an individual holding § 12232 practice privileges; or (b) § 12252(1)(A)(3)(b) / § 12253 — the firm holds a valid CPA-firm license from a state the Board has verified to be in substantial equivalence (or the Board individually determines the firm's qualifications are substantially equivalent). Route (b) is expressly no-notice, no-submission, no-fee (§ 12253(2)) and carries the same consent conditions as individuals (§ 12253(3)). Paragraph B (SSARS reviews and COMPILATIONS) and paragraph F (other SSAE examination/review/AUP) are handled separately by § 12252(1)(B), which permits the work plus use of the 'CPA'/'CPA firm' title without a license on the same two routes. A firm that opens an OFFICE in Maine, or that uses 'CPA'/'CPA firm' at a Maine office, must be licensed outright — § 12252(1)(A)(1)-(2), no exceptions. § 12275(14)(C) separately protects title use by an unlicensed, no-office firm that complies with § 12252(1)(A)(3), (1)(B) or (1)(C).

FIRMS - TAX / NON-ATTEST: recorded false and verified INDEPENDENTLY of the attest analysis. Tax return preparation and tax advice are NOT within the § 12201(3-A) 'attest service' definition (which is limited to SAS, SSARS, SSAE and PCAOB engagements). § 12202 expressly provides that 'Anyone may practice accounting and engage in services which involve accounting or auditing skills, including management advisory or consulting services, the preparation of tax returns and the furnishing of advice on tax matters,' subject only to not holding out as a licensee and not issuing a § 12201(10-A) report. The residual firm provision § 12252(1)(C) confirms no license is needed for non-attest services; it imposes conditions only on USE OF THE 'CPA'/'CPA firm' TITLE while doing them (meet § 12253, or perform through an individual with § 12232 privileges AND have legal authority to perform the services in that individual's principal-place-of-business state). No registration, notice or fee in either case. The Board's own CPA FAQ confirms: 'You do not need to be licensed to prepare tax returns.'

PEER REVIEW: recorded true. It is (i) a condition of GRANTING/RENEWING a Maine firm license — § 12252(8) requires any CPA firm providing an attest service other than compilations to complete a peer review within 18 months of initial licensure and every 3 years thereafter, with an annual written no-attest certification available to firms that do none (implemented by 02-280 ch. 6 § 3, which also requires On-Site review where the attest work includes audits and permits Off-Site review otherwise); AND (ii) a condition of the NO-REGISTRATION attest privilege under route (a), § 12252(1)(A)(3)(a), which requires the out-of-state firm to 'qualif[y] for a firm license pursuant to subsections 3 and 8' — subsection 8 being peer review. It is NOT expressly stated as a condition of the § 12253 route (b); see open_questions.

FEES/CONTEXT: a Maine firm license is $35 annually (expiring September 30) with a $50 late fee; an individual Maine CPA license is $35 plus a $21 criminal background check. Those are LICENSURE fees and do not attach to the practice privilege. Maine still requires 150 semester hours for LICENSURE; PL 2025, c. 297 lowered only the hours needed to SIT for the exam to 120.

records.citation: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 2-321 (individual practice privilege, as amended by Ch. 406 of 2025 / SB 51, eff. 2025-10-01); § 2-401 (firm permit + no-office firm exemptions); § 2-4A-02 (peer review)
records.flux_note: Three items. (1) 2025 SB 51 / Ch. 406 rewrote the §2-321 equivalency test effective 2025-10-01 (already operative): out-of-state CPA is deemed substantially equivalent if the individual holds a valid CPA license from another state AND was required to pass the Uniform CPA Examination for it — decoupling MD mobility from other states' 150-hour changes. Effective-date clause is the standard 'October 1, 2025' (verified on official mgaleg bill page; not an emergency/supermajority-conditional clause; passed 45-0 Senate, 140-0 House). (2) 2026 HB 643 / Ch. 174 (new bachelor's+2yr licensure pathway) is enacted but NOT effective until 2026-10-01; it amends only §§2-302 and 2-303 (licensure qualifications) and does NOT touch §2-321 mobility or §2-401 firm rules. (3) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: the Board's firm-permit application page (cpaapplyfirm.shtml) still states out-of-state firms 'must obtain a permit' ('This requirement also pertains to CPA firms that are located in other states'), contradicting §2-401 (firm-mobility exemption effective 2019-10-01) and the Board's own firm-mobility page ('CPA firms that are licensed in another state will not have to hold a firm permit in Maryland'). The apply page appears stale (pre-2019); statute + the Board's dedicated mobility pages agree, so firm_registration_attest is recorded false, but the conflict is flagged here per protocol.
records.data_gap_note: The no-notice/no-fee rule is explicit only in the statute (§2-321(c)); the Board's mobility page is silent on notice/fee (consistent, not contradicting). Official COMAR online URL for 09.24.04 returned 404; COMAR 09.24.04.03 was read only via Cornell LII (unofficial) and contains no out-of-state/practice-privilege provision — whether any COMAR chapter implements mobility is unverified.
records.notes: Individual: §2-321 grants a true no-notice, no-fee practice privilege ('without any notice, fee, or other submission to the Board') to any out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is outside MD, holding a valid license obtained after being required to pass the Uniform CPA Exam. equivalence_test='other': statutory deemed-substantial-equivalency (near open CPA=CPA with an exam condition) — NOT NASBA state-level list, NOT individual education/experience criteria. Conditions: individual and employing firm consent to Board jurisdiction, compliance with MD law, home-state board as agent for service, and must cease if home license lapses. A practice-privilege sole practitioner may perform attest services only through a firm holding a §2-401 permit. Firms: a firm with NO MD office may perform attest services for a client in the State WITHOUT a permit if it '(1) meets the application and peer review requirements under §§ 2-402, 2-402.1, and 2-403 ... and § 2-4A-02; and (2) performs services through an individual with a practice privilege under § 2-321' (firm mobility law eff. 2019-10-01). Caveat: the phrase 'meets the application ... requirements' is ambiguous (qualify-as-if-applying vs. must file something); the Board's firm-mobility page reads it as no permit required. Non-attest/tax: a firm not meeting permit requirements may still perform non-attest professional services using the 'CPA'/'CPA firm' title without a permit if performed through a practice-privileged individual — so firm_registration_tax=false. peer_review_required=true is a condition OF THE NO-PERMIT ATTEST PRIVILEGE (via §2-4A-02: peer review at least every 3 years, AICPA-standard or Board-approved program), not of a registration — no registration exists for no-office firms. UPDATE (verifier): the 2025 mobility rewrite was a dual enactment - Ch. 406 (SB 51) and Ch. 407 (HB 887, cross-file). The 2-401(b)(2)/(d)(2) no-permit exemption carries a trailing condition the quotes truncate: the firm performs services "in the state where the individual with a practice privilege retains a principal place of business" - changes no boolean but is part of the operative conditions.

records.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87B(h)(2)-(3); § 87D(a), (m); § 87B1/2(k); St. 2020, c. 319 (Act Modernizing Public Accountancy, approved 2021-01-11)
records.flux_note: S.209 -> S.2946 'An Act relative to modernizing the pathway to becoming a certified public accountant' passed the Senate 37-0 on 2026-02-12 and has sat in House Ways and Means since 2026-02-17 (House companion H.4356, new draft of H.352, reported favorably 2025-08-07, also in House W&M). NOT ENACTED as of 2026-07-31 -- which is the last day of the 194th General Court's formal sessions, so it either completes passage imminently or dies/carries to informal sessions. If enacted as Senate-engrossed, SECTION 5 strikes the NASBA-NQAS language from 87B(h)(2) and replaces it with individual criteria (valid other-state CPA license + education/experience of 87A1/2(e) + passed Uniform CPA Exam, with grandfather for anyone holding a valid certificate on or before 2025-12-31); no-notice/no-fee language is retained. Effective-date clause is SECTION 6, a flat 'This act shall take effect on January 1, 2027' -- no supermajority-conditioned immediate-effect option exists in the bill, so no vote-count check is applicable. The 2027-01-01 date in rule_changes_on is CONTINGENT on enactment.
records.data_gap_note: Firm attest mobility: the board's formal guidance (voted 2023-01-19) is explicit that out-of-state firms with no MA office/principal place of business need no MA license, but the statutory basis requires definitional chaining -- 87D(m) deems a 'person qualified... pursuant to (h)(2)' a licensed person, 87A defines 'Person' to include 'corporation, association, partnership or other legal entity', and 87B(h)(3) treats the out-of-state firm as consenting to board jurisdiction while acting through its mobile CPA agent; no single sentence of the compiled statute says 'firms need not register'. Also: mass.gov is bot-protected (HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); board pages were verified via Internet Archive snapshots of 2025-11-13 and 2026-05-12 (identical guidance text in both). 252 CMR 2.15 (quality review) official text was not fetchable from mass.gov; its content was corroborated via the board's own peer-review reminder guidance and Cornell LII's reproduction.
records.notes: Massachusetts is a full-mobility state since St. 2020 c. 319 (approved 2021-01-11), which struck former 87B(h)(1) -- the board calls it removing 'the last barrier to mobility'. Individuals: out-of-state CPAs with principal place of business outside MA practice (including attest) with no license, no notice, no fee, under 87B(h)(2); current codified test is NASBA NQAS state-level substantial-equivalence verification (individual NQAS verification as fallback), and the board states all states have been deemed substantially equivalent. Firms: out-of-state firms with NO physical office or principal place of business in MA may provide services (attest and non-attest) without a MA firm license per board guidance; firms WITH a MA office/PPB must be licensed (87B1/2, 87D(e)). An out-of-state firm that does seek a MA license uses 87B1/2(k), which conditions issuance on compliance with firm ownership AND peer review requirements; 252 CMR 2.15 makes completed quality review (within 3 years) a firm-license renewal condition and requires firms newly undertaking audit/attest to undergo review within 18 months. peer_review_required=true refers to the FIRM LICENSE, not the no-registration mobility privilege -- the privilege itself is not peer-review-conditioned on the face of the statute or board guidance. Tax/non-attest: 87D(a) restricts only report issuance; tax return preparation and non-attest services are expressly outside the prohibition, and board guidance draws no attest/non-attest distinction for no-office out-of-state firms.

records.citation: MCL 339.727a (individual practice privilege, no notice/fee); MCL 339.728(1), (4), (5) (firm licensure trigger = in-state office; no-license out-of-state firm practice incl. attest); MCL 339.729(2) (peer review condition); MCL 339.734a (conditions of privilege). Occupational Code, 1980 PA 299, Art. 7.
records.flux_note: HB 4893 (2025-26 session) rewrites the licensure pathways in MCL 339.725 AND the 727a mobility equivalency test: new-language 727a would recognize licenses from jurisdictions requiring the uniform CPA exam plus any of three education/experience combos (150hr+1yr; post-baccalaureate accounting degree+1yr; 120hr/bachelor's+2yr), with a grandfather clause for individuals holding valid licenses as of 2024-12-31. Status: passed House 93-9 on 2025-11-12; referred to Senate Regulatory Affairs Committee 2025-12-02; still awaiting Senate hearing per MICPA update of 2026-03-17; NOT enacted -- compiled MCL current through PA 16 of 2026 (rendered 2026-06-13) still shows the existing 727a text. The bill's own effective-date clause reads 'This amendatory act takes effect 90 days after the date it is enacted into law,' so no changeover date exists yet (rule_changes_on null; the supermajority immediate-effect check is moot until enactment). SECOND flux item (stale board page): a legacy LARA 'CPA Firms' page (old CMS URL 0,4601,7-154-89334_72600_72602_72731_72855_91572-358925--,00.html) still serves the PRE-2018 version of section 728, which required firm licensure when a firm without a Michigan office performed audit/prospective-financial-examination/PCAOB engagements for a client with its home office in Michigan, and allowed only review/compilation without a license. PA 81 of 2018 (eff. 2018-06-17) repealed that home-office trigger; current 728(5) allows attest without a license. The board's current firm guide (rev 2026-01-26) and PA 81 notice match the current statute; the stale page is legacy content but still publicly served and surfaces in search results. UPDATE (verifier): TWO additional pending Senate bills introduced 2026-07-15 (Sen. Moss, Senate Regulatory Affairs) directly touch the answered sections: SB 1112 amends MCL 339.724 + 339.728 (temporary permit + the FIRM LICENSURE section under firm_registration_attest/tax) and SB 1113 amends MCL 339.725 + 339.727a + 339.729 (pathways, the PRACTICE-PRIVILEGE section itself, and peer review; apparent Senate counterpart to HB 4893). Scope correction: engrossed HB 4893 (H-2) amends 339.725, 727a AND 729. Currency: compiled MCL current through PA 20 of 2026 with 727a unchanged; MICPA confirmed HB 4893 still in Senate Regulatory Affairs as of 2026-06-09. Third-party aggregator claims that HB 4893 'became law 12/02/2025' are FALSE (that date was committee referral; no PA number exists). 2025 MR 18 accountancy admin-rule update (eff. 2025-09-29) checked - immaterial to recorded fields.
records.flux_summary: A bill that would rewrite Michigan's mobility rule (HB 4893) has passed the House but is still waiting on a Senate committee hearing -- it is not law yet, and Michigan's current rule is unchanged for now. Two related Senate bills were introduced in July 2026. We're watching this legislation, not reacting to a change that hasn't happened. Confirm directly with the Michigan Board before relying on this.
records.data_gap_note: The no-notice/no-fee answer rests on the unambiguous statute text of 727a(2); no CURRENT board webpage restates the individual practice privilege in its own words (the board's acknowledgment of 727a privileges appears in its firm-licensing materials and a legacy page), so treat notice_required/fee_required as statute-anchored with board-side silence rather than board-side confirmation. Could not confirm HB 4893 status between 2026-06-13 (compiled-MCL cutoff showing no change) and 2026-07-31; monitor the bill page.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: 727a grants out-of-state CPAs (principal place of business elsewhere) 'all the privileges of licensees' with no certificate, license, permit, notice, fee, or submission; conditions of exercise are consent to board jurisdiction etc. under 734a. Equivalence test operates at the licensing-JURISDICTION level (does the other jurisdiction require 150 semester hours + uniform CPA exam + 1 year experience), with an individual substantial-equivalency fallback in 727a(1)(b) for licensees of non-equivalent jurisdictions (pre-2012-exam licensees exempt from the education element). Statute does NOT name NASBA/NQAS -- classified nasba_state_level because the primary test is jurisdiction-level UAA-style equivalency; note the individual fallback. A temporary practice permit ($100, max 1 yr, per-engagement info) exists under 724(b) ONLY for out-of-state accountants who do NOT meet 727a. FIRMS: licensure required only if the firm 'establishes or maintains an office in this state' (728(1)); $300 initial/2-yr, $200 renewal per board guide rev 2026-01-26. A firm with NO Michigan office may perform review/SSAE engagements/compilations (728(4)) and full attest or ANY other professional services incl. tax while using the CPA-firm title (728(5)) WITHOUT a Michigan license, if it (a) works through a 727a-privileged individual, (b) is authorized for those services in that individual's home jurisdiction, and (c) meets 728(2)(a) CPA-majority ownership, 728(2)(b) licensed-CPA supervision of attest/compilation, and 729(2) peer review. So firm_registration_attest = false (no registration/permit, but substantive conditions incl. peer review apply) and firm_registration_tax = false (same no-license route; tax = 'any other professional services'). PEER REVIEW: true -- it is a condition of the no-registration out-of-state practice route (728(4)(a) and 728(5)(c) both incorporate 729(2)), not of a registration, and 729(2) itself obligates only firms performing audits, reviews, or compilations relied on by third parties; a tax-only out-of-state firm would not trigger the peer-review program. For Michigan-licensed firms peer review is a renewal condition (proof within preceding 3 years, 729(3)).

records.citation: Minn. Stat. § 326A.14 (mobility, as amended by Laws of Minnesota 2025, ch. 39, art. 4, § 16); Minn. Stat. § 326A.05, subd. 1 (firm permits); Minn. R. 1105.7900 (interstate mobility, as amended eff. 2026 per 50 SR 812)
records.flux_note: Changeover complete. Laws 2025 ch. 39 (SF 3045), art. 4 s. 16 replaced the NASBA/state-level substantial-equivalency test in 326A.14 with individual criteria (good-standing license + bachelor's with accounting concentration + passed Uniform CPA Exam); the section's own clause reads 'This section is effective the day following final enactment' (unconditional — no supermajority-contingent immediate-effect mechanism in MN), and the chapter was signed by the governor May 23, 2025, so the mobility rewrite took effect 2025-05-24. Companion licensure-pathway changes (326A.03 subd. 6a bachelor's+2yr, 6b transitional) took effect 2026-01-01, with the 150-hour pathway sunsetting 2030-07-01. Board conforming expedited rules (RD4940: Minn. R. 1105.1500, .2600, .2900, .3800, .7900; item D of 1105.7900 repealed by the session law) were approved by an ALJ 2025-12-19 and are now the compiled rule text (history 50 SR 812; published electronically 2026-03-30) — compiled statute and compiled rule agree. The board's LEGACY site (boa.state.mn.us) still described the pre-2025 NASBA/NQAS regime as late as a 2025-09-06 archive snapshot (stale guidance), but that site now 301-redirects to the new mn.gov/boa site; no live board page contradicting the current statute could be confirmed (new site is bot-gated). No 2026-session amendments to ch. 326A found.
records.data_gap_note: The board's current website (mn.gov/boa, including /apply-for-a-mn-license/already-licensed-in-another-state.jsp and /firms/) is behind Radware Bot Manager (CAPTCHA to curl and WebFetch) and is not archived in Wayback, so live board guidance could not be read directly; the board-page leg of dual-sourcing rests on archived board-authored pages (nonres.html snapshot 2025-09-06; rulemaking.html snapshot 2025-12-06) plus the board's own adopted rule 1105.7900. firm_registration_tax=false rests primarily on the codified statute (326A.05 subd. 1(c)); the archived board firm statement ('If your client is headquartered in Minnesota, your firm must obtain a Minnesota firm license') does not distinguish attest from non-attest — read it as shorthand for the attest rule, but confirm live board guidance when accessible. Exact State Register publication date of the rules' Notice of Adoption (50 SR 812; expedited rules effective on publication) was not independently verified — one secondary result claimed effective 2026-02-14; the compiled rule is dated 'published electronically March 30, 2026'. UPDATE (verifier): the RD4940 rules adoption (2025-12-12) and effective date (2026-02-14) are corroborated by the board's own rulemaking page - no longer single-source. DiffLab design note: mn.gov/boa HOMEPAGE is fetchable but subpages trip a Radware gate; boa.state.mn.us 301-redirects to mn.gov/boa (re-confirmed 2026-07-31). Residual un-conformed artifact: rule 1105.7900 item B still carries an "(a) or (b)" cross-reference alongside the 326A.05 clause-(5) quirk.
records.notes: Scheme: automatic no-notice, no-fee individual mobility on individual criteria (326A.14 subd. 1(a): good-standing out-of-state license + bachelor's or higher with accounting concentration or board-determined equivalent + passed Uniform CPA Exam); consent-to-jurisdiction conditions in subd. 1(c). Practice-privilege individuals performing attest services (326A.01 subd. 2 clauses (1) SAS audits, (4) SSAE examinations of prospective financials, (5) PCAOB engagements) for entities headquartered in MN may do so only through a firm holding an MN permit (326A.14 subd. 1(d); 326A.05 subd. 1(a)(4)). Out-of-state firms without an MN office: MN permit required for those attest services for MN-HQ clients; a narrow no-permit path exists under 326A.05 subd. 1(b) for services in 326A.01 subd. 2 'clause (2) or (5)' (GAGAS; PCAOB) and compilations (subd. 6), conditioned on majority-CPA ownership, home-state peer review equivalent to subd. 8 paras. (a)/(e), and performance through a practice-privilege individual. INTERNAL QUIRK: clause (5) (PCAOB) appears in BOTH the permit mandate (a)(4) and the no-permit path (b), and SSARS reviews (clause (3)) appear in neither list — likely un-conformed cross-references from the 2015 renumbering of the attest definition; conservative reading applied (permit required for attest for MN-HQ clients). Non-attest/tax services: no firm permit needed under subd. 1(c) if ownership-qualified, performed through a practice-privilege individual, and lawful in the home state. peer_review_required=true refers to (i) peer review as a statutory condition of MN firm-permit renewal (subd. 8(a), max once every 3 years) and (ii) home-state equivalent peer review as a condition of the subd. 1(b) no-permit attest path — not a separate condition on the individual privilege. MN also registers non-CPA 'RAPs' (registered accounting practitioners), irrelevant to CPA mobility.

records.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-33-17 (as amended by H.B. 1137, 2026 Reg. Sess., ch. 315, eff. July 1, 2026); Miss. Code Ann. § 73-33-1(3)
records.flux_note: HB 1137 (2026 ch. 315), effective 2026-07-01 (30 days before verification), replaced the state-level substantial-equivalency mobility test in 73-33-17 with an individual-criteria test: valid CPA license from ANY state + passed all sections of the Uniform CPA Exam + completed the education/experience requirements of 73-33-5(2)-(3) (which now include a bachelor's-degree + 2-years-experience pathway). A grandfather clause (new 73-33-17(2)) preserves practice privileges for out-of-state CPAs who held privileges on or before 2025-12-31. HOWEVER, the board's compiled Rules & Regulations (April 2026 edition, still current on the board site) and its Licensing & Exams web guidance still state the PRE-amendment test ('valid CPA license from a substantially equivalent jurisdiction OR ... individual qualifications ... substantially equivalent'), and the board's statute reprint in the same PDF is the pre-HB1137 text — stale board guidance vs. current statute. The disagreement concerns WHICH equivalence test applies, not whether privilege/notice/fee/firm-permit obligations exist (those are identical in both texts). Recorded the enacted statute's test (individual_criteria), which is also the stricter reading. Board rulemaking to implement HB 1137 (accounting-concentration and experience definitions are delegated to board rule) had not yet appeared as of 2026-07-31.
records.data_gap_note: Miss. Code 73-33-1 (firm permits) was verified via Justia's 2024 code reprint plus the board's own statutes reprint (April 2026 PDF) — HB 1137 did not amend 73-33-1, so both are current — but the official LexisNexis-published MS Code itself was not fetched (Justia 403s generic fetchers; needed browser UA). Open interpretive question: how the board will apply 'completed the education and experience requirements in Section 73-33-5(2) and (3)' to out-of-state CPAs (facially, a 120-hour licensee from another state qualifies with 2 years' experience under 73-33-5(2)(c)/(3)(b)); no post-HB1137 board guidance exists yet.
records.notes: Scheme (current statute, eff. 2026-07-01): individual out-of-state CPAs get automatic no-notice, no-fee practice privilege if principal place of business is outside MS, they hold a valid license from any state, passed all sections of the Uniform CPA Exam, and meet MS education/experience requirements (73-33-5(2)-(3)); privileges held on/before 2025-12-31 are grandfathered. Privileged individuals/firms consent to board jurisdiction (73-33-17(3)). FIRMS: a firm with NO MS office needs a permit under 73-33-1(3)(a) ONLY to perform 73-33-17(4) services (SAS financial-statement audits, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, PCAOB engagements) for a client with its home office in MS -> firm_registration_attest=true. SSARS reviews and compilations for MS-home-office clients may be done WITHOUT a permit under 73-33-1(3)(b) only if the firm meets ownership qualifications, 'complies with the peer review requirements set forth by board rule,' and works through a privileged individual. Other services (tax/consulting) need no permit under 73-33-1(3)(c) if performed through a privileged individual and lawful in the firm's home state -> firm_registration_tax=false (conditional exemption, not unconditional). peer_review_required=true refers to BOTH: peer-review compliance is a condition of obtaining/renewing the firm permit (Board Rule 3.1.6(a) and Rule 3.1.1/Chapter 5), AND a statutory condition of the no-permit review/compilation privilege (73-33-1(3)(b)). Reciprocal licensure (73-33-9) remains available but is expressly separate from 73-33-17 practice privilege. UPDATE (verifier): HB 1137 signing date resolved to 2026-03-13 (legislature official history XML + MSCPA June 2026 session summary; the 3/16 date in an earlier MSCPA article is wrong). Caution for future verifiers: the board site's "FINAL PROPOSED SET OF RULES INITIALLY ADOPTED BY BOARD.pdf" is a PRE-2026 document containing no HB1137/73-33-5(2) language - it is not post-HB1137 rulemaking.

records.citation: RSMo § 326.283 (individual practice privilege); RSMo § 326.289 (firm permits); 20 CSR 2010-2.022 (Privilege to Practice)
records.flux_note: TWO issues. (1) ENACTED CHANGE: SB 1233 (2026), signed by Gov. Kehoe July 2026, repeals the substantial-equivalency test in 326.283 and replaces it with INDIVIDUAL CRITERIA: a valid unrestricted license in good standing from any state, provided that at initial licensure the individual passed the Uniform CPA Exam and met one of three education/experience combos (bachelor's + accounting concentration + 2 yrs experience; bachelor's + 30 hrs + 1 yr; post-baccalaureate degree + 1 yr). Grandfather clause preserves privileges for anyone licensed and holding MO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31. No-notice/no-fee language is retained. Also adds a sole-practitioner/single-member-LLC exemption request from the CPA-title firm-permit requirement (non-attest only). The TAT text has NO emergency clause for the accountancy sections (the only contingent-effective-date section, Section B, covers interior-design repeals 324.406/324.424), so ch. 326 changes take effect on Missouri's constitutional default date 2026-08-28; press coverage (Accounting Today, CFO Dive, Inside Public Accounting) uniformly confirms Aug. 28, 2026. On that date equivalence_test flips from nasba_state_level to individual_criteria. (2) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm_registration_attest: compiled statute 326.289.1(2) (as amended 2020, HB 2046) lets a firm with NO office in Missouri perform attest/compilation WITHOUT a permit if it meets ownership, peer-review, practice-privilege-individual, and lawful-in-home-state conditions; but the board's still-compiled rule 20 CSR 2010-2.022(5) (last amended eff. 2012-06-30, authority cites RSMo Supp. 2011) states attest services for a client with a home office in Missouri must be performed 'through a firm holding a current permit to practice in this state,' and the board's Initial Firm Permit application (form 375-0715) still instructs out-of-state firms on obtaining a permit to provide attest/review/compilation services. Per the conservative rule, firm_registration_attest is recorded TRUE (permit required); the statute's no-permit pathway is quoted in the quotes array. No board rulemaking to conform 2.022 to the 2020 statute or to SB 1233 was pending on the DCI proposed-rules page as of 2026-07-31.
records.data_gap_note: The board site (pr.mo.gov) has no standing mobility/practice-privilege guidance page; board-side evidence comes from the board's promulgated rule 20 CSR 2010-2.022 and the board's Initial Firm Permit application form. firm_registration_tax=false rests on statute 326.289.1(3) plus rule silence — no affirmative board guidance page addresses non-attest out-of-state firms. firm_registration_attest is a conservative value forced by a statute/rule conflict, not an agreed dual-source answer.
records.notes: Current law (through 2026-08-27): UAA-style mobility. Individuals with principal place of business outside MO and a license from a state the board/NASBA NQAS deems substantially equivalent (or individually equivalent) practice with no notice, no fee, no registration (326.283.1). Attest/compilation by a privileged individual must comply with 326.289. Individuals with a valid but RESTRICTED license must apply to the board for practice privilege (20 CSR 2010-2.022(2)). Firm side: MO-office firms doing attest/compilation or using the CPA title need a permit (326.289.1(1)); no-office firms have a statutory no-permit attest pathway conditioned on ownership qualifications, peer review compliance, performance through a practice-privileged individual, and lawfulness in the individual's home state (326.289.1(2)) — but see flux_note conflict with rule 2.022(5); no-office firms may perform nonattest/noncompilation services under the CPA title without a permit through a privileged individual (326.289.1(3)). Peer review is both a permit-renewal condition (326.289.9, max once every 3 years, implemented at 20 CSR 2010-5.070–5.080) AND an express condition of the no-permit out-of-state attest pathway (326.289.1(2)(b)); the board firm-permit form states firms performing compilations/reviews/audits MUST be enrolled in a peer review program. Separate from board permits, 326.289.1(4)(a) requires all firms practicing public accounting in MO to register with the secretary of state (corporate qualification; sole proprietorships and general partnerships exempt). 326.283 also preserves temporary practice incidental to a CPA's regular out-of-state practice. From 2026-08-28 (SB 1233): individual-criteria mobility with 2024-12-31 grandfather; sole-practitioner exemption request added to 326.289.

records.citation: Mont. Code Ann. § 37-50-325 (practice privilege for nonresident certified public accountant -- rules); § 37-50-335 (registration of firms -- exemptions); § 37-50-330 (firm ownership); ARM 24.201.531 (practice privilege); ARM 24.201.1108 (peer review alternatives and exemptions)
records.flux_note: Montana's MOBILITY provisions themselves were NOT amended in the 2025-26 wave: MCA 37-50-325 (individual practice privilege) and 37-50-335 (firm mobility) both carry history ending at 'amd. Sec. 3/5, Ch. 162, L. 2017' in the Montana Code Annotated 2025, and board rule ARM 24.201.531 (PRACTICE PRIVILEGE) is still the version effective 2014-11-21. Montana was nonetheless touched by the wave on adjacent fronts, all now already operative: (1) SB 166 (Ch. 346, L. 2025) rewrote the education pathway in MCA 37-50-305, dropping the express 150-semester-hour rule in favor of board-set coursework -- enrolled act Sec. 2 reads 'Effective date. [This act] is effective January 1, 2026' (delayed effective date stated in the act's own title; no immediate-effect/supermajority option, so no vote-count check was needed); implementing board rules ARM 24.201.502/.503/.516 were amended effective 2025-09-13 (MAR Notice 2025-167.2). (2) HB 246 (Ch. 76, L. 2025), effective 2025-10-01, standardized 'substantial equivalency' determinations across all Title 37 licensing boards (amending MCA 37-1-302, 37-1-304 and, within accountancy, 37-50-203) and repealed duplicative reciprocity sections -- it did NOT amend 37-50-325 or 37-50-335. (3) Implementing HB 246, the board adopted NEW ARM 24.201.527 SUBSTANTIAL EQUIVALENCY (MAR Notice 2025-350, effective 2026-03-07), which incorporates by reference a board-published '2025 substantial equivalency list.' That new rule is expressly limited to endorsement LICENSE APPLICATIONS ('License applications from individuals licensed in substantially equivalent states are routine applications...'; implementing statute 37-1-304, MCA), and the adopting notice states the change 'does not change the board's existing practices for licensing out-of-state accountants.' rule_changes_on is set to the most recent operative equivalency-related changeover (2026-03-07). Watch item, not a present conflict: Montana now has two coexisting equivalency mechanisms -- ARM 24.201.531(2) (NASBA-approved jurisdictions deemed substantially equivalent, governs PRACTICE PRIVILEGE) and ARM 24.201.527 (board-published list, governs ENDORSEMENT). If the board's list ever diverges from NASBA's, the two could be read against each other; today they address different pathways and do not state opposite answers for any field recorded here. Montana's legislature meets in odd years only, so no 2026 regular session bill exists; next regular session convenes January 2027.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: MCA 37-50-325(1)(a) grants a nonresident CPA whose principal place of business is outside Montana, holding a valid license from a state NASBA/NQAS has verified as substantially equivalent, 'all the privileges of persons holding a license of this state without the need to obtain a license under 37-50-302,' and (1)(b) states 'no notice, fee, or other submission is required.' Subsection (2) supplies an INDIVIDUAL-criteria fallback for CPAs licensed in a non-verified state: they get the same privilege if they personally obtain NQAS verification that their own CPA qualifications are substantially equivalent (with a pre-2012 licensure education grandfather in (2)(b)). equivalence_test is therefore recorded as nasba_state_level because that is the primary/default test (and ARM 24.201.531(2): 'The board has determined that all jurisdictions approved by NASBA are deemed to be "substantially equivalent."'), with an individual-NQAS alternate route. Note the fee/notice caveat in 37-50-325(2)(c): 'no notice, fee, or other submission is required unless the person is required to register pursuant to 37-50-335' -- i.e., firm registration duties still attach to firms that establish or maintain an office in Montana. Conditions of the privilege (37-50-325(3)): consent to board jurisdiction and discipline, compliance with chapter 37-50 and board rules, cease practice if the home-state license lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process. FIRMS: 37-50-335(1) requires ANNUAL registration only of 'All firms that establish or maintain offices in this state for the practice of public accounting'; 37-50-335(2) allows a fee for that annual registration. An out-of-state firm with NO Montana office needs no registration for either attest or non-attest work: 37-50-335(4) lets it 'use the title "CPA" or "CPA firm" in this state without registering' and (a) render attest services and compilations if it complies with Montana peer review and firm ownership qualifications, works through an individual with 37-50-325 practice privileges, and holds home-state privileges covering attest/compilation; or (b) perform non-attest professional services if it works through a person with 37-50-325 practice privileges and holds home-state privileges for those services. Both firm_registration_attest and firm_registration_tax are therefore false FOR FIRMS WITHOUT A MONTANA OFFICE; a Montana office triggers registration for either service type. Attest work for a Montana-home-office client must still be done through a firm complying with 37-50-335 (37-50-325(4)). PEER REVIEW: peer_review_required = true and it is a condition of the NO-REGISTRATION ATTEST PRIVILEGE, not of a firm permit -- 37-50-335(4)(a)(i) conditions the out-of-state firm's attest/compilation privilege on complying with 'the state's peer review and firm ownership qualifications.' Importantly, ARM 24.201.1108(1)(a) exempts from the Montana peer review requirement 'out-of-state firms that do not have a physical location in this state, but perform attest or compilation services in this state, and have a peer review in the state in which they are located, and are otherwise qualified for practice privileges' -- so the condition is satisfied by a home-state peer review, not by enrolling in Montana's program. Peer review is NOT a condition of the non-attest (tax) firm privilege under 37-50-335(4)(b). Registered Montana firms must enroll in a board-approved peer review program if they perform audits, reviews, compilations, SSAE engagements, or non-issuer PCAOB-standard engagements (ARM 24.201.1103(1)); the program is currently administered for Montana by the Nevada Society of CPAs. FIRM OWNERSHIP: 37-50-330(1)(b) requires that 'a simple majority of ownership in the firm, in terms of equity and voting rights, is held by accountants' licensed in Montana or in a substantially equivalent jurisdiction or qualifying for practice privilege.

records.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 1-125.01 (as amended by Laws 2026, LB718, § 5, eff. 2026-07-18); firm permits Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 1-126, 1-134, 1-135, 1-136; peer review Neb. Rev. Stat. § 1-153 and 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 13, § 004.01; practice privilege rule 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 7, § 001.02
records.flux_note: Nebraska joined the 2025-26 wave: LB718 (signed 2026-02-25, no emergency clause, effective 2026-07-18 per the Legislature's compiled-statute effective-date line) rewrote § 1-125.01, moving inbound mobility FROM open CPA=CPA (any active out-of-state CPA license sufficed, 2009 LB31 text now stricken) TO individual-criteria guardrails: the CPA must have passed the Uniform CPA Exam and, at initial licensure, met minimum education/experience requirements defined by the board. Implementing rules (288 NAC ch. 3, 7, 8, 9, 13) were filed/updated 2026-07-25 — 288 NAC 7-001.02A defines the criteria as the three Nebraska pathways (master's+1yr, bachelor's+30hr+1yr, or bachelor's+2yr) and 7-001.02B grandfathers anyone who held privileges as of 2024-12-31. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm registration for non-attest work: the amended statute conditions only ATTEST (for entities with home office in NE) on a firm permit and grants individuals privilege with no notice/fee, but the board's live web guidance (Apply for Permit page: 'Firms must register with the Board if they are practicing public accountancy in the state of Nebraska and/or for a Nebraska client'; firm FAQ: any CPA planning 'public accounting work' in NE 'must license their CPA firm in Nebraska') requires firm registration for ANY Nebraska-client work — the conservative value (firm_registration_tax=true) is recorded per policy. Board mobility page is stale (still points to cpamobility.org and 2010 rule-change documents). UPDATE (verifier): prior-wave context - LB854 (2024, eff. 2025-01-01) lowered exam-sitting eligibility to 120 hours; LB718 completed the licensure-pathway changes.
records.data_gap_note: firm_registration_tax=true is the CONSERVATIVE value from a live statute-vs-board-guidance conflict: § 1-125.01(4) as amended requires a NE firm permit only for attestation services for entities with home office in NE, but the board's Apply-for-Permit page and firm FAQ (not yet updated post-LB718) require registration for any public accountancy work for a Nebraska client and provide out-of-state firm application tracks. Statute-only reading would make it false; do not present false without board confirmation.
records.notes: Nebraska is two-tier (certificate + permit) domestically, but inbound individual mobility is no-notice/no-fee under § 1-125.01: out-of-state CPAs with principal place of business elsewhere practice and use the CPA title 'without the need to hold a certificate or a permit... or to notify or register with the board or pay any fee', subject to the new individual-criteria guardrails (exam + education/experience at initial licensure; 288 NAC 7-001.02A three-pathway test; pre-2025 privilege holders grandfathered by 7-001.02B). Not eligible if license under suspension/revocation (other than fee nonpayment/CPE). Consent to board jurisdiction is automatic. Governmental bodies may still demand NE-permitted persons/firms (§ 1-125.01(3)). FIRM side: attest for any entity with home office in NE may only be performed through a firm holding a NE permit under § 1-136 (statute), and the board demands firm registration for any NE-client public accountancy work (broader guidance; see flux_note); out-of-state firms need not have an NE-licensed partner but must name the licensed partner responsible for Nebraska business (board Apply-for-Permit page). PEER REVIEW: required as a condition of the firm permit for practice units performing attest engagements and/or compilations (288 NAC 13-004.01, updated 2026-07-25; § 1-153 authorizes; board peer-review page: 'a requirement... as a condition for obtaining a firm permit for firms that perform attest and/or compilation engagements'); firms performing only SSARS preparation engagements or no reviewable engagements are exempt. Peer review attaches to the firm permit, not to the individual no-registration privilege. LB718 also repealed § 1-136.04 and rewrote licensure pathways (§ 1-136.02).

records.citation: NRS 628.315 (practice privilege, individuals and firms); NRS 628.335 (firm registration limited to firms with an office in Nevada); NAC 628.580 with NAC 628.010 (practice-monitoring/peer review applies to privilege holders performing attest-type services)
records.flux_note: No pending mobility change and no statute/board disagreement found. Context: Nevada joined the 2025-26 licensure wave, but only on pathways, not mobility -- the 2025 session moved licensure requirements from statute to board regulation, and the Board's adopted pathway regulation (R054-25 lineage; bachelor's + 2 years experience + exam) took effect 2026-02-27. Because NRS 628.315 grants an open CPA=CPA privilege with no substantial-equivalency test, pathway changes in other states do not alter Nevada mobility answers. Firm-level mobility itself dates from SB 437 (2023), ch. 61, Stats. of Nevada 2023 p. 298-301, effective 2023-07-01 (NRS 628.315 history line: 'Added to NRS by 2009, 311; A 2023, 300'). UPDATE (verifier): the unresolved 2025-session bill number is now CONFIRMED as AB 510 (2025), ch. 29, Stats. of Nevada 2025 pp. 148-151, eff. 2025-05-26 for regulation-adoption purposes - named throughout the official R054-25 adopted text and informational statement (leg.state.nv.us/Register/RegsReviewed/$R054-25A.pdf), which also independently confirms the SB 437 (2023) ch. 61 citation for NRS 628.335.
records.data_gap_note: peer_review_required=true rests on the codified rule leg only for its application to out-of-state privilege holders: NAC 628.580(1) requires 'a practitioner' performing audit/review/full disclosure compilation/attestation services to enroll in a board-approved practice-monitoring program, and NAC 628.010 defines 'practitioner' to include a CPA or CPA firm 'granted practice privileges pursuant to NRS 628.315'; the Board's peer-review web page describes the requirement only for 'licensees' and is silent on privilege holders. Conservative (more-demanding) reading recorded per liability rule. Note also NAC 628.580(4): a practitioner not performing such services reports that fact, and one entering a first such engagement must notify the Board within 60 days and enroll within 18 months. NRS ch. 628 itself contains no peer-review text; the requirement is regulatory (NAC) only.
records.notes: Nevada is an open CPA=CPA mobility state for BOTH individuals and firms -- unusual: NRS 628.315(1) deems a natural person with a valid CPA license in good standing from any other state, AND a CPA firm holding a valid registration in good standing from any other state, to be a Nevada CPA/CPA firm 'for all purposes under the laws of this State other than this chapter.' No substantial-equivalency/NASBA test appears anywhere, hence equivalence_test='other'. NRS 628.315(2) expressly waives the certificate (628.190), permit (628.380), and firm registration (628.335); no notice filing and no fee exist. NRS 628.335(2) requires firm registration only for firms 'with an office in this State,' for attest, compilation, public accounting practice, or CPA-styled naming -- so firm_registration_attest and firm_registration_tax are both false for firms with no Nevada office (a firm opening a Nevada office must register regardless of service line). Conditions of the privilege (NRS 628.315(3)): consent to Board jurisdiction/discipline, compliance with ch. 628 and Board regulations (which pulls in the NAC practice-monitoring requirement for attest-type work), cessation if the principal-place-of-business license/registration lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process. Board's out-of-state page matches the statute verbatim in substance and cites cpamobility.org. Board web guidance is NOT stale.

records.citation: RSA 309-B:6-a (Mobility), as enacted by N.H. Laws 2026, ch. 34, sec. 34:5 (HB 1259), eff. Apr. 22, 2026; RSA 309-B:8, I(a)(3), I(b), III, VIII; RSA 309-B:14, I, XVI; N.H. Admin. R. Ac 302.05, Ac 303.05, Ac 405.02
records.flux_note: NH is mid-transition on three separate axes. (1) NEW ACT NOT YET CODIFIED: HB 1259 = Chapter 34, Laws of 2026, signed and effective 2026-04-22 (sec. 34:7 'This act shall take effect upon its passage'; act footer 'Approved: April 22, 2026 / Effective Date: April 22, 2026' -- no supermajority/immediate-effect condition existed, so no vote-count check was required). Sec. 34:5 inserts a brand-new RSA 309-B:6-a 'Mobility' granting no-notice/no-fee practice privilege, and sec. 34:1 STRIKES the RSA 309-B:3, XVIII definition of 'substantial equivalency' (verified against the enrolled HTML: the deleted text is inside class cs12BD948D = text-decoration:line-through and is bracketed, so this is a genuine deletion, not lost strike markup). As of 2026-07-31 the official RSA compilation at gc.nh.gov does NOT yet reflect Chapter 34: gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/XXX/309-B/309-B-6-a.htm returns 404, the chapter TOC has no 309-B:6-a, and the compiled 309-B:3 still prints the repealed 'substantial equivalency' definition and the 'May 2014' UAA edition. So the enacted act and the compiled statute currently DISAGREE (compilation lag). (2) DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCES: the prior practice-privilege section RSA 309-B:6 was repealed by 2024, 327:159, eff. 2024-07-01, yet RSA 309-B:8, I(a)(3)(B), I(b)(1), III(c)-(d) and RSA 309-B:14, I-XIV still condition firm and individual exemptions on 'practice privileges under RSA 309-B:6 and RSA 310:17'. RSA 310:17 is a license-RECIPROCITY (endorsement) provision, not a practice privilege. HB 1259 did not conform those cross-references to the new 309-B:6-a. (3) BOARD RULEMAKING PENDING: NH Board of Accountancy minutes of 2026-04-27 record 'HB1259 signed into law' and a 5-0 vote to 'request rulemaking support for Ac 300'; no Ac 300 amendment appears in the Rulemaking Register through issue No. 30 (2026-07-30). The current Ac rules (Ac 300 eff. 2025-12-05; Ac 400 eff. 2025-09-14) predate the act, and Ac 302.05(a) ('permit ... required for all CPA firms wishing to do business in NH') is broader than RSA 309-B:8, I(b), which lets a no-office firm perform non-attest services without a permit -- a statute-vs-compiled-rule conflict resolved here in the conservative direction (firm_registration_tax = true). UPDATE (verifier): (1) FETCHER CORRECTION - gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/XXX/309-B/309-B-6-a.htm does NOT return 404; it returns HTTP 200 serving the General Court SOFT-404 page (title "The General Court of New Hampshire | 404", body "ERROR 404 - Page Not Found"). DiffLab must monitor that URL on BODY CONTENT, not status code, or the new section appearing will never fire. (2) Act sec. 34:6 also repealed RSA 309-B:7, VI and VII (substantially equivalent FOREIGN designation applicants), removing the foreign-designation substantial-equivalency route - it belongs in the equivalence_test picture. (3) NEW HAMPSHIRE IS CURRENTLY A HYBRID and a single equivalence_test value loses this: RSA 309-B:6-a, II grandfathers anyone holding practice privileges on 2026-04-22 under the OLD state-based substantial-equivalency route, so NH runs individual_criteria PROSPECTIVELY while a grandfathered cohort continues under state-based substantial equivalency. (4) Rulemaking detail: board minutes item III.C records "Ac 300 - Certification - Addition approved by Board Chair 4/23" plus a 5-0 vote to certify Ac 300 and authorize the chair to sign the certification letter. (5) Pending OPLC rulemaking Notices 2026-121 / 2026-122 (Rulemaking Register No. 25, 2026-06-25) propose amending Plc 1001/1002/1004 "Chapter Specific Definitions and Fees" - Plc 1002.01 is the source of the $66 firm permit fee cited in notes, so that figure is itself in flux.
records.data_gap_note: The no-notice / no-fee / individual-criteria mechanics rest primarily on the enacted act text (NH General Court, Chapter 34 final version). OPLC has published NO post-enactment mobility guidance: the board's Winter 2026 newsletter describes HB 1259 only as a '2026 STATUTE CHANGE PROPOSAL', and the board leg for enactment is the 2026-04-27 public minutes. The board's own CPA/PA firm permit application (Rev. 11/30/21, still the live form) cites repealed RSA 309-B:6 and superseded rule 'Administrative Rule 402.05' (peer review is now Ac 405.02), and it does not mention the RSA 309-B:8, I(a)(3) no-permit exemption at all. Firm mobility is therefore recorded conservatively: no primary source confirms that an out-of-state firm may rely on the attest exemption now that its predicate (a 309-B:6 privilege) has been repealed and replaced by 309-B:6-a. UPDATE (verifier - CONTESTED FIELD, conservative value retained): firm_registration_tax=true rests on a SINGLE compiled rule sentence (Ac 302.05(a)) standing against THREE contrary primary sources - RSA 309-B:8, I(b); RSA 309-B:14, XVI; and the board's own firm application, whose registration-trigger list is exhaustive on its face and contains no non-attest trigger. Per the conservative-value rule the restrictive value is retained (a wrongly permissive answer is the dangerous one), but downstream consumers should treat this specific field as CONTESTED, not settled. Related unresolved conflict: Ac 303.05(c) requires that "The applicant CPA firm shall demonstrate, pursuant to RSA 309-B:8, I, that it has or will have a physical presence in NH by a date certain..." - a physical-presence condition sitting awkwardly against a no-office mobility regime. Cross-reference inventory corrected: the RSA 309-B:14 paragraphs carrying the 309-B:6 reference are I, II, III, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, XIII, XIV (NOT I-XIV; IV, V, XI and XII do not). Source-date discrepancy: Ac 400's effective date prints as 9-15-25 in the compiled Ac 100-500 file but as "September 14, 2025" on OPLC's Laws & Rules page; this record silently adopted the OPLC date. Currency caveat: a Board meeting was HELD 2026-06-29 and its minutes are not yet posted, so the 4/27/2026 minutes are the latest AVAILABLE record, not the latest record; and OPLC's Rev. 01/2026 Initial Application Checklist is newer than the Rev. 11/30/21 firm form yet still recites pre-amendment content.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: RSA 309-B:6-a, I (new, eff. 2026-04-22) grants an out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is outside NH the privilege to perform or offer services in NH (in person, mail, telephone, or electronic means) 'without notice to the board, the submission of any other documentation, or the payment of any fee' if the individual holds a valid, unrevoked license from another state/territory/DC AND 'satisfies the education, examination, and experience requirements of RSA 309-B:5'. That is an INDIVIDUAL-CRITERIA test measured against NH's own statutory requirements -- not NASBA/NQAS state-level substantial equivalency, whose defining paragraph (RSA 309-B:3, XVIII) was struck by the same act. Post-HB 1259, RSA 309-B:5, III accepts (a) a post-baccalaureate degree, (b) bachelor's + 30 additional credit hours, or (c) a bachelor's alone, with the experience requirement being 1 year for (a)/(b) and 2 years for (c). RSA 309-B:6-a, II grandfathers anyone who, as of 2026-04-22, held NH practice privileges 'pursuant to this state's substantial equivalency provisions'. RSA 309-B:6-a, III makes the privilege conditional on consent to board jurisdiction, compliance with RSA 309-B and board rules, cessation if the home license lapses, and appointment of the home board as agent for service. FIRM / ATTEST: RSA 309-B:8, I(a)(3) requires a permit for 'Any firm that does not have an office in this state but offers or renders attest services ... for a client having its home office in this state', UNLESS the firm (A) has the qualifications of paragraphs III and VIII (majority CPA ownership + peer review), (B) performs the services 'through an individual with practice privileges under RSA 309-B:6 and RSA 310:17', and (C) may lawfully do so in the privileged individual's home state. Because prong (B)'s predicate (309-B:6) has been repealed and the legislature did not repoint it to 309-B:6-a, this record treats a permit as REQUIRED (true) rather than assuming the exemption is currently operative. The board's live firm application reinforces that: 'This registration form is for In-State and Out-of-State firms. Your firm must register if ... The CPA firm provides attest services ... and compilation services ... for a client having its home office in New Hampshire'. Note NH sweeps COMPILATIONS in alongside attest at the board/rule level (Ac 302.05(b), Ac 302.06 use 'assurance services or compilation services'), even though the statutory out-of-state trigger in 309-B:8, I(a)(3) names attest only. FIRM / TAX & OTHER NON-ATTEST: recorded conservatively as true because of a live statute-vs-rule conflict. RSA 309-B:8, I(b) and RSA 309-B:14, XVI would permit a firm with no NH office to perform other professional services under the CPA title without a permit if done through a privileged individual and lawful at home; but the current compiled rule Ac 302.05(a) states flatly that 'A CPA firm permit to practice is required for all CPA firms wishing to do business in NH.' Per the conservative-value rule, true. PEER REVIEW: yes, and in two ways -- (i) as a permit condition (RSA 309-B:8, VIII; Ac 405.02(a) requires any firm providing audits, reviews, compilations or agreed-upon procedures to the public to enroll in a peer review program; Ac 302.05(b)(4)-(5) and Ac 303.05(g)-(h) require the peer review affidavit and most recent acceptance letter with the permit application; board form: 'Your Permit to Practice will not be considered for approval without this form'), and (ii) as a condition of the statutory no-permit attest exemption for out-of-state firms (RSA 309-B:8, I(a)(3)(A) incorporates paragraph VIII). Also note Ac 303.05(e) demands that a simple majority of firm ownership 'belongs to those who are certified in NH', which is stricter than RSA 309-B:8, III(a) ('licensed in some state of the United States') -- another rule/statute divergence affecting out-of-state firms. REGULATOR: the Board of Accountancy sits inside the NH Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC); the board page lists 'Certified Public Accountant, Domestic Firm Permit, Foreign Firm Permit' as the credentials it regulates. Firm permit fee is $66 per Plc 1002.01 (OPLC fee-correction notice), superseding the $60 printed on the form.
