records.data_gap_note: Board publishes no substantive mobility guidance page (FAQ silent on out-of-state practice); official compiled N.J.A.C. is only on the OAL/LexisNexis JS platform, so rule text was verified via the LII/Cornell mirror plus the board-hosted readoption notice (57 N.J.R. 55(a)) confirming the chapter was readopted without amendment. Firm-attest scope nuance: rule 13:29-4.2(a) triggers registration only for audits/SSAE prospective-financial examinations/PCAOB engagements for clients with home offices in NJ, and 13:29-4.2(b) permits SSARS reviews/compilations without registration subject to peer review, while the statute's post-2019 'attest' definition (45:2B-44) also includes SSARS reviews -- conservative value recorded (registration required for attest). Amended 45:2B-50.1(d) ('through a firm which meets the requirements of subparagraph (c) ... or that is registered') is ambiguous on whether qualifying under (c) without completing registration suffices; conservative reading (registration required) recorded.
records.notes: Since 2026-02-19, NJ grants automatic individual practice privilege (CPA=CPA-style but with statutory individual criteria: any-state license + exam + 1 yr experience) with an express no-license/no-notice/no-fee clause (45:2B-50.1(a),(b)). Conditions: consent to board jurisdiction, compliance with NJ act/regs, cessation if home license lapses, home-state board as agent for service (50.1(c)). Grandfather: individuals licensed elsewhere before the act's effective date who then held NJ practice privileges keep them (50.1(f)). Firms: out-of-state firm offering/rendering ATTEST in NJ must register (45:2B-54(a)(1)(c)) and to register must meet simple-majority CPA ownership (54(b)(2)), the C.45:2B-67 peer review/Quality Enhancement Program qualifications, and lawful home-state attest practice; peer_review_required=true refers to these conditions on firm registration plus N.J.A.C. 13:29-5.4 enrollment for firms licensed with the Board performing attest/accounting engagements (and 13:29-4.2(b) requires peer review even for the no-registration SSARS review/compilation pathway). Non-attest services (tax, consulting, compilation) by an out-of-state firm need NO registration if lawful in home state and performed through practice-privilege individuals (45:2B-54(a)(2)). Practice-privilege individuals may perform attest only through a qualifying/registered firm (50.1(d); N.J.A.C. 13:29-4.1(b)). Same act added a bachelor's+2yr licensure pathway (45:2B-49/51) and rewrote reciprocal licensure (45:2B-53) to individual criteria.

records.citation: NMSA 1978 §§ 61-28B-26, 61-28B-11(B), 61-28B-13, as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 105 (HB 296), eff. Jan. 1, 2026; implementing rules NMAC 16.60.3.14 and 16.60.4.8(F)
records.flux_note: NM joined the 2025-26 wave: HB 296 (Laws 2025, ch. 105, signed 2025-04-08, House 61-0 / Senate 39-1) rewrote the Public Accountancy Act effective 2026-01-01 (explicit Section 9 effective-date clause, no supermajority contingency) — replaced the old 150-hour substantial-equivalency privilege in 61-28B-26 with a two-prong comparable-licensure/exam-based test, added a broad exam-only no-notice privilege in 61-28B-11(B), and added no-permit firm mobility for attest in 61-28B-13(C). The statutory changeover is PAST (in force since 2026-01-01). Still mid-flight: board rulemaking — a 2025-12-09 rule hearing proposed amendments to all five NMAC 16.60 parts, but as of 2026-07-31 the compiled NMAC at srca.nm.gov still shows pre-HB296 versions (16.60.3.14 last amended 12/12/2021, still framed on the repealed 'substantial equivalency' test). The stale rule does NOT state an opposite answer on any recorded field (its no-notice/no-fee and no-permit-attest-firm provisions agree with the new statute). Board FAQ is also stale/incomplete: it states a firm permit is required only 'if the firm has an office in New Mexico,' omitting the statute's default that a no-office firm rendering attest for a NM client needs a permit UNLESS it meets the 61-28B-13(C) conditions.
records.data_gap_note: Official compiled statute at nmonesource.com (NM Compilation Commission) not fetched — JS-heavy/anti-bot; law.justia.com returns 403 to plain fetchers. Statutory leg is the enrolled final act on the legislature's own site (clean enacted text, verified free of strike/bracket markup artifacts). firm_registration_attest=false is CONDITIONAL — see notes; a no-office firm that does not meet all 61-28B-13(C) conditions MUST obtain a permit.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: 61-28B-26(A) — out-of-state CPA (principal place of business not in NM) presumed to have met comparable licensure requirements and may exercise all practice privileges without a NM certificate if the CPA (1) is licensed by a state that requires the education+experience of 61-28B-8(D) (bachelor's+30hrs+1yr, bachelor's-with-concentration+2yrs, or master's+1yr — the new UAA-style pathways), or (2) holds a valid US-jurisdiction license issued on an exam-passing basis plus 8(D)-level education/experience. Separately, 61-28B-11(B) grants a privilege to perform services 'without notice to the board or being certified' to ANY US-jurisdiction CPA whose licensure required a qualifying exam — no education/experience condition — effectively near-CPA=CPA; hence equivalence_test=individual_criteria (no NASBA/NQAS state-level reliance anywhere in the new text). 26(B): no notice, fee or other submission may be required; 61-28B-27 fee schedule expressly excepts 11(B) privilege holders. Conditions of privilege (26(C)): consent to board jurisdiction/discipline, comply with Act and rules, cease attest if home license lapses, home board as agent for service of process. Privileged persons performing attest must meet 61-28B-11 requirements (26(D)). NMAC 16.60.3.14 (pre-HB296 but consistent): practice without notifying board or remitting fee; website practitioners must disclose principal state of licensure, license number and contact address, and must notify board within 30 days of disciplinary occurrences under 16.60.5.11 — event-driven, not a pre-practice notice. FIRMS: 61-28B-13(B) — permit required for (1) firm with NM office doing attest, (2) firm with NM office using CPA title, (3) firm WITHOUT a NM office that offers/renders attest for a NM client EXCEPT per Subsection C. 13(C) no-permit attest path (firm mobility): services through an exam-qualified US-licensed individual who consents to board discipline + simple-majority CPA ownership (13(H)(1)) + peer review compliance (13(L)). So firm_registration_attest=false ONLY for firms meeting all C conditions; otherwise a permit is required. 13(D): no-office firm may perform NONATTEST services using CPA title without permit if through a 26-privileged person and lawful in its principal-place state — firm_registration_tax=false. PEER REVIEW: true both ways — 13(L) makes peer review a condition of permit renewal, and 13(C)(3) makes meeting Subsection L a condition of the no-permit attest privilege; NMAC 16.60.4.8(F) requires unregistered attest firms to keep records of participation in a comparable compliance assurance program (16.60.4.10). SUNSET: the entire 1999 Public Accountancy Act is scheduled for repeal 2030-07-01 under NM's sunset scheme (routinely extended). Board FAQ mobility answer (exam + 1yr experience) roughly tracks but does not precisely restate the new statutory test — treat statute as controlling. UPDATE (verifier): the "no NASBA/NQAS state-level reliance anywhere in the new text" claim describes the STATUTE only - compiled NMAC 16.60.3.14(B), retained in the pending proposed amendments, still authorizes optional board reliance on NASBA/AICPA qualification appraisal. The October 2025 proposed-rule redlines (e.g. rld.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/16.060.0003-with-proposed-changes.pdf) belong on the DiffLab watch to catch adoption of the HB 296 implementing rules.

records.citation: N.Y. Educ. Law § 7406(2) (practice privilege); §§ 7408, 7410 (firm registration and peer review); 8 NYCRR 70.7
records.flux_note: Chapter 530 of the Laws of 2025 (S6891B), signed 2025-11-21 and effective 2026-11-21 ('This act shall take effect twelve months after it shall have become a law'), rewrites Educ. Law 7406(2): the current test - licensure by a state the Board of Regents has determined substantially equivalent, or individual qualifications verified by the department - is replaced by individual criteria: valid license in good standing, out-of-state principal place of business, completion of either of the professional education and experience requirements in 7404(1)(2)-(3), and passage of the written examination in 7404(1)(4). NY Senate OpenLegislation already displays both versions of 7406 side by side (pre- and post-2026-11-21) and they AGREE with the enacted bill text, so this is a clean enacted-but-not-yet-effective change, not a source contradiction. Chapter 530 also adds a bachelor's-degree + exam + 2-years-experience licensure pathway. UPDATE (verifier): implementing rulemaking has actively begun - the proposed Part 70 amendment implementing Chapter 530 was published in the State Register for a 60-day comment period, with anticipated adoption at the September 2026 Board of Regents meeting and effective date 2026-11-21 (per the July 29, 2026 NYS Board for Public Accountancy public meeting packet). 8 NYCRR 70.7 itself is not yet conformed.
records.data_gap_note: equivalence_test set to 'other' rather than 'nasba_state_level' because the codified regulation (8 NYCRR 70.7) references states recognized by 'a national professional accounting organization acceptable to the Department' plus an individual department-verification fallback - NASBA/NQAS is the de facto mechanism but is not named in the statute or regulation, so nasba_state_level could not be confirmed from primary sources. fee_required=false rests on NYSED's explicit statement plus the absence of any fee provision for the privilege in 7406(2)/70.7 (no affirmative 'no fee' clause in the statute itself; the 7408 FIRM registration fee amount was not verified and fee_required refers only to the individual privilege). The post-2026-11-21 statutory text was verified via the enrolled bill text (S6891B/Ch. 530) and the OpenLegislation future-version display; fetched excerpts contained ellipses, so exact punctuation of full paragraphs was not captured.
records.notes: Framework: out-of-state CPAs (principal place of business outside NY) practice under Educ. Law 7406(2) with no license, no notice, and no fee. EXCEPTION: a CPA with discipline, pending charges, or license denial within the preceding 7 years must notify the department on a prescribed form and receive written permission BEFORE practicing. Service-type split is statutory: services under 7401 subds. 1-2 (attest and compilation) may be performed only through a firm registered under 7408; services under 7401 subd. 3 (tax, advisory, other non-attest) may be performed through an out-of-state firm holding a valid license/registration/permit in another state with no NY registration. CAVEAT on firm_registration_tax=false: 7408 independently requires registration of any firm that uses 'CPA'/'CPA firm' (or 'PA') in its title - a non-attest out-of-state firm holding itself out under a CPA firm name in NY may still trigger title-based registration; no NYSED guidance found on this intersection. Peer review of attest services at least every 3 years (7410; first review within 18 months of initial attest service) is a condition of firm registration - 7408 lists failure to undergo peer review as a ground against registration, and NYSED requires peer review documents each time the firm registers. An out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is IN New York gets no privilege and must obtain a NY license. Privilege-holders are automatically subject to NYSED regulatory oversight as if NY-licensed. Note: prior hint referenced '7406-a' - no such section exists; the privilege is 7406(2).
records.home_state_substantially_equivalent_note: NASBA Legacy Pathway carve-out: an individual licensed here via the alternative post-2012 pathway is NOT eligible for mobility practice privileges in other substantially-equivalent states. This dataset has no way to know which pathway a given license came from, so this stays unverified rather than assumed true. Source: https://nasba.org/licensure/substantialequivalency/ (checked 2026-08-08).

records.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 93-10 (practice privileges); 21 NCAC 08M .0105(f) (peer review for out-of-state firms)
records.flux_note: No pending change to the mobility statute found. NC's 2025 pathway act (SB 321 / S.L. 2025-35, signed 2025-07-01) amended ONLY G.S. 93-12(5) (adds bachelor's + 2 years supervised experience licensure pathway); its own text reads 'SECTION 2. This act becomes effective January 1, 2026.' — an unconditional date, no supermajority/immediate-effect option — and it is already effective. It did NOT amend G.S. 93-10; the compiled 93-10 history line ends with 2009-347 and the Board's mobility page matches the statute (no stale-page disagreement). 21 NCAC 08M .0105 shows 'Readopted Eff. June 1, 2026' with substance unchanged on the out-of-state-firm peer review point.
records.data_gap_note: A search-engine summary claimed a 2025 'SB 160' with CPA mobility provisions stalled in the NC House and may be reintroduced in 2026; this could not be substantiated on ncleg.gov and is treated as unverified noise. Also note an edge case: the no-fee firm notice under 93-10(c)(3) covers SAS audits, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and PCAOB engagements — SSARS reviews/compilations are NOT on the notice list, while the peer-review rule 08M .0105(f) keys off the same (c)(3) list; whether 08M .0105(a) independently reaches an out-of-state firm doing only SSARS reviews for NC clients is not explicitly resolved in the sources.
records.notes: NC is an automatic-mobility state (since S.L. 2009-347). Individuals: G.S. 93-10(a) grants out-of-state CPAs (principal place of business outside NC) the privilege to practice in NC 'without notice to the Board, the submission of any other documentation, or the payment of any fee' if they (1) hold a valid unrevoked CPA certificate from another US jurisdiction, (2) hold a valid unrevoked license/permit, (3) passed the Uniform CPA Examination, and (4) have no felony or dishonesty/deceit/fraud conviction (unless home jurisdiction determined no effect on license). No substantial-equivalency test — the former equivalency conditions (a)(5),(6) were repealed in 2009 — hence equivalence_test='other' (open CPA=CPA-style with good-standing/exam/no-felony conditions). Firms: G.S. 93-10(c) grants out-of-state firms with no NC office the same privilege for ALL services (attest and non-attest/tax) without registration, documentation, or fee; the only obligation is a NO-FEE notice to the Board ('Notice of Intent to Practice' per the Board) before/when performing (c)(3) services: a. financial statement audits (SAS), b. examinations of prospective financial information (SSAE), c. PCAOB-standard engagements. So firm_registration_attest=false (no registration/permit — but the no-fee (c)(3) notice IS required for those engagements) and firm_registration_tax=false (nothing at all for tax/non-attest). Peer review: TRUE as a condition of the no-registration attest privilege (not of any registration — none exists): 21 NCAC 08M .0105(f) requires a CPA firm without NC offices that provided G.S. 93-10(c)(3) services to NC clients to enroll in a peer review program (AICPA Peer Review Program or substantially compliant program per .0105(d)). Both privileges carry deemed consent to NC law and Board jurisdiction (93-10(b),(c)(1)-(2)). S.L. 2025-35 (eff. 2026-01-01) changed NC's own licensure pathways only — inbound mobility is unaffected.

records.citation: N.D. Cent. Code ch. 43-02.2, §§ 43-02.2-04.1 (substantial equivalency / practice privilege) and 43-02.2-06 (permits to practice - firms); N.D. Admin. Code ch. 3-01-03 (firm review) and 3-02-02 (fees)
records.data_gap_note: Two residual ambiguities could not be resolved from primary sources, neither of which changes the recorded values but both of which a compliance product should surface: (1) N.D. Admin. Code 3-02-02-04 still contains the sentence 'Individuals registered under the substantial equivalency provisions shall be required to file an annual renewal form and pay the annual renewal fee, plus the late filing fee if applicable.' This is a conditional obligation on individuals who ARE registered (i.e., who took the board's Substantial Equivalency Application route and hold an ND certificate); it does not on its face require an unregistered out-of-state CPA to register, and NDCC 43-02.2-04.1(2) opens with 'Notwithstanding any other provision of law ... no notice, fee, or other submission shall be provided by any such individual,' which by its terms overrides. No board page or rule was found requiring a practice-privilege holder to file or pay anything. (2) N.D. Admin. Code 3-01-03-03 says 'Firms practicing public accounting are required to undergo a practice review' without expressly limiting it to ND permit holders; whether the board applies it to an out-of-state firm operating in ND without a permit under NDCC 43-02.2-06(1)(b) is not addressed in any primary source located.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: NDCC 43-02.2-04.1(1) is the classic UAA sec. 23 substantial-equivalency practice privilege - an individual whose principal place of business is not in ND has all privileges of ND certificate holders with no ND certificate or permit, based on holding a CPA license from a state that NASBA's National Qualification Appraisal Service has VERIFIED to be substantially equivalent (state-level test), with a fallback where the individual obtains individual NQAS verification. Because the primary trigger is the NASBA/NQAS state-level determination, equivalence_test = nasba_state_level; ND has NOT moved to an individual-criteria or open CPA=CPA test. Subsection (2) expressly states 'no notice, fee, or other submission shall be provided' -> notice_required = false, fee_required = false. Conditions attach instead through automatic consent under subsection (3) (ND jurisdiction, compliance with chapter and board rules, cessation if home license lapses, appointment of home board as agent for service). N.D. Admin. Code 3-03-01-04 also provides that nonresident accountants practicing public accountancy in ND must meet the public-practice CPE requirements of their home jurisdiction - a substantive condition, not a filing or fee. FIRMS: ND's firm-permit trigger is OFFICE-BASED ONLY, not attest-based. NDCC 43-02.2-06(1)(a) requires a permit only for a firm 'with an office in this state' that practices public accountancy or uses CPA/LPA titles. NDCC 43-02.2-06(1)(b) lets any firm without an ND office perform professional services within the practice of public accountancy and use the CPA/CPA-firm title in ND with NO permit, provided (i) it performs those services through an individual with ND practice privileges under 43-02.2-04.1(1) and (ii) it can lawfully do so in that individual's principal-place-of-business state. NDCC 43-02.2-12(1) and (3) confirm the exemption by referring to firms 'otherwise exempt from the firm permit requirement' and by cross-referencing 43-02.2-06(1)(b). ND therefore does NOT have the UAA sec. 7(a)(1) attest trigger that most states use, so firm_registration_attest = false as well as firm_registration_tax = false - both rest on the same office-based test, and neither was inferred from the other. Note that under the 43-02.2-02(8) definition, tax-return preparation IS 'practice of public accountancy' when provided by a CPA/LPA firm, so tax work is squarely inside 43-02.2-06(1)(b)'s no-permit exemption rather than outside the statute. PEER REVIEW: recorded true, and it is a condition of the FIRM PERMIT, not of the no-permit out-of-state privilege. NDCC 43-02.2-06(7) authorizes the board to require practice reviews no more often than every three years 'as a condition to renewal of permits under this section'; the board implemented that in N.D. Admin. Code 3-01-03-03 (Law Implemented: NDCC 43-02.2-06), and the board's Firms page ties it to attest work ('audits, reviews and compilations') on a three-year cycle. A firm with no ND office that holds no ND permit has no ND permit to renew; see data_gap_note. 2025-26 WAVE: North Dakota is an outlier - it did NOT change its mobility or pathway law. The only 2025 accountancy enactment was HB 1156 (69th Legislative Assembly, ch. 381), which created NDCC 43-02.2-06.1 and amended 43-02.2-06(3) to permit firm ownership by a qualified plan/ESOP; passed 91-0 House and 47-0 Senate, signed and filed 2025-03-24, NO emergency clause, so effective 2025-08-01 under NDCC 1-02-13, and already reflected in the compiled code. It has no mobility or pathway content. The board's 2025 rule package (effective 2026-01-01) likewise touched only firm ownership (3-01-03-02) and retired/inactive status (3-02-02-05) - no mobility, no education pathway. The official 2025 'NDCC Sections Affected by Bill' table shows only 43-02.2-06(3) and 43-02.2-06.1 touched in chapter 43-02.2. ND's legislature is biennial (odd years) and the 69th Assembly has adjourned; there is no 2026 regular session, and no pending board rulemaking on mobility was found. Secondary reporting (lead only, not relied on) says ND intends to draft pathway legislation for the 2027 session; that is not introduced legislation, so rule_in_flux is false as of 2026-07-31 - but ND is a high-probability 2027 changer and should be re-checked when the 70th Assembly convenes in January 2027.

records.citation: 4 CMC §§ 3401-3440 (Accountancy Act of 2002, PL 13-52), esp. 4 CMC § 3401 (definitions), § 3422 (issuance/renewal of certificates), § 3423 (firm permits to practice); NMIAC §§ 1-10-801 (interstate practice), 1-10-2301 to 1-10-2310 (substantial equivalency/notification), 1-10-1605 (fees)
records.flux_note: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (not a pending legislative change). The CNMI's codified statute contains NO practice-privilege / substantial-equivalency mobility provision at all. The full text of PL 13-52 (Accountancy Act of 2002) was read section-by-section (Sections 1-24): Section 6 (codified 4 CMC § 3422) is titled 'Issuance and Renewal of Certificates' and provides only certificate-by-RECIPROCITY (the applicant applies for and is issued a CNMI certificate); Section 7 (codified 4 CMC § 3423) is firm permits. No section of the Act grants a practice privilege. HOWEVER, the Board's compiled administrative rules repeatedly presuppose a statutory substantial-equivalency standard that does not exist: NMIAC § 1-10-801(a)(2)(i) tells out-of-state individuals they may render services 'pursuant to: (i) Substantial equivalence (see section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422])', NMIAC § 1-10-801(b) refers to 'the substantial equivalency standard set out in the Act, section 6 [4 CMC § 3422]', and NMIAC § 1-10-801(c)(3)-(4) requires notice/consent 'as required for substantially equivalent practitioners under section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422]'. 4 CMC § 3422 as codified by the CNMI Law Revision Commission contains no such standard. The rules appear to have been drafted from the 2004+ UAA model against a statute that was never amended to match. This markup/contradiction was checked: the codified § 3422 (Source: PL 13-52, § 6, modified) and the original enrolled PL 13-52 Section 6 were compared line-by-line and AGREE with each other — so this is not a lost-strikethrough artifact; it is a genuine statute-vs-compiled-rule conflict. Conservative values recorded throughout: privilege treated as existing but conditioned on notice AND fee AND discretionary Board authorization; firm permit required for both attest and tax. No 2025-26 licensure/mobility wave legislation or rulemaking was found for CNMI — the Commonwealth Register is current through Vol. 48 (July 2026) with no Board of Accountancy entries, and the accountancy rules are still the 2007-adopted set as compiled in 2016. UPDATE (verifier - individual_practice_privilege REFUTED true -> set null): NO STATUTE GRANTS A PRACTICE PRIVILEGE. Full-text search of the enrolled PL 13-52 AND the codified 4 CMC 3401/3422/3423 (both downloaded and text-extracted) returns ZERO hits for "substantial equivalen", "practice privilege", or "principal place of business". Codified 4 CMC 3422 is captioned "Issuance and Renewal of Certificates" and 3422(c) provides only that "The Board shall issue a certificate to a holder of a certificate, license, or permit issued by another state upon a showing that:" - that is RECIPROCITY (get a CNMI certificate), not mobility. The sole basis for any privilege is a DISCRETIONARY board rule, NMIAC 1-10-801(c): "the Board MAY authorize the individual to exercise practice privileges in the CNMI provided the individual meets each of the following requirements" - permission on application, not an as-of-right privilege - and it rests on a thin statutory hook. The statute cuts the other way: 4 CMC 3422(a) provides "The holder of a certificate issued under this section may only practice public accountancy in a firm that holds a permit issued under section 3423 of this Act." A permissive true would tell a CPA a privilege exists where the profession's own authority treats CNMI as a non-mobility jurisdiction. null (not_verified) is the honest value: apply to the Board. No CNMI mobility legislation since (Commonwealth Register current through Vol. 48, July 2026, no Board of Accountancy entries; latest public laws PL 24-33/34/35 July 2026, none accountancy).
records.flux_summary: CNMI's actual law contains no practice-privilege provision at all -- it only lets a CPA apply for a CNMI certificate directly (reciprocity, not mobility). The Board's own compiled rules, though, repeatedly refer to a 'substantial equivalency' standard as if the law contains one. It doesn't. Because the law itself grants no privilege, we're not treating the Board's rules as if they override it. Confirm directly with the CNMI Board before relying on this.
records.data_gap_note: DUAL-SOURCE COULD NOT BE MET — the (a) board-page leg does not exist. The CNMI Board of Accountancy (also called Board of Public Accountancy) HAS NO WEBSITE. Searched: general web search for 'CNMI Board of Accountancy website'; commerce.gov.mp (CNMI Dept. of Commerce) including its /about-us/affiliates page, which lists affiliated agencies (e.g. Commonwealth Development Authority, Dept. of Finance) but does NOT list the Board of Accountancy; registrar.cnmi.gov; and NASBA's CNMI page. NASBA's jurisdiction page (lead only, not cited) confirms the Board has not established a website and that licensing is administered centrally through NASBA Licensing Services (PO Box 198589, Nashville TN); the Board is also currently not accepting Uniform CPA Examination applications, so candidates sit in another jurisdiction and apply for a Transfer of Grades certificate. Because no board page exists, source_url is null and confidence is capped at 'single_source' — NOT 'unverified', because the codified primary law WAS located and fully read on the official government publisher: the CNMI Law Revision Commission (cnmilaw.org), which publishes both the Commonwealth Code and the NMI Administrative Code. Retrieved and text-extracted in full: 4 CMC § 3401, § 3422, § 3423 (per-section PDFs) and NMIAC Title 1 Chapter 10 (Board of Accountancy, 50pp, © 2016 Commonwealth Law Revision Commission), plus the enrolled PL 13-52 PDF. All cnmilaw.org section PDFs return FlateDecode-compressed streams that defeat naive fetching — they required local pdftotext extraction; a plain fetch yields only PDF structural metadata. Remaining gap: no board-published interpretation, no application forms, no fee resolution adopted 'by resolution' under NMIAC § 1-10-1601 (the § 1-10-1605 amounts are the codified 'initially in effect' schedule and may have been superseded by an unpublished Board resolution). UPDATE (verifier - DiffLab/source migration, CONFIRMED not speculative): cnmilaw.org is scheduled for decommissioning around 2026-08-10 per the Commission's own banner, and the successor cnmilaw.gov DOES NOT PRESERVE PATHS - /pdf/cmc_section/, /pdf/admincode/ and all *.php legacy paths 404 rather than redirect, and the successor serves opaque numeric IDs instead (4 CMC 3422 = /commonwealth-code/3742, 4 CMC 3423 = /commonwealth-code/3743; the 4 CMC 3401 ID is likely nearby but MUST be confirmed, never guessed). citation_url has been switched to the cnmilaw.gov form; every cnmilaw.org URL anywhere in our dataset needs the same migration before 2026-08-10 or it will silently 404. cnmilaw.org is also intermittently unreachable already.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL PRACTICE PRIVILEGE (true, but qualified): the ONLY source granting it is the Board's compiled rule, NMIAC § 1-10-801(c), and it is DISCRETIONARY — 'the Board MAY authorize the individual to exercise practice privileges.' This is closer to a notice-and-fee registration regime than to no-notice CPA=CPA mobility. It is NOT open mobility. Conditions under § 1-10-801(c): (1) active CPA license in good standing issued by another state; (2) satisfaction of the 5-in-10 experience requirement of 4 CMC § 3422(c)(2)(C) — five years of practice outside the CNMI within the ten years immediately preceding; (3) notice to the Board; (4) consent to the terms/conditions of practice privileges. The 5-in-10 experience overlay is materially MORE restrictive than the UAA mobility model and is the key trap for practitioners assuming standard mobility. NOTICE (true): NMIAC Part 2300 § 1-10-2301 — notice is due immediately and must be RECEIVED within 28 days of accepting an engagement in the CNMI or of direct solicitation/marketing targeted at CNMI persons; notice renews on the Board's license-renewal cycle and must be amended within 28 days of a change of principal place of business or of any denial/revocation/suspension. Notice may be given on a Board form or electronically to a master notice list 'including the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service' — note this is a notice DELIVERY mechanism, not the equivalency test. Minimum reportable info (§ 1-10-2310): current address, telephone, fax, email, principal state of licensure and license number. SAFE HARBOR (§ 1-10-2305, non-reportable activities): a non-resident is NOT deemed to have entered the CNMI if contact is limited to teaching a college/CPE course, delivering a lecture, moderating a panel, and/or rendering services to the individual's own employer or fellow employees/affiliates (but not to the employer's clients). FEE (true): NMIAC § 1-10-1605(b) sets a distinct 'Substantial equivalency' licensure fee category alongside Active/Inactive/Foreign — initial $150, renewal $100, reinstatement $150, provisional $100 — and § 1-10-2301(c) ties notice renewal to the license renewal cycle, so the privilege is fee-bearing. Caveat: § 1-10-1601 lets the Board adopt fee schedules 'by resolution... from time to time', so amounts may be stale; the EXISTENCE of a fee is what is recorded. FIRM REGISTRATION — ATTEST (true): 4 CMC § 3423(a) is categorical: 'A firm must hold a permit issued under this section in order to practice public accountancy.' There is NO out-of-state firm exemption and NO firm-mobility provision anywhere in the Act or the rules — the CNMI never adopted the 2004+ UAA firm-mobility model. Reinforced by Act § 13(j): 'No holder of a certificate issued under Section 6 of this Act shall practice public accountancy in any firm that does not hold a valid permit issued under Section 7.' § 3423(c) additionally requires that every sole proprietor/partner/officer/shareholder/member/manager who regularly works in the CNMI hold a CNMI certificate, and that each OTHER partner/officer/etc. hold a certificate and be licensed in another state; § 3423(d) requires registering each CNMI office under the charge of a CNMI certificate holder. Firm permit fees (§ 1-10-1605(b)(5)): initial $250, renewal $200 annually, reinstatement $250, provisional $200. FIRM REGISTRATION — TAX (true, and NOT inferred from attest): this is established by the statute's OWN definition, not by analogy. 4 CMC § 3401(g) defines 'practice of public accountancy' to expressly include 'the preparation of tax returns or the furnishing of advice on tax matters', and § 3423(a) requires a permit to 'practice public accountancy'. Therefore a firm doing tax work in the CNMI needs the same permit. IMPORTANT LIMIT: the § 3401(g) definition is triggered only by 'a person or firm HOLDING ITSELF OUT TO THE PUBLIC AS A LICENSEE' — so a non-CPA tax preparer is outside the Act, but any out-of-state CPA firm presenting itself as such is inside it. PEER REVIEW (null — genuinely indeterminate, NOT 'not required'): both legs are permissive and agree with each other, so there is no statute/rule conflict here, just discretion. 4 CMC § 3423(g): the Board 'MAY by rule require' quality reviews no more often than once every three years as a condition of permit renewal; NMIAC § 1-10-710(a): the Board 'MAY require a licensee to undergo a peer review as a condition of renewed licensing.' A peer review apparatus plainly exists — § 1-10-715 exempts firms peer-reviewed within the preceding three years, § 1-10-720 states that a certificate holder issuing compilation reports outside a permitted firm 'MUST undergo a peer review', and § 1-10-725 mandates submission of adverse and second-consecutive-adverse/modified reports within 42 days — but no source establishes peer review as a blanket automatic condition of every firm permit, and no Board resolution exercising the § 1-10-710 discretion could be located. Recorded null per the honest-null discipline. EQUIVALENCE TEST (individual_criteria): recorded because NMIAC § 1-10-801(c) ENUMERATES criteria the individual must personally satisfy (active out-of-state license + 5-in-10 experience). It is expressly NOT NASBA state-level equivalency: the CNMI is not itself a NASBA-designated substantially-equivalent jurisdiction, and the rule's alternative 'Substantial equivalence' route points to a statutory standard (4 CMC § 3422) that does not exist, leaving § 1-10-801(c)'s individual criteria as the only operable path. The NASBA NQAS reference in § 1-10-2301(a)(2) is a notice-list channel only. DEFINITION TRAP — 'STATE': 4 CMC § 3401(k) defines 'State' as 'any State of the United States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam.' American Samoa is NOT included, and neither are other jurisdictions. Because § 1-10-801(c)(1) requires a license 'issued by another state', a CPA licensed ONLY in American Samoa appears NOT to qualify for the CNMI practice privilege. FOREIGN PRACTITIONERS: Act § 13(i) (unlawful acts) exempts foreign-credentialed accountants whose CNMI activities are limited to serving residents/entities of their own country and who issue no reports on CNMI persons' financial statements. UPDATE (verifier - factual correction): the claim that "the CNMI is not itself a NASBA-designated substantially-equivalent jurisdiction" is REFUTED by NASBA's Substantial Equivalency page (all 55 accountancy board jurisdictions are currently substantially equivalent). CNMI's own licensing standards ARE NASBA-designated substantially equivalent; what CNMI lacks is an INBOUND practice-privilege grant - a different thing entirely, and the distinction matters because it is the one a practitioner is most likely to get backwards.

records.citation: Ohio Rev. Code 4701.14(I) (individual practice privilege, as amended by H.B. 238, 135th G.A.); Ohio Rev. Code 4701.14(E) and 4701.04 (firm registration/peer review); Ohio Admin. Code 4701-13-02 (firm registration types)
records.flux_note: Changeover already completed. H.B. 238 (135th G.A.), signed 2025-01-08, rewrote ORC 4701.14(I) from a substantial-equivalency mobility test to automatic individual-criteria mobility; the legislature's official effective-date line reads 'Effective Date: April 9, 2025. Certain provisions effective 01/01/2026' -- the 01/01/2026 provisions are the ORC 4701.06 licensure-pathway changes (master's+1yr or bachelor's+2yr), now also in effect. Compiled code confirms 4701.14 version effective 2025-04-09. Subsequent housekeeping: H.B. 96 (136th G.A., budget) amended 4701.01/4701.04/4701.16 eff. 2025-09-30 (firm-structure clarifications); OAC 4701-13-02 re-adopted eff. 2025-09-01; OAC 4701-7-04/-06 eff. 2026-01-01. No pending mobility legislation or rulemaking found as of 2026-07-31; statute, rules, and board guidance do not conflict on the individual privilege.
records.data_gap_note: Out-of-state FIRMS are not expressly addressed by any Ohio primary source. The firm_registration_attest=true answer derives from ORC 4701.14(E) (attest report may not carry a firm's name 'unless the...business organization is a registered firm' -- location-neutral) plus OAC 4701-13-02(C) ('Any public accounting firm...that performs...attest report must...register with the board as a peer review firm'). But the registration mandate in ORC 4701.04(A) is textually limited to firms 'located in this state,' and board web guidance frames firm registration around 'Ohio-based' businesses; no source states how a firm with NO Ohio office registering for Ohio attest work is handled in practice. firm_registration_tax=false rests on 4701.04(A)'s located-in-this-state scope, the board's 'any Ohio-based business' framing, and OAC 4701-7-09 (which contemplates out-of-state firms serving Ohio clients electronically with only a website-contact duty) -- HOWEVER, OAC 4701-13-02(D) requires tax/consulting firm registration for any business that 'assumes or uses' CPA/PA titles, and whether that reaches a remote out-of-state firm using 'CPA' in its name is unresolved. Direct board confirmation recommended for both firm fields.
records.notes: Ohio moved early in the national wave: H.B. 238 (135th G.A.) replaced NASBA/NQAS substantial-equivalency mobility with automatic mobility on individual criteria, effective 2025-04-09. An individual whose principal place of business is not in Ohio has ALL privileges of an Ohio CPA certificate + permit (including attest) with no notice, no fee, and no application if the individual (a) holds a valid foreign certificate (defined in ORC 4701.01(R) to require good standing), (b) has a baccalaureate or higher degree, (c) completed an educational program with an accounting concentration, and (d) passed all parts of the CPA exam. Exercise of the privilege constitutes consent to board jurisdiction and appointment of the home-state board as service agent (4701.14(I)(2)). Test classified individual_criteria because the statute conditions the privilege on the four enumerated personal qualifications rather than a state-level equivalency determination -- though in practice it operates as near-CPA=CPA automatic mobility (OSCPA and the board's partners describe it as 'automatic interstate mobility'; virtually every licensed CPA meets the criteria). The old OAC substantial-equivalency rule (4701-7-02) survives but is now scoped to certificate-by-reciprocity under ORC 4701.06(J), not the practice privilege. Peer review: a condition of the FIRM registration, not of the individual privilege -- attest-performing firms must register as 'peer review firms' and undergo triennial peer review (ORC 4701.04(F), OAC 4701-13-02(C)); tax/consulting-only firms are exempt from peer review but must register if they use CPA/PA titles (OAC 4701-13-02(D)). Board FAQ and For Firms pages carry 2021 template dates and describe the practice privilege only generically (they never describe the new 4701.14(I) inbound criteria), but nothing on them contradicts the current statute.
records.home_state_substantially_equivalent_note: NASBA Legacy Pathway carve-out: an individual licensed here via the alternative post-2012 pathway is NOT eligible for mobility practice privileges in other substantially-equivalent states. This dataset has no way to know which pathway a given license came from, so this stays unverified rather than assumed true. Source: https://nasba.org/licensure/substantialequivalency/ (checked 2026-08-08).

records.citation: 59 O.S. § 15.12A (individual practice privilege; firm non-attest privilege at (A)(4)); 59 O.S. § 15.15(A)(3) and § 15.15C (out-of-state firm attest exemption); 59 O.S. § 15.30 (quality/peer review); as amended by Laws 2023, SB 172, c. 26 (eff. 2023-11-01) and Laws 2026, HB 4317, c. 186 (eff. 2026-11-01)
records.flux_note: HB 4317 (Laws 2026, c. 186) — Oklahoma's UAA 9th-edition rewrite — passed House 83-0 (2026-03-11) and Senate 44-0 (2026-04-29), Governor signed 2026-05-05 (bill history; OSCPA reported May 6). No emergency clause; enrolled act Section 5 states verbatim: 'This act shall become effective November 1, 2026.' It rewrites 59 O.S. 15.12A from the current substantial-equivalency scheme (NASBA-verified jurisdictions presumed equivalent, PLUS a catch-all presumption for licensees of non-verified jurisdictions) to an individual-criteria mobility model: any valid out-of-state CPA/PA license + passed Uniform CPA Exam + at initial licensure met one of three pathways (post-baccalaureate accounting degree + 1 yr experience; bachelor's + 30 extra hours + 1 yr; bachelor's with accounting concentration + 2 yrs). The no-notice/no-fee sentence and the firm non-attest privilege are retained in the new text. Both statute versions are published on OSCN (CiteID 552496 = operative until 2026-10-31; CiteID 385656 = text effective 2026-11-01). Board rulemaking for 2026 ('2026 Regulatory Text' PDF, image-only scan, content unverified) is pending and should be watched. UPDATE (verifier): HB 2736 (Laws 2025, c. 192, eff. 2025-11-01) also amended 59 O.S. 15.8/15.9 exam-eligibility education - prior-wave context, no field change. The 2026-11-01 version of 15.12A appends "Such an individual shall be subject to the requirements in paragraph 3 of this subsection" to the no-notice sentence - post-changeover, the no-notice privilege is expressly conditioned on paragraph-3 compliance. Open question on un-diffed 15.12A(A)(4) CLOSED: the current (2023) compiled text does contain the firm non-attest paragraph with the "without a firm license, permit, or notice to the Board" language (verifier confirmed on CiteID 552496).
records.data_gap_note: Peer-review condition (15.15(A)(3)(b) -> 15.30) is statute-sourced; the board FAQ confirms attest firm mobility but does not restate the peer-review condition, so that field is effectively single-source on the board leg. The 15.12A(A)(4) firm non-attest verbatim quote was captured from the OSCN page carrying the 2026-11-01 version; the operative 2023 text contains an equivalent paragraph (15.15C cross-references it) but was not character-diffed. OAC 10:15 admin rules reviewed via unofficial LII only; no contradiction found (10:15-21-1's 120-day reciprocal-application rule governs those establishing practice/employment in Oklahoma, not mobility practitioners).
records.notes: CURRENT LAW (operative until 2026-10-31, per SB 172 eff. 2023-11-01): (1) INDIVIDUALS — out-of-state CPAs/PAs whose principal place of business is NOT in Oklahoma get full practice privileges with NO notice, NO fee, NO submission, under BOTH prongs of 15.12A(A): licensees of NASBA-verified substantially-equivalent jurisdictions (para 1) AND licensees of non-verified jurisdictions (para 2) are each 'presumed to have qualifications substantially equivalent' — i.e., effectively open CPA=CPA mobility, hence equivalence_test='other' (hybrid: NASBA state-level verification framework with a universal catch-all; becomes true individual_criteria on 2026-11-01 under HB 4317). Privilege holders consent to Board jurisdiction and must cease practice if the home license lapses. CPAs who move their principal place of business INTO Oklahoma must obtain a reciprocal certificate/permit within 120 days (OAC 10:15-21-1; board FAQ). (2) FIRMS — firm registration/permit (15.15/15.15A) applies to firms with an OFFICE in Oklahoma. A firm with NO Oklahoma office: may perform NON-ATTEST services (tax, consulting, and 15.1A(12) compilation-type services) using the CPA/CPA-firm title with 'no firm license, permit, or notice to the Board' (15.12A(A)(4), 15.15C); may perform ATTEST services WITHOUT registration only if it (a) meets the CPA-majority-ownership qualifications of 15.15A(F)(1),(3), (b) complies with 15.30 peer/quality review, (c) performs through an individual with 15.12A practice privileges, and (d) can lawfully do so in its home state (15.15(A)(3)). Board FAQ confirms: full firm mobility since 2023-11-01 'even if the work being performed is attestation-related'; registration required only with a physical Oklahoma office. peer_review_required=true refers to this condition on the NO-registration attest privilege (and 15.30 also conditions permits for registered firms); it does not attach to non-attest-only practice. LIABILITY NOTE: firm_registration_attest=false is a CONDITIONED false — a firm failing any 15.15(A)(3) condition must register.

records.citation: ORS 673.153 (holders of licenses issued by other states); ORS 673.160 (registration of business organizations); ORS 673.455 (peer review); ORS 673.010(20) ("Substantially equivalent") -- all as amended by Or. Laws 2025 ch. 132 (SB 797), effective 2026-01-01; implementing rules OAR 801-005-0010, 801-010-0080, 801-010-0345, 801-050-0020 (BOA 1-2026, filed 01/29/2026, eff. 02/01/2026)
records.flux_note: Oregon is mid-wave and has multiple live moving parts. (1) STATUTORY CHANGEOVER ALREADY OPERATIVE: SB 797 (2025) = Or. Laws 2025 ch. 132 rewrote ORS 673.010(20), 673.153, 673.160 and 673.455. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED ON THE ACT ITSELF: the enrolled act runs SECTION 1 through SECTION 39 with NO effective-date section, NO operative-date section and NO emergency clause (verified by reading all 26 pages of the enrolled PDF, including pages 25-26; no '2026' string appears anywhere in the act). Oregon Const. Art. IV sec. 28 sets only a 90-day floor, but the operative default is statutory: ORS 171.022 -- 'an Act of the Legislative Assembly takes effect on January 1 of the year after passage.' 2025 regular session adjourned sine die 2025-06-27. Legislative Counsel's own ORS annotation confirms the date by printing the editorial gloss 'the effective date of this 2025 Act [January 1, 2026]' in the Note following ORS 673.410. Therefore rule_changes_on = 2026-01-01. No supermajority/immediate-effect analysis was needed because the act contains no such option. (2) BOARD RULE CHANGEOVER: BOA 1-2026, amend filed 01/29/2026, effective 02/01/2026, conformed OAR ch. 801 to SB 797. Materially, it DELETED the old mobility subsection (1) of OAR 801-010-0080 and retitled that rule 'Applications by Reciprocity' -- confirmed by the OSCPA comment published on the board's own past-rulemaking page ('The proposed draft removes subsection (1) but retains subsection (4) (renumbered as subsection (2))... the omission of subsection (1) eliminates explicit OAR language on mobility'). Net effect: individual mobility now rests on ORS 673.153 alone, with no implementing OAR. (3) OPEN RULEMAKING RIGHT NOW: the board's rulemaking page states rulemaking began June 4 with rule exposure 2026-07-01 and a public comment period running 2026-07-01 through 9:00 a.m. 2026-09-24. The exposed rule list is not published on that page, so it is unknown whether mobility/firm-registration rules are in scope. The same page also flags board/LRC policy work on private-equity ownership of CPA firms, which would touch ORS 673.160 firm requirements. (4) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON FIRM-REGISTRATION SCOPE: OAR 801-010-0345(3) requires out-of-state firms serving Oregon clients to register if they perform 'Attestation engagements' or PCAOB engagements. 'Attestation services' under ORS 673.010(1) and the board's own OAR 801-005-0010 definition includes SSARS reviews (para. (b)) and other SSAE examination/review/agreed-upon-procedures work (para. (d)). But ORS 673.160(1)(c) triggers registration ONLY for 673.010(1)(a) SAS audits, (c) SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and (e) PCAOB engagements, and ORS 673.160(3)(a) expressly EXEMPTS out-of-state firms doing 673.010(1)(b)/(d) work and compilations. The board's own peer-review web page follows the narrower statutory reading ('Out-of-state firms performing compilation and/or review services for Oregon clients are not required to register with the Board'). The compiled rule is therefore BROADER than the statute. Because both sources answer firm_registration_attest 'true', the conservative value is recorded either way; the disagreement affects only which engagement types trigger it, and the conservative (rule-based, broader) reading is described in notes. (5) STALE BOARD WEB GUIDANCE: the board's licensee-FAQ page and its License Application Requirements page still cite 'substantial equivalency as defined in ORS 673.010(21)' -- that is the PRE-2026 cross-reference that SB 797 sec. 12 struck out of ORS 673.153(1) and renumbered; the current definition sits at ORS 673.010(20) with new three-pathway criteria. OAR 801-010-0080's 'Statutes/Other Implemented' line still lists ORS 673.040, which SB 797 sec. 37 REPEALED. These are stale-citation defects, not substantive conflicts, but they show board guidance trailing the statute. UPDATE (verifier - rule_changes_on CLEARED to null, per the Puerto Rico precedent): the recorded 2026-01-01 is the SB 797 changeover, seven months in the past and fully in force - a forward-looking changeover field holding a past date reads to any consumer as "a change is coming" and would make downstream alerts fire on completed history. The completed changeover is recorded here instead; rule_in_flux stays TRUE because Board rulemaking implementing SB 797 is live with a decision point expected around late September 2026. SEPARATELY, correcting the researcher's timing gloss: SB 1510 is ALREADY EFFECTIVE (on or about 2026-06-05) and created the Registered Enrolled Agent credential - it is not a prospective 2027 tax-side change. The substantive conclusions are unchanged.
records.flux_summary: Oregon's mobility statute was rewritten by a 2025 law that took effect January 1, 2026, and the Board updated its own rules to match in February 2026. The Board also has open rulemaking underway right now (public comment through September 24, 2026) that could touch mobility again, and its statute and its rule disagree slightly on which services trigger firm registration -- we recorded the stricter reading. Confirm directly with the Oregon Board before relying on this.
records.data_gap_note: Per-field evidence legs are uneven and are stated here rather than averaged away. STRONG DUAL-SOURCE: firm_registration_attest and peer_review_required -- board's own peer-review page (oregon.gov/boa, fetched verbatim) PLUS codified ORS 673.160/673.455 (oregonlegislature.gov, fetched verbatim) PLUS codified OAR 801-010-0345 and 801-050-0020 (official Secretary of State OARD, fetched). GOOD: individual_practice_privilege and equivalence_test -- codified ORS 673.153/673.010(20) fetched verbatim, plus the board's License Application Requirements page which states the converse rule (an Oregon principal place of business requires an Oregon license) and recites the substantial-equivalency criteria. WEAKEST LEG -- READ THIS BEFORE RELYING: notice_required=false and fee_required=false rest on the codified statute ORS 673.153(2)(b) alone, corroborated only negatively by the fact that the current codified board rules contain no mobility notice/fee provision (the board deleted the old mobility subsection of OAR 801-010-0080 effective 2026-02-01). I could NOT obtain a board page affirmatively stating the no-notice/no-fee rule: the board's licensee-FAQ page (oregon.gov/boa/pages/frequently-asked-questions-for-licensees.aspx), which search-engine snippets show is the page that discusses mobility, returns HTTP 401 to every automated fetch attempted (curl with browser UA + cookie jar, PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, and WebFetch; multiple casings and query-string variants all 401). It therefore could not be quoted verbatim, and per those snippets it is stale anyway (still citing repealed/renumbered ORS 673.010(21)). Note also that OAR 801-010-0080(1) contains the sentence 'Reciprocity applicants must apply for an Oregon CPA license under this section within 60-days from the start date of Practicing Public Accountancy in Oregon.' That sentence sits inside a rule now titled 'Applications by Reciprocity' whose section (1) opens by addressing individuals who 'hold a valid CPA license in another state and wish to obtain' an Oregon license, and the board's License Application Requirements page scopes the same 60-day language to individuals establishing an Oregon principal place of business. Read that way it does not contradict ORS 673.153(2)(b). It is flagged here because a broader reading would impose a 60-day filing duty on mobility practitioners, and the rule's own authority line cites ORS 673.153. UPDATE (verifier): notice_required and fee_required are the weakest-supported fields in this record - their second leg is NEGATIVE-ONLY (absence of any fee/notice provision) and the Board's own mobility FAQ returns HTTP 401 (independently reproduced by the verifier), so no affirmative board statement corroborates them. Precision on the cited rule: the operative text is OAR 801-010-0080(1)(f) and the narrow reading is supported by the rule's preamble scoping - stronger than the researcher's wording ("OAR 801-010-0080(1) contains the sentence...") implies. Rulemaking-status wording corrected: the exposed rule list was NOT RETRIEVED (not "not published") - it can be pulled from the Secretary of State's Oregon Bulletin / OARD notice filings and from oregon.gov/BOA/Documents/, both of which do publish rule lists. WARNING FOR FUTURE REVIEWERS: oregon.public.law and similar mirrors still serve PRE-2026 ORS 673.153 text - do not let a later reviewer "correct" this record back to the repealed version.
records.notes: SUMMARY: Oregon grants broad, no-notice, no-fee individual practice privilege to out-of-state CPAs, and exempts out-of-state firms from registration for non-attest (including tax) work, but requires firm registration for the highest-assurance attest engagements. INDIVIDUAL: ORS 673.153(1) grants the privilege to a holder whose principal place of business is in another state who has an active CPA license, whose licensing state's requirements are 'substantially equivalent' to Oregon's, and who is in good standing. ORS 673.153(2)(a) gives that person all the rights and privileges of an Oregon licensee with no Oregon license required. ORS 673.153(2)(b) affirmatively PROHIBITS the board from requiring notice, an annual fee, or 'any other submission' as a condition of practicing -- this is a statutory command to the board, which is why notice_required and fee_required are recorded false. In exchange, ORS 673.153(3) deems consent to board jurisdiction, agreement to comply with ORS 673.010-673.465 and board rules, agreement to cease practice immediately if the home license goes invalid, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process; ORS 673.153(4) deems the same consents from the employing business organization (a sole proprietor counts as a business organization). IMPORTANT INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL CEILING: ORS 673.153(5) bars a mobility practitioner from performing SAS audits, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, or PCAOB engagements for a business organization whose HOME OFFICE is in Oregon unless that organization is registered under ORS 673.160. TWO BOARD-INTERPRETATION TRAPS from the board's License Application Requirements page: (i) 'An individual who wishes to establish a principal place of business in the State of Oregon is required to obtain an Oregon CPA license'; (ii) 'A licensee working remotely (outside of Oregon) for an Oregon firm is considered to have a principal place of business in Oregon and must be licensed in Oregon.' The remote-worker rule is aggressive and materially narrows mobility for out-of-state CPAs employed by Oregon firms -- it defeats the ORS 673.153(1) predicate (principal place of business in another state). FIRM, ATTEST: registration required. Statutory trigger, ORS 673.160(1)(c): a firm with no Oregon office must register if it performs the attestation services described in ORS 673.010(1)(a) (SAS audits), (c) (SSAE examinations of prospective financial information) or (e) (PCAOB engagements) for a client having an office in Oregon. Statutory carve-out, ORS 673.160(3)(a): a firm with no Oregon office may perform ORS 673.010(1)(b) SSARS reviews, (1)(d) other SSAE examination/review/AUP engagements, and compilation services -- and may use the CPA firm title -- WITHOUT registering, provided it meets the ORS 673.160(5) qualifications (majority licensed ownership, responsible Oregon-connected supervision, competency of the report signer) and performs the work through a person authorized under ORS 673.153. CONSERVATIVE PRACTICE WARNING: the compiled board rule OAR 801-010-0345(3) is broader, requiring out-of-state firms serving Oregon clients to register for any 'Attestation engagements' or PCAOB engagements; since 'attestation services' as defined in ORS 673.010(1) and OAR 801-005-0010 sweeps in reviews and other SSAE work, a firm relying on the ORS 673.160(3)(a) carve-out for review/SSAE work is exposed to a board rule that reads as requiring registration. Treat registration as the safe course for any engagement above compilation. Registration mechanics: two-year term, $265 statutory fee (ORS 673.160(8)), application must list all states where the firm is licensed and evidence the (5) qualifications; OAR 801-010-0345(3)(c) requires naming the ORS 673.150 licensee or ORS 673.153-authorized person responsible for supervising and signing attest reports; OAR 801-010-0345(6)(f) requires written notice to the board within 30 days if an out-of-state registered firm opens an Oregon office. FIRM, TAX/NON-ATTEST: no registration. ORS 673.160(3)(b) expressly lets a firm perform professional services in Oregon other than attestation or compilation services, using the CPA firm title, without registering, on two conditions: it performs the services through a person authorized under ORS 673.153, and it may lawfully perform those services in the state where that person's principal place of business is located. Tax-only out-of-state CPA firms therefore do not register. Separately verified that this is not undercut by Oregon's tax-preparer licensing scheme: ORS 673.610(4) exempts a CPA holding an active license issued by ANY state and a public accounting firm registered in ANY state from ORS 673.605-673.740, and SB 1510 (2026, = Or. Laws 2026 ch. 75, sec. 14) re-enacted that exemption unchanged (it only added enrolled agents and their employees as new exemptions (7) and (8)), so no new 2027 tax-side burden. PEER REVIEW -- BOTH A REGISTRATION CONDITION AND A FREESTANDING CONDITION ON THE NO-REGISTRATION PRIVILEGE, which is why this field needs care: (i) as a REGISTRATION/RENEWAL condition, ORS 673.160(9) requires renewal applicants to undergo peer review under ORS 673.455 unless they notify the board they are exempt because they perform no attestation or compilation services in Oregon, and OAR 801-010-0345(4)(c)(G) requires proof of peer-review enrollment with the application if the firm intends to perform attestation, review or compilation services; (ii) as a FREESTANDING condition independent of registration, ORS 673.455(2) reaches 'each business organization exempt from registration requirements under ORS 673.160 (3)' that performs attestation or compilation services, and also reaches 'each person authorized to practice public accountancy in this state under ORS 673.153' individually -- a mobility sole proprietor 'must meet peer review standards pertaining to business organizations.' So an out-of-state firm that lawfully skips registration because it only does reviews/compilations STILL owes peer review. The board's own peer-review page does not say this (it states only that such firms need not register), so the statute is the controlling source here. OAR 801-050-0020(1) likewise requires every firm performing attest or compilation services in Oregon or for Oregon clients to participate in an approved program; firms performing only bookkeeping or tax services may request exemption. Approved programs: AICPA (PRIMA) and the OSCPA-administered program; the reviewed party bears the cost (ORS 673.455(2)). EQUIVALENCE TEST -- coded 'other' deliberately, not inferred: ORS 673.010(20) is a state-specific hybrid, not a NASBA designation and not a pure individual test. Its primary prong is STATE-LEVEL -- it asks whether 'the other state requires the individual, as a condition of licensure,' to pass the Uniform CPA Examination and to satisfy one of four Oregon-enumerated pathways: (a)(A) 150 semester hours + baccalaureate or higher + 1 year verified experience; (a)(B) baccalaureate + 2 or more years verified experience; (a)(C) master's + 1 or more years verified experience; or (a)(D) requirements otherwise prescribed by the board. Its fallback prong (b) is INDIVIDUAL -- if the other state does not impose those requirements, the individual nonetheless qualifies if the individual personally has those qualifications. Oregon does not delegate the determination to NASBA in statute; the board's rule merely permits it to use NASBA/NQAS information when verifying, which is an evidentiary aid, not the legal test. Note the bachelor's+2 and master's+1 pathways are new in SB 797 and mirror the national 2025-26 wave; Oregon deliberately retained the 150-hour pathway to preserve outbound mobility for Oregon CPAs. VERIFICATION METHOD NOTE: the SB 797 enrolled act was compared line-by-line against the compiled ORS 2025 Edition text of ORS 673.153 and 673.160 and they match exactly. Oregon enrolled bills mark deleted text with square brackets rather than strikethrough formatting, so the deletion markup survives PDF text extraction intact -- the bracketed deleted phrase in sec. 12, '[the holder has a license from another state that is of substantial equivalency, as defined in ORS 673.010 (21)]', was correctly identified as the REPEALED pre-2026 test and not mistaken for live law. No false contradiction arose. Confirmed via the official Oregon Laws 2026 'ORS Sections Amended, Repealed or Added To' table that the 2026 regular session touched ONLY ORS 673.605, 673.610, 673.615, 673.625, 673.637 and 673.685 (all tax-practitioner sections, all via SB 1510 = ch. 75) and did NOT amend any section in the ORS 673.010-673.465 accountancy series -- so no 2026 statutory change to mobility. PRACTITIONER WARNING (verifier, promoted from mid-paragraph): an out-of-state firm performing SSARS reviews or non-prospective SSAE work for Oregon clients is REGISTRATION-EXEMPT under ORS 673.160(3)(a) but still owes peer review under ORS 673.455(2), and faces OAR 801-010-0345(3) on top - exemption from registration is not exemption from peer review.

records.notes: Regime: Act 27 of 2025 replaced NQAS substantial equivalency with 'automatic mobility' (CPA Law sec. 5.5, added June 30, 2025). INDIVIDUALS: an out-of-state CPA whose principal place of business is outside PA has all privileges/obligations of a PA licensee with no license, notice, filing, or fee (sec. 5.5(b)(8) expressly forbids the board from requiring notice or fee) IF the individual meets individual criteria: (i) bachelor's + 150 semester hours incl. accounting-related credits + exam + 1 year experience, OR (ii) bachelor's with accounting-related credits + exam + 2 years experience (sec. 5.5(b)(1)). Grandfather: sec. 5.5(b)(7) preserves privileges of out-of-state CPAs whose licenses were valid in PA as of the 2025-06-30 effective date. Note the sec. 2 definition of 'automatic mobility' reads like open CPA=CPA (actively licensed + good standing), but the operative sec. 5.5(b)(1) imposes the education/exam/experience criteria -- classified individual_criteria. FIRMS: 'firm' in PA law means a PA-licensed qualified association; an out-of-state firm with NO office in PA is a 'qualified unlicensed entity' (sec. 5.4(d)) and may practice public accounting in PA through sec.-5.5-qualified individuals or PA licensees with no license, notice, or fee (secs. 5.4(b), 5.5(b)(8), 8.8(a)(1)(ii), 12(c) exception). 'Public accounting' is defined to include BOTH attest activity and tax preparation/advice (sec. 2), so both firm_registration_attest and firm_registration_tax are false for out-of-state firms without a PA office. A firm that opens an office in PA ceases to be a qualified unlicensed entity and must obtain a firm license under sec. 8.8. PEER REVIEW: sec. 8.9 makes peer review a condition of a firm's initial/renewal PA LICENSE only; neither sec. 5.4 nor 5.5 conditions the mobility privilege on peer review, so it is not required for out-of-state firms practicing under mobility (false as to the privilege; true for PA-licensed firms). CE: sec. 8.2(d.1) (added by Act 27) lets those practicing under reciprocity or automatic mobility follow home-state CE (PA CE applies if home state has none). Separate paths exist for relocation: reciprocal certificate (sec. 5) and Act 41 of 2019 general endorsement -- distinct from the no-registration mobility privilege. No other pending 2025-26 PA mobility legislation found (SB 1183 concerns charitable audit thresholds, not the CPA Law).

records.flux_note: Ley Núm. 174-2025 (P. del S. 642), approved 2025-12-19 and certified by the Departamento de Estado on 2025-12-23, amends ONLY Sección 3 of Ley 293-1945 (the education/experience licensure pathways -- it adds the bachelor's + 2 years supervised experience route, i.e. Puerto Rico's participation in the 2025-26 national pathway wave). Its Artículo 4 (Vigencia) reads: 'El Artículo 3 de esta Ley comenzará a regir inmediatamente después de su aprobación y el resto de los Artículos comenzarán a regir a noventa (90) días después de su aprobación.' UPDATE (verifier - rule_changes_on CLEARED to null): the recorded 2026-03-19 changeover is CONSUMMATED HISTORY, not a pending change. Ley 174-2025 was approved 2025-12-19; its Articulo 4 reads verbatim "El Articulo 3 de esta Ley comenzara a regir inmediatamente despues de su aprobacion y el resto de los Articulos comenzaran a regir a noventa (90) dias despues de su aprobacion" (Departamento de Estado certified copy, "Certifico que es copia fiel y exacta del original", 23 de diciembre de 2025). 19 Dec + 90 days = 19 Mar 2026 - arithmetic correct, no supermajority condition to check - but that date is 4.5 months BEFORE this record's verified_date and the compiled text already carries the amendment (Rev. 29 May 2026 Sec. 3(e)(3) 120-hour bachelor's + two-years route and new Sec. 3(h) experience block, neither present in the pre-amendment codified Sec. 774). Pointing a forward-looking changeover field at a completed change would make downstream alerts fire on something that already happened. rule_in_flux stays TRUE on the pending Articulo 3 rulemaking.
records.flux_summary: A December 2025 law changed how CPAs qualify for licensure in Puerto Rico -- it did not touch the mobility rule itself. The Board is required to update its own regulations to match the new law but hasn't published anything yet, so we're watching for that regulation rather than reacting to a mobility change that's already happened. Confirm directly with the Puerto Rico Board before relying on this.
records.data_gap_note: Confidence is SINGLE_SOURCE, not dual_source, because the Board's own .gov pages do not publish any mobility content. Both the Spanish page (https://www.estado.pr.gov/juntas-examinadoras/contadores-publicos-autorizados) and the English mirror (https://www.statedepartment.pr.gov/juntas-examinadoras/certified-public-accountants) were fetched in full; they give only the Board's address, members, NASBA contact (the Board's Executive Administrator is a NASBA employee, ecolon@nasba.org), the 'Base Legal' line, three/four reglamentos (Ethics, Continuing Education, Reasonable Accommodation -- none about mobility, firms or peer review), and two notices. Nothing on the Board site addresses out-of-state practice privilege, notice, fees, out-of-state firm permits, substantial equivalency, or peer review. The only primary text answering these fields is the codified statute. That statute was obtained from bvirtualogp.pr.gov (Biblioteca Virtual of the PR Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto, a .pr.gov host), compiled version 'Rev. 29 de mayo de 2026', which carries the L.P.R.A. section numbers inline; OGP's own footer disclaims that it is 'una compilación oficial'. The 2025 amendment was independently verified against the official certified scan of the enrolled act at https://bvirtualogp.pr.gov/ogp/Bvirtual/leyesreferencia/PDF/2020/0174-2025.pdf ('Certifico que es copia fiel y exacta del original, Fecha: 23 DE DICIEMBRE DE 2025', Secretaria de Estado). An independent codified-code cross-check was attempted at law.justia.com/codes/puerto-rico/2020/titulo-20/capitulo-39/subcapitulo-i/775/ and /778/ -- both returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch and to curl with a browser User-Agent, so no second rendering of the L.P.R.A. text was obtainable; Justia is an unofficial publisher in any case. LexJuris (lexjuris.com) is a private mirror and was used only as a lead. firm_registration_tax is left NULL: 'Práctica de la Contabilidad Pública' is defined in Sec. 18(12) as ATTEST services only, so the Sec. 5 registration mandate literally reaches only attest; but the Board's own notice says broadly that 'entidades jurídicas de servicios profesionales' should obtain a license from the Junta, and Sec. 11(b)/(d) bar any unregistered firm from using the 'contadores públicos autorizados'/'C.P.A.'s' title. No primary source squarely answers whether an out-of-territory firm performing ONLY tax/non-attest work for Puerto Rico clients must register, and the tax rule must not be inferred from the attest rule. UPDATE (verifier - stated blocker was WRONG): the claim that "no second rendering of the L.P.R.A. text was obtainable" is REFUTED - law.justia.com/codes/puerto-rico/2020/titulo-20/capitulo-39/subcapitulo-i/775/, /778/ and /772/ all return HTTP 200 to a browser-UA fetch. CAVEAT that keeps record-level confidence at single_source: Justia's snapshot is the 2020 code, i.e. PRE-Ley-174-2025, so it validates Secciones 4/5/18 (untouched) but must NOT be used for Seccion 3 (amended). Also CLOSED: codified 20 L.P.R.A. Sec. 775(a)(3) reads "la sec. 772(12) de este titulo", proving the OGP "Seccion 19" reference is a compilation artifact and the enrolled law correctly points at the Seccion 18(12) attest definition - no substantive cross-reference conflict remains. IMPORTANT QUALIFIER on equivalence_test: "nasba_state_level" alone understates the test - Seccion 4(a)(1)(ii) ADDITIONALLY requires that the licensing jurisdiction "tenga reciprocidad con Puerto Rico", and NO roster of reciprocal jurisdictions is published, so a CPA cannot self-determine eligibility from public sources.
records.notes:
STRUCTURE: Puerto Rico DOES grant an individual practice privilege, in Sección 4(a)(1) (20 L.P.R.A. § 775), on the classic pre-2025 UAA model, and it is expressly a no-notice, no-registration privilege ('sin necesidad de registro o notificación a la Junta'). But PR layers TWO conditions most states do not: (1) Sec. 4(a)(1)(ii) requires that the licensing state/jurisdiction 'tenga reciprocidad con Puerto Rico' -- a reciprocity precondition ON TOP of substantial equivalency; and (2) Sec. 4(d) is a hard carve-out: every report issued in PR must be signed by a natural person licensed by the PR Board, and out-of-jurisdiction CPAs practicing under the privilege 'no podrán suscribir informes a menos que obtengan una licencia por reciprocidad expedida por la Junta de Contabilidad de Puerto Rico.' So the privilege exists but does NOT include signing reports. Practitioners should be warned prominently.

EQUIVALENCE_TEST = nasba_state_level: Sec. 4(a)(1)(iii) keys the privilege to a license from a jurisdiction that NASBA's National Qualification Appraisal Service has determined substantially equivalent to the UAA. Sec. 4(a)(1)(iv) supplies the standard individual fallback (a NASBA verification that the individual's own qualifications are substantially equivalent) -- that is the ordinary UAA two-track design, not a state-specific 'individual_criteria' scheme, so nasba_state_level is the correct primary classification. Sec. 18(15) separately defines 'equivalencia sustancial' as a determination by the Board or its designee. Grandfather: anyone who passed the Uniform CPA Exam and held a valid license from another US jurisdiction before 2000-01-01 is exempt from the Sec. 3(e) education requirement for purposes of Sec. 4.

CONDITIONS OF THE PRIVILEGE (Sec. 4(a)(2)): by exercising it, the individual and any firm employing them consent to the Board's jurisdiction and disciplinary authority, agree to comply with the Act and Board rules, agree to cease practice if the home-state license lapses, and appoint the home-state board as agent for service of process.

FIRMS -- attest = TRUE and unusually restrictive: Sec. 5 (§ 778) requires ANY firm or juridical person engaging in Puerto Rico in the 'práctica de la contabilidad pública' (defined at Sec. 18(12) as attest: SAS audits, SSARS reviews/compilations, SSAE engagements, PCAOB audits, plus other Board-adopted standards) to register with the Board as a CPA firm, and Sec. 6 (§ 779) then issues a 3-year license for a fee. Sec. 4(a)(3) reinforces this: a privileged individual performing Sec. 18(12) services for any entity headquartered ('con sede') in Puerto Rico may do so ONLY through a firm holding a Sec. 6 permit. There is NO UAA-style out-of-state firm mobility exemption in this Act. Worse for out-of-territory firms, Sec. 5(a)(1) requires at least one partner/member/owner/shareholder to be a PR-licensed CPA who is a bona fide Puerto Rico resident for US IRC purposes; Sec. 5(a)(2) requires every PR-resident accountant owner to be a PR CPA; Sec. 5(a)(3) requires anyone who personally signs reports in PR to be a PR CPA; and Sec. 5(a)(4) requires each resident manager of a PR office to be PR-licensed. Practical effect: a mainland firm generally cannot perform or sign attest work for PR clients without registering AND standing up a PR-resident PR-licensed CPA owner.

PEER REVIEW = FALSE: a full-text search of the compiled Act for 'pares', 'peer', 'revisión entre', 'control de calidad' and 'inspección de calidad' returns zero hits. Sec. 5(a) states firms 'deberá cumplir con los siguientes requisitos' and then gives a closed four-item list, none of which is peer review; Sec. 6(b) conditions renewal only on continuing education. The Board publishes no peer-review reglamento. (Lead only, not cited: the Colegio de CPA de PR states the Junta does not require quality-program membership for license renewal; AICPA/Yellow Book/COSSEC peer review obligations are separate and non-Board.)

INTERNAL DRAFTING DEFECTS IN THE COMPILED TEXT (worth surfacing to AssetLab, but they do not change any answer): Sec. 4(a)(3) cross-references 'el inciso (12) de la Sección 19' while the definitions are in Sección 18 and Sección 19 is the severability clause -- Sec. 14 and Sec. 3 both correctly cite 'el inciso (12) de la Sección 18', so this is a renumbering typo. Sec. 11(f)-(h) cite 'los incisos (11) y (12) de la Sección 18' where inciso (11) is 'Sede', probably intending (12) 'Práctica' and (13) 'Compilación'. Also, Sec. 6(a) says the Board issues licenses to 'toda persona o firma registrada bajo las Secciones 4, 5 y 6' -- read against the express 'sin necesidad de registro o notificación a la Junta' in Sec. 4(a)(1), the Sec. 4 registrants referred to are the foreign-country registrants of Sec. 4(c), not US substantially-equivalent privilege holders; this is why fee_required is recorded as false, but the tension is noted.

ADMINISTRATION: NASBA is the contracted administrator of PR CPA licensing and renewals (the Board's listed Executive Administrator is NASBA staff). A Board notice states NASBA is migrating to a new licensing system: last day to file in the current system 2026-07-11, no filings 2026-07-12 to 2026-08-02, new system opens 2026-08-03, and every PR CPA must create a new account. This is operational, not a rule change, but it will disrupt any reciprocity-license filings in that window.
