records.flux_note: Rhode Island rewrote its Public Accountancy Act in the 2026 session. Identical companion acts P.L. 2026 ch. 408 (H 8128) and ch. 409 (S 3076) were 'Enacted 06/23/2026' and each provides 'SECTION 2. This act shall take effect upon passage' -- i.e. the operative changeover date is 2026-06-23 (already past as of the 2026-07-31 verified_date). There is no supermajority/immediate-effect conditional clause to check; RI acts simply take effect on enactment. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (publication lag, not substantive conflict): the compiled R.I. General Laws on the legislature's statute site still display the PRE-2026 text -- https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE5/5-3.1/5-3.1-5.htm still shows the old 'Certified public accountants' section with the 150-hour rule and History ending at P.L. 2007, and https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE5/5-3.1/5-3.1-7.htm still shows the now-REPEALED subsection (g) 'Substantial equivalency' (NASBA-state-level test), while https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE5/5-3.1/5-3.1-9.htm still shows the old firm-permit text tied to firms that 'establish an office in this state'. The Board's own FAQ dated 2026-07-20 documents this lag: 'NOTE: It takes about 5 months for the Legislature to update the R.I. General Laws to reflect the changes made during the legislation session. The General Laws should be updated in November/December 2026. In the meantime, you can review the changes to the law here by reviewing 2026 Public Law Chapter 408.' The values recorded here follow the enacted, in-force public law, which the Board's own current pages confirm. Note the stale/compiled text is NOT more permissive on any recorded field except firm_registration_tax, where the old text (permit needed to use the title 'CPAs'/'CPA firm' generally) was arguably broader; the new § 5-3.1-9(c) express non-attest carve-out is the enacted and in-force rule and is what the Board publishes. Additionally, the Board's regulation 400-RICR-00-00-1 (last amended pre-2026) has not yet been conformed to the 2026 act -- it contains no mobility or firm-mobility provisions at all, so it does not contradict, but a conforming rulemaking is expected.
records.notes:
INDIVIDUAL: New R.I. Gen. Laws § 5-3.1-5(f)(1) grants practice privilege to a CPA holding a valid license in good standing from any state whose principal place of business is not RI, with 'no notice, fee, or other submission' required -- so notice_required=false and fee_required=false for entry/practice. CAVEAT (not a pre-practice notice): amended § 5-3.1-7(d) still requires 'any individual who has entered the state under the provisions of individual mobility practice privileges pursuant to § 5-3.1-5(f)' to notify the Board in writing within 30 days of the issuance/denial/revocation/suspension of any credential by another state or the commencement of a disciplinary or enforcement action -- an event-triggered reporting duty, not a registration or entry notice.

EQUIVALENCE TEST: individual_criteria. § 5-3.1-5(f)(1) conditions the privilege on the INDIVIDUAL: (i) at initial licensure the individual was required to show evidence of meeting one of RI's three statutory pathways in § 5-3.1-5(b) (post-bacc + 1 yr; bachelor's + 30 hrs + 1 yr; or bachelor's + 2 yrs), OR (ii) the individual held an active CPA license in good standing from any state as of December 31, 2024 and had RI practice privileges as of that date (grandfather). The repealed § 5-3.1-7(g) NASBA state-level substantial-equivalency test is gone. § 5-3.1-5(f)(5) permits (does not require) the Board to 'rely on the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service to determine which other jurisdictions licensees' or individuals may be eligible' -- NASBA is an administrative aid, not the legal test, so this is individual_criteria rather than nasba_state_level.

ATTEST BY OUT-OF-STATE FIRM: permit REQUIRED. § 5-3.1-9(b)(3) requires a permit of 'Any firm that does not have an office in this state but offers or renders attest or compilation services ... for clients in this state.' § 5-3.1-9(l)(5) reinforces it. Note RI sweeps COMPILATION services in with attest for this purpose. Also § 5-3.1-5(f)(4): an individual with mobility privileges may perform attest/compilation only through a firm meeting § 5-3.1-9.

TAX/NON-ATTEST BY OUT-OF-STATE FIRM: no permit, conditionally. § 5-3.1-9(c) lets a firm not caught by (b) perform non-attest and non-compilation services while using the 'CPA'/'CPA Firm' title without a permit ONLY IF (1) it works through an individual holding § 5-3.1-5(f) mobility privileges and (2) it may lawfully do so in its principal-place-of-business state. § 5-3.1-9(l) adds consent-to-jurisdiction conditions. So firm_registration_tax=false is conditional, not unconditional -- product copy should state the two conditions.

PEER REVIEW: it is a condition of the FIRM PRACTICE-UNIT PERMIT, specifically of RENEWAL, not of the no-registration non-attest privilege. § 5-3.1-9(h): 'All applicants for permit renewal shall satisfy the peer-review requirements prescribed in § 5-3.1-10.' § 5-3.1-10(a) directs the Board to require peer review 'as a condition to the renewal of permits for practice units under § 5-3.1-9' no more often than every 3 years. Board rule 400-RICR-00-00-1 § 1.9.1(B) restates this; § 1.9.1(E) exempts practice units that perform no accounting or auditing engagements (they certify that fact at renewal). The Board's FAQ says a firm permit application is incomplete without 'peer review documentation, if applicable', so initial applicants may also have to produce it -- see open_questions.

SCOPE NOTE: under § 5-3.1-3(13)/(17) and § 5-3.1-18, RI licensure/mobility is triggered by issuing REPORTS; pure bookkeeping, tax return preparation and tax advice may be offered without RI licensure or mobility. That statutory carve-out is independent of the firm-permit analysis above.

Board guidance is consistent with the statute, though the out-of-state firm form is dated 6/23 (pre-Act 34) — see notes. records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: Out-of-state CPAs with principal place of business outside SC get full practice privileges with no license, notice, fee, or submission (§ 40-2-245(A)-(C)). EQUIVALENCE TEST = 'other': since 2025-06-30 the test is effectively open CPA=CPA — passed exam + active license from ANY state + good standing; no NASBA state-level equivalency lookup and no individual education/experience evaluation (same shape as CA AB 1175). FIRMS: § 40-2-40(B)(3) makes registration the default trigger for a no-SC-office firm performing attest (§ 40-2-20(2)) or compilation (§ 40-2-20(6)) services for an SC client, UNLESS exempt under § 40-2-30(I). The § 40-2-30(I)(2) exemption (firm mobility, enacted 2022 Act 174) lets a qualifying firm perform attest without registration if it (a) meets § 40-2-40(C) ownership qualifications AND § 40-2-255(C) peer review, (b) works through an individual with § 40-2-245 privileges, and (c) can lawfully perform the services in the privileged individual's home state — so firm_registration_attest=false is CONDITIONAL: firms not meeting those conditions must register (board Form: Initial Out-of-State Firm Registration, $60 fee, peer-review report required). TAX/NON-ATTEST: § 40-2-30(I)(3) allows other professional services (incl. tax) with no registration, through privileged individuals lawful in their home state — firm_registration_tax=false. PEER REVIEW: conditions BOTH paths — it is a qualification for the no-registration attest privilege (§ 40-2-30(I)(2)(a) incorporating § 40-2-255(C)) and a renewal condition for registered firms; the board's out-of-state registration form demands proof of peer-review enrollment/report. CAUTION: whether the § 40-2-30(I)(2) exemption reaches compilation-only engagements (compilations are defined separately at § 40-2-20(6) and Act 34 added them to the § 40-2-40(B)(3) trigger) is unresolved — a compilation-only out-of-state firm should conservatively assume registration is required. Board's old URL llr.sc.gov/cpa/ is a 404; current board home is llr.sc.gov/acct/.

Amended by 2026 HB 1035 = SL 2026, ch 160 (eff. 2026-07-01).
records.flux_note: STARTING HINT WAS WRONG on the chapter: South Dakota accountancy law is SDCL ch. 36-20B (not 36-36/36-36A); rules are ARSD art. 20:75. South Dakota IS part of the 2025-26 wave. 2026 HB 1035 (Rep. Weisgram et al.), enacted as SL 2026, ch 160, rewrote SDCL 36-20B-66 and 36-20B-67 and took effect 2026-07-01 -- i.e. 30 days before this verification date. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED: the enrolled text of HB 1035 (mylrc doc 303860) contains NO emergency clause and NO effective-date section (zero hits for 'emergency' and 'effective' in the enrolled text), so the SDCL 2-14-16 default applies: an act passed at a regular session that does not prescribe when it takes effect 'takes effect on the first day of July after its passage.' Signed by the Governor 2026-03-02. Final-passage votes were House 67-0 (of 70 elected) and Senate 34-0 (of 35 elected) -- a supermajority WAS present in both chambers, so an emergency clause would have carried, but none was included; therefore the fallback date 2026-07-01 governs, not immediate effect. The SD Legislature does not publish a per-bill 'effective date' line, so the date is derived from SDCL 2-14-16 plus the absence of an emergency clause. PRE-2026 LAW: the old 36-20B-66 was the 2009 UAA substantial-equivalency provision; HB 1035 replaced the equivalency framing with explicit individual education/experience criteria and added the express 'no notice, fee, or other submission' sentence. 36-20B-67 now grandfathers anyone who exercised privileges under the pre-2026 section on or before 2024-12-31. PARALLEL BOARD RULEMAKING: the Board held a rules hearing 2026-04-30; those rules were filed as 52 SDR 125 and also took effect 2026-07-01 (visible in the source line of ARSD 20:75:03:15, which was retitled from 'Substantial equivalency and reciprocity' to 'Issuance of certificate to applicant licensed by another state' and had 'substantially equivalent' struck in favor of 'comparable'). Those rules touched education/experience/reciprocity, NOT the mobility or firm-permit rules. NO PRIMARY-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT FOUND: the board's mobility page has been updated and reproduces the new 36-20B-66 text verbatim, and no ARSD rule contradicts the statute. One residual stale artifact: the board mobility page still opens with the legacy sentence 'South Dakota is a substantially equivalent state.' and links to CPAmobility.org, which is inconsistent in framing with the statute's move away from an equivalency test; it does not contradict any field value. Flagged in flux because the changeover is only 30 days old, secondary/NASBA guidance is likely to lag, and the Board's 2026-08-12 meeting agenda was not yet posted as of this verification.
records.data_gap_note: TWO NUANCES THE BOOLEANS MASK. (1) firm_registration_attest=true is service-split, not blanket. SDCL 36-20B-2 defines 'attest' to include five categories, but only three of them trigger an out-of-state firm permit: 36-20B-32.1(3) requires a permit for a firm without a SD office only when it performs 36-20B-2(1) SAS audits, 36-20B-2(3) SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, or 36-20B-2(4) PCAOB engagements for a client residing in or home-officed in SD. SSARS reviews (36-20B-2(2)) and compilations (36-20B-1(5)) are expressly routed to 36-20B-32.2, which permits them WITHOUT a firm permit if the firm meets the 36-20B-33 and 36-20B-36 qualifications and works through an individual with practice privileges. 36-20B-2(5) other SSAE examinations/reviews/AUPs are named in neither 32.1(3) nor 32.2 and appear to fall to 36-20B-32.3 (no permit) -- that residual category is the least certain point in the whole record and a firm should not rely on it without board confirmation. (2) peer_review_required=true attaches by two different mechanisms: for the permit route it is a condition of firm-permit RENEWAL (ARSD 20:75:07:02) with peer-review program/date/results disclosed at initial application (ARSD 20:75:03:08(1)(f)); for the NO-permit compilation/SSARS-review route it is a statutory precondition of the privilege itself via 36-20B-32.2(1)'s cross-reference to 36-20B-36. The ARSD 20:75:07 rules are drafted around a 'permitted firm,' so the compliance mechanics for a non-permitted out-of-state firm relying on 36-20B-32.2 (who administers/accepts the review, what is filed with the SD board) are not spelled out in rule and remain unresolved.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: SDCL 36-20B-66 grants full practice privileges to a CPA whose principal place of business is outside SD and who holds a valid CPA certificate/license from any state, with NO notice, NO fee, and no other submission -- the statute says so in terms. It is NOT open CPA=CPA mobility: the individual must ALSO have passed the Uniform CPA Examination and individually hold one of three education/experience combinations (bachelor's + 2 yrs experience; bachelor's + 1 yr experience + 30 extra semester hours; or graduate degree + 1 yr experience), which is why equivalence_test is 'individual_criteria' rather than 'other'. Note the state-level NASBA/NQAS substantial-equivalency determination that the pre-2026 statute used was removed by HB 1035. Practitioners who were already exercising privileges under the old section on or before 2024-12-31 are separately grandfathered by 36-20B-67 and need not re-qualify under the new criteria. 'State' is defined in 36-20B-1(20) as the 50 states, DC, PR, USVI, Guam and CNMI -- foreign-licensed accountants are NOT covered by 36-20B-66. Exercising the privilege is an automatic consent to SD board personal and subject-matter jurisdiction, to compliance with ch. 36-20B and board rules, and to appointment of the home-state board as agent for service of process (36-20B-68); if the home-state license lapses the individual must cease practice in SD immediately. FIRM: an out-of-state firm needs a SD firm permit to perform SAS audits, SSAE prospective-financial-information examinations, or PCAOB engagements for SD-resident/SD-home-office clients (36-20B-32.1(3)); correspondingly, an individual with practice privileges may perform those same three service types for an SD-home-office entity only through a permitted firm (36-20B-70). Permit fee under ARSD 20:75:03:08 is $100 initial plus a per-owner/tiered scale ($75/owner for 1-9 owners, up to $3,000 for 100+ owners); the rule expressly prices 'each firm exercising practice privileges in this state required to hold a permit pursuant to SDCL subdivision 36-20B-32.1(3),' confirming out-of-state firms are in scope. Application is due within 90 days after commencing an engagement; permits expire annually on July 31. TAX/NON-ATTEST: no permit. 36-20B-32.3 lets an out-of-state firm perform 'other professional services' and even use the CPA-firm title without a SD permit, on two conditions -- the work is done through an individual with 36-20B-66/67 practice privileges, and the firm may lawfully do so in that individual's principal-place-of-business state. This is a real condition, not a pure exemption. Board mobility page corroborates by listing only audit/SSAE/PCAOB as the out-of-state firm permit trigger. TITLE TRAP: 36-20B-32.1(2) requires a permit for any firm WITH an office in this state that uses the CPA-firm title; an out-of-state firm that opens an SD office needs a permit for title use alone regardless of service mix.

Code Ann. §§ 62-1-108, 62-1-113; peer review: Tenn. Code Ann. § 62-1-201(b); Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0020-01-.11, 0020-01-.13, 0020-06-.04
records.flux_note: Statutory changeover already occurred: Pub. Ch. 524 § 38 (rewriting § 62-1-117 to automatic individual mobility with no notice/fee) took effect 2025-07-01 per § 65(c) of the act ('SECTIONS 1-31, 33, 34, and 36-64 of this act take effect on July 1, 2025'); the new licensure-pathway sections (§§ 32, 35: 150hr+1yr or 120hr+2yr) took effect 2026-01-01 per § 65(b). Residual flux: board rules Chapters 0020-01 through 0020-05 predate the act (0020-01 last revised May 2024) and the board voted in 2026 to open rulemaking to conform them to the Less is More Act plus a retrospective review; Chapter 0020-06 (peer review) was already amended effective 2025-09-28. Rule 0020-01-.13 (Interstate Practice) simply defers to § 62-1-117 for out-of-state individuals, so no statute-vs-rule contradiction exists on mobility. The current compiled § 62-1-117 lives on LexisNexis (the state's official code publisher, JS-gated advance.lexis.com) and could not be fetched directly; Justia's mirror still shows the superseded 2024 text (pre-2025-07-01), which is a staleness artifact, not a live conflict. records.notes: NEW MOBILITY TEST (eff. 2025-07-01): any individual with principal place of business outside TN who holds a valid CPA license in good standing from another state MUST be granted practice privileges if, at the time licensed, they showed evidence of passing the Uniform CPA Exam — an individual-level criterion (no NASBA/NQAS state-level equivalency determination remains in the statute; the old 'Reciprocity' section including substantial-equivalency verification was deleted wholesale). Functionally this is near-automatic CPA=CPA mobility; the only screens are good standing and exam passage. Conditions (117(b)): the individual AND the employing CPA firm consent to board jurisdiction, compliance with TN law/rules, cessation if home license lapses, and service-of-process agency. FIRMS: Pub. Ch. 524 added no firm mobility provision. § 62-1-108(a): 'A firm must hold a permit issued under this section in order to provide attest services or to use the title CPAs/CPA firm/PAs/PA firm' — so an out-of-state firm performing ATTEST for TN clients needs a TN firm permit (board guidance: only CPAs operating within a licensed CPA firm can provide attest; initial firm permit fee $50, annual renewal $50, and board requires a Resident Manager holding an active TN CPA/PA license, which is burdensome for no-office firms). TAX/NON-ATTEST: no permit is required for the services themselves — § 62-1-113(a) expressly permits nonpermitted performance of tax return preparation, management advisory and similar services — BUT the permit obligation is also triggered by USE OF THE CPA/accounting TITLE in the firm name (§ 62-1-113(d); board: permit required for firms 'which use the terms Accountant, Accounting, or CPA in the name of the firm'), an unresolved edge for tax-only out-of-state firms holding out under a 'CPAs' name to TN clients. PEER REVIEW: condition of firm permit RENEWAL (§ 62-1-201(b); Rule 0020-06-.04(1)), 3-year cycle; and Rule 0020-06-.04(8) (amended eff. 2025-09-28) separately requires firms/individuals with NO TN office providing attest to TN clients to participate in an approved peer review program. A separate reciprocal-certificate route (§ 62-1-107(c), Rule 0020-01-.13, $100+$100 fees) exists only for those establishing a TN principal place of business — not required for mobility practice.

records.flux_note: SB 522 (89th Leg., 2025, Ch. 40) rewrote the individual mobility test effective 2025-09-01: it deleted the NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test from 901.462(a) and replaced it with individual criteria (passed uniform CPA exam + education pathway of (A) 150-hr baccalaureate w/ accounting concentration, (B) graduate degree w/ accounting concentration, or (C) baccalaureate w/ accounting concentration + experience of 1 year for pathways A/B or 2 years for pathway C, measured at time of home-state licensure). The enrolled SB 522 text and the compiled statute AGREE exactly - no enrolled-vs-compiled contradiction. However, the TSBPA's own practice-privilege page (fetched 2026-07-31) STILL describes the repealed pre-SB 522 NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency checklist - board page and statute currently DISAGREE on the equivalence test; the board page appears stale, not evidence of a pending change. 901.462(f) grandfathers individuals who on 2024-12-31 held an out-of-state license and practiced under the privilege. Firm-side rules (901.461 full firm mobility) unchanged since HB 1520 eff. 2019-09-01. UPDATE (verifier): the board HAS conformed its rules - 22 TAC 517.2 was amended to delete the NASBA NQAS reference and add no notice/fee/registration requirement (proposed 50 TexReg 4198, 2025-07-25; adopted without changes; filed with SOS 2025-09-19; effective 2025-10-09), and 22 TAC 501.53 (eff. 2025-04-02) requires privilege practitioners to comply with all Board rules of professional conduct. The legal test is therefore settled at BOTH statute and rule level; the only remaining disagreement is the stale TSBPA web page, so rule_in_flux=true is a conservative flag AssetLab may judge narrowable once the board page updates. Adjacent 2025 enactments (do not change any field): SB 262 adds a home-state licensure pathway operative 2026-08-01 (120-hr bachelor's + 2 yrs experience; TSBPA rules eff. 2025-10-10), which affects how pathway-C comparability under 901.462(a) is exercised by inbound CPAs; SB 522 § 1 also amended 901.259 (reciprocal certification, incl. NQAS verification route).

records.notes: Individuals: out-of-state CPA with ACTIVE license and principal place of business outside Texas may exercise all privileges of Texas license holders with no notice, no fee, no registration, if they meet the SB 522 individual criteria (exam + education pathway + 1-2 yrs experience). Privilege conditions: board jurisdiction, comply with Act and rules, home-state regulator deemed agent for service of process, must cease if home license invalid; board may bar an individual it determines does not meet 901.462(a) (901.462(e)). Firms: Texas has full firm mobility (HB 1520, 2019) - an out-of-state firm needs NO Texas firm license, registration, or notice for attest OR non-attest work performed by licensed/privileged individuals, UNLESS it establishes or maintains an office in Texas (901.351(a-1) then requires a firm license). Attest services (901.002(a)(1)) for an entity with its HOME OFFICE in Texas additionally require: 901.354(a)-(b) ownership compliance (CPA-majority), compliance with the board's peer review program (901.159), and performance by a Texas-licensed or privileged individual. peer_review_required=true refers to that condition on the no-license attest privilege - there is no registration/permit for it to attach to; board FAQ says compliance may be via the home-state peer review program.

records.notes:
MOBILITY IS OPEN AND NOTICE-FREE FOR INDIVIDUALS. 27 V.I.C. sec.250q(a)(1) grants an out-of-territory CPA whose principal place of business is not in the USVI 'all the privileges of permittees of this Territory without the need to obtain a permit under sections 250c or 250d', and expressly states that 'no notice or other submission must be provided by any such individual.' Because no permit and no submission are required, there is no fee -- fees under this chapter attach to permit applications (sec.250d(e): 'The Board shall charge a fee for each application for initial issuance or renewal of a permit under this section'). Privilege is conditioned on automatic consent to Board jurisdiction, compliance with the chapter and Board rules, cessation if the home-state license lapses, and appointment of the home-state board as agent for service (sec.250q(a)(2)(A)-(D)).

EQUIVALENCE TEST IS STATE-LEVEL NASBA ONLY. sec.250q(a)(1) keys entirely to 'any state that the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service has verified to be in substantial equivalence with the CPA licensure requirements of the AICPA/NASBA Uniform Accountancy Act.' The UAA's alternative INDIVIDUAL-qualification prong was NOT enacted into sec.250q -- there is no individual-criteria fallback for the practice privilege. (NQAS individual verification does appear at sec.250c(c)(2), but that governs issuance of a reciprocal CERTIFICATE to someone who establishes a principal place of business IN the Territory -- a different question. Do not read it into the privilege.) Hence equivalence_test = nasba_state_level. Practical consequence: a CPA licensed in a jurisdiction NOT NQAS-verified as substantially equivalent has no sec.250q privilege at all.

FIRM ATTEST PERMIT -- TRUE, BUT THE TRIGGER IS A NARROWED LIST. sec.250d(a)(1)(C) requires a permit for 'Any firm that does not have an office in the Territory but performs attest services described in Section 250 (b)(1), (3) or (4) of this chapter for a client having its home office in the Territory.' Cross-referencing the sec.250(b) definition: (b)(1) = SAS audits/engagements; (b)(3) = SSAE examinations of prospective financial information; (b)(4) = PCAOB-standard engagements. NOT in the mandatory list: (b)(2) SSARS reviews of financial statements, and (b)(5) other SSAE examinations/reviews/agreed-upon-procedures. sec.250q(a)(3) mirrors this from the individual side -- a privilege-holder performing those same three service types for a Territory-home-office entity 'may practice only through a firm that has obtained a permit issued under section 250d.'

THE MIDDLE TIER (REVIEWS AND COMPILATIONS) -- NO PERMIT BUT CONDITIONS ATTACH. sec.250d(a)(2): a firm with no Territory office may perform sec.250(b)(2) reviews or sec.250(f) compilations for a Territory-home-office client, and use the CPA/CPA-firm title, WITHOUT a permit, 'only if: (A) it has the qualifications described in subsections (c) and (h) of this section; and (B) it performs such services through an individual with practice privileges under Section 250q'. Subsection (h) is the PEER REVIEW subsection and subsection (c) is the CPA-ownership/competency subsection -- so peer review and majority-CPA ownership are conditions of the NO-REGISTRATION privilege here, not merely of a permit.

TAX AND OTHER NON-ATTEST -- NO FIRM PERMIT. sec.250d(a)(3): a firm not caught by (a)(1)(C) or (a)(2) 'may perform other professional services while using the title CPA or CPA firm in this Territory without a permit' if it works through a sec.250q privilege-holder and may lawfully do so in that individual's principal-place-of-business state. This is the classic UAA no-permit-for-tax carve-out. Verified from the statute directly; NOT inferred from the attest rule.

PEER REVIEW -- BOTH A PERMIT CONDITION AND A PRIVILEGE CONDITION. sec.250d(h) makes peer review (max once per three years) a condition 'to renewal of permits under this section', i.e. of the firm permit. Separately, as noted above, sec.250d(a)(2)(A) imports subsection (h) as a condition of the no-permit review/compilation privilege. So the answer is 'both', which is why peer_review_required is true on either framing. Individual privilege-holders doing only tax/consulting under sec.250d(a)(3) are not routed through (h). The Board's own page independently confirms: 'All CPA firms that issue attest or compilation reports shall be enrolled in a peer review program approved by the Board.'

RESIDENT AGENT. sec.250e requires a non-resident person or firm APPLYING for a certificate under sec.250c or a firm permit under sec.250d to appoint a resident agent for service of process. This attaches to the permit application, not to the sec.250q privilege.

EFFECTIVE DATE / NO 2025-26 WAVE CHANGE. Act 7596 sec.5: 'This Act shall take effect one year after enactment.' Passed by the Legislature 24 April 2014, signed by Governor John P. de Jongh, Jr. on 16 May 2014 (per the governor's approval page bearing the territorial seal), giving an operative date of approximately 16 May 2015. The USVI did NOT participate in the 2025-26 national licensure/mobility rewrite wave: the Legislature's bill tracker shows no accountancy bill in the 31st, 32nd, 33rd, 34th, 35th or 36th Legislatures, and no board rulemaking analogue to the NV/AR route was found. rule_in_flux is therefore false.

INTERNAL CROSS-REFERENCE DEFECTS IN THE ACT (flagged, not resolved). The enrolled act contains several dangling citations to sec.250q subsections that do not exist as enacted: the sec.250(h) 'Home office' definition points to 'section 250q(a)(4)'; sec.250d(c)(1) and sec.250d(c)(2)(A) both reference a firm 'that must have a permit pursuant to Section 250q (a) (4)' and a licensee 'who meets the requirements set out in Section 250q (a) (1) or in Section 250q (a) (2)'; and sec.250c(a) and sec.250c(c)(1) refer to 'the substantial equivalency standard set out in section 250q(a)(2)'. As enacted, sec.250q(a) has only paragraphs (1), (2) and (3), where (2) is the consent-to-jurisdiction clause and there is no (4). These are renumbering artifacts from the UAA model text. They do NOT affect any field above, all of which rest on unambiguous operative language in sec.250q(a)(1), sec.250q(a)(3), sec.250d(a)(1)(C), sec.250d(a)(2), sec.250d(a)(3) and sec.250d(h). Not treated as a source disagreement (it is one document internally inconsistent, not two sources stating opposite answers), so rule_in_flux remains false.

SCALE CONTEXT. The Board reports 'approximately 62 Certified Public Accountants (CPA) and approximately 26 CPA firms licensed in the US Virgin Islands' -- a very small jurisdiction; expect slow/thin administrative publishing.

UNRELATED TO MOBILITY (do not conflate): the Board requires a Virgin Islands Regulatory / local CPA examination for reciprocal LICENSURE by someone establishing a principal place of business in the Territory. That is a licensure requirement, not a practice-privilege requirement, and it does not attach to sec.250q mobility.

records.citation: Utah Code 58-26a-305 (exemptions from licensure / practice privilege, as amended by S.B. 15, Laws of Utah 2025, ch. 283, eff. 2026-07-01); Utah Code 58-26a-301(1)(b) and 58-26a-302(3) (firm registration, as amended by S.B. 117, 2026 G.S. (compiled as ch. 64), eff. 2026-07-01); Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-305 and R156-26a-303a (as amended by Filing No. 58008, eff. 2026-07-08)
records.flux_note: Utah is mid-changeover in the 2025-26 wave. S.B. 15 (Laws of Utah 2025, ch. 283) took effect 2026-07-01 via a flat special-effective-date clause ('This bill takes effect on July 1, 2026' -- no supermajority condition, so no vote-count analysis needed; it passed unanimously regardless). It deleted the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service substantial-equivalency test from 58-26a-305 and replaced it with: valid out-of-state license in good standing + evidence at time of licensure of passing qualifying examinations; the pre-existing no-notice/no-fee clause carried forward. DOPL's implementing rule amendment (Filing No. 58008, published Utah State Bulletin 2026-06-01, effective 2026-07-08 per Bulletin 2026-07-15) conformed R156-26a to S.B. 15 and S.B. 117 (2026). LIVE CONFLICT on the firm fields: amended statute 58-26a-305(1)(a) exempts only 'an individual', and 58-26a-301(1)(b) requires registration for any qualified business entity engaged in the practice of public accounting 'except as specifically provided in Section 58-26a-305 or 58-1-307' -- a strict statutory reading gives out-of-state FIRMS no exemption. But the just-amended rule R156-26a-305(3) (retained through the 2026-07-08 amendment) still grants FIRM MOBILITY: an out-of-state firm need not register if its principal place of business is not in Utah, it holds an active unrestricted home-jurisdiction firm license in good standing, and it meets Utah's ownership (58-26a-302(3)(a)(iii)) and peer-review (R156-26a-303a) requirements. Statute and compiled rule state opposite answers, so per the contradiction rule the CONSERVATIVE values are recorded (firm_registration_attest = true, firm_registration_tax = true), with the caveat that the board's own operative rule says qualifying firms are exempt. Watch for conforming legislation or further rulemaking.
records.data_gap_note: Firm-registration fields are recorded conservatively (true) because of the statute-vs-rule conflict described in flux_note -- DOPL's current rule would say a qualifying out-of-state firm (attest or tax) need NOT register. Also note the registration trigger is the 'practice of public accounting', defined as acting 'while holding oneself out as a certified public accountant'; it includes tax preparation/advice, so tax is NOT exempted by statute (do not read a non-attest carve-out into Utah law). The official current-rule page (adminrules.utah.gov) returns 404 to non-browser fetchers; codified rule text was verified via the official Utah State Bulletin PDFs (rules.utah.gov) and a utah.gov PMN copy instead. UPDATE (verifier): open-question correction - the 2026-06-01 Bulletin publication of Filing 58008 is captioned "NOTICE OF SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE", meaning an original proposed-amendment filing preceded it and was modified (the researcher's no-prior-filing statement is contradicted by the caption on the cited document). Also: the amended rule keys the initial-peer-review-report trigger to "Subsection 58-26a-102(16)" while the compiled statute defines "Report" at 102(20) - the rule's own cross-reference numbering is stale, further flux evidence.
records.notes: Individual mobility: Utah Code 58-26a-305(1)(a) + (2)(a) grants out-of-state CPAs full practice privilege with 'no notice, fee, or other submission' -- conditions are a valid license/permit in good standing from another state, evidence (at time of original licensure) of passing the equivalent qualifying examinations, and statutory consents (Utah jurisdiction/discipline, cease practice if home license becomes invalid, home board as agent for service of process). equivalence_test = 'other': since 2026-07-01 Utah applies no NASBA/substantial-equivalency screen; it is a near-CPA=CPA regime conditioned only on good standing + exam passage (before 2026-07-01 it was NASBA NQAS state-level or individual verification). Rule R156-26a-305(2) adds that a mobility CPA may only perform the same level of services (attest or non-attest) permitted in the home jurisdiction. Firm side: registration under 58-26a-302(3) requires simple-majority CPA ownership, a designated responsible Utah licensee, and separate registration per in-state location; peer review is a renewal condition (58-26a-303(2)(b); R156-26a-303a: firms practicing public accounting must undergo peer review at least every three years, scope commensurate with practice -- effectively reaching firms issuing attest/compilation reports per the 58-26a-102(14)/(20) definitions). Peer review is ALSO a condition of the rule's no-registration firm-mobility privilege (R156-26a-305(3)(c)) -- i.e., it conditions both the registration route and the exemption route. Board web guidance is thin (navigation hub only); the substantive board-side source is DOPL's own administrative rule and rulemaking filings.

records.citation: 26 V.S.A. §§ 74, 74c (§§ 13, 71a, 74c as amended by 2026 Vt. Acts & Resolves No. 119 (H.588), Secs. 8-10, eff. on passage June 8, 2026); 26 V.S.A. § 75(c); Vt. Bd. of Public Accountancy Administrative Rules 6.1, 10.7 (eff. June 1, 2014) (CVR 04-030-010)
records.flux_note: MULTIPLE, ACTIVE. (1) CHANGE JUST TOOK EFFECT: 2026 Act No. 119 (H.588), Sec. 10, rewrote 26 V.S.A. § 74c from 'SUBSTANTIAL EQUIVALENCY' to 'MOBILITY'. The act's own effective-date clause, Sec. 20(a), places Secs. 1-10 (accountants) 'on passage'; the enrolled act's last line states 'Date Governor signed bill: June 8, 2026'. Vermont's on-passage clause carries no supermajority/two-thirds condition, so no vote-count check was needed (bill status page publishes 0 roll calls). rule_changes_on = 2026-06-08. Verified against the enrolled PDF RENDERED TO IMAGES (not pdftotext) so strike/underline markup was preserved: the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service verification route and the Board's 'state the Board determines has licensure requirements substantially equivalent' state-level test are both STRICKEN; the underlined replacement requires the individual to hold a valid CPA license from ANY state AND to have passed the Uniform CPA exam AND to individually meet one of three education/experience combinations. That is an individual_criteria test, not nasba_state_level. (2) STALE CODIFIED TEXT: the Vermont Statutes Online page for § 74c still displays the PRE-Act-119 substantial-equivalency text and states on its face 'The Statutes below include the actions of the 2025 session of the General Assembly' - it has not been updated for the 2026 session. This is compilation lag, not a substantive conflict; the act text controls. (3) STALE BOARD GUIDANCE: OPR's 'Non-Resident Accounting Firm by Mobility' instructions (footer January 2026) still cite '26 V.S.A. § 74c. Substantial Equivalency' and require the firm's responsible individual to hold a license 'from a jurisdiction that has licensure requirements substantially equivalent' - superseded by Act 119. Conversely the CPA Application Instructions (January 2026) already list all three Act 119 education/experience pathways, i.e. they ran AHEAD of the statute (pre-Act-119 § 71a offered only the 150-hour route; (A) was repealed). (4) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON firm_registration_tax - CONSERVATIVE VALUE RECORDED: 26 V.S.A. § 74(b) says a firm with no Vermont office 'may otherwise practice public accounting as authorized under this chapter, and may use the title "CPA" or "CPA firm" without a registration' (subject to ownership, § 75(c) and § 74c conditions), which on its face exempts tax/non-attest work; but OPR's own CPA Application Instructions state flatly that under the mobility path 'the out of state firm must be licensed in Vermont under the Non-Resident Accounting Firm by Mobility application', and OPR operates license type '192 - Accounting Firm with Mobility' with a $275 initial / $115 biennial renewal fee. Statute permissive vs. board page restrictive on the same field, so the conservative (more-required) value true is recorded. (5) BOARD RULES PREDATE EVERYTHING: the Board's Administrative Rules are 'Effective: June 1, 2014' and still contain Part 7 'Temporary Registration' keyed to 26 V.S.A. § 74a, which was REPEALED by 2019 Act No. 30, § 9. Act 119 conditions § 74c(a)(2) on criteria met 'in accordance with rules adopted by the Board', but as of 2026-07-31 no accountancy rulemaking appears on Vermont's proposed-rules docket (secure.vermont.gov/SOS/rules, 27 rules posted, none accountancy), so implementing rules are outstanding.
records.data_gap_note: No board page squarely states that an out-of-state firm doing ONLY tax/non-attest work for a Vermont client is exempt from registration; the only board-published treatment of out-of-state firms is the 'Non-Resident Accounting Firm by Mobility' registration, which is presented without any service-type carve-out. firm_registration_tax is therefore recorded as true on the conservative rule, not because the statute says so - 26 V.S.A. § 74(b) reads the other way. Also: § 75(c) is only enabling ('The Board may by rule require'); the operative peer-review mandate lives in Rule 10.7 and in the board's application instructions, and the rules themselves are 12 years old and unamended for Act 119. UPDATE (verifier - CONTESTED FIELD, conservative value retained): firm_registration_tax=true is a genuine two-official-source conflict and must not be read as settled. The cited statute 26 V.S.A. 74(b) verbatim permits a no-office firm to "otherwise practice public accounting as authorized under this chapter, and may use the title CPA or CPA firm without a registration" subject to conditions - i.e. the STATUTE reads toward false - while OPR board guidance supports true. Per the conservative-value rule the restrictive value is retained (a wrongly permissive answer is the dangerous one) and rule_in_flux stays true, but downstream consumers should treat this specific field as contested, not verified. Fee figures corrected: the Vermont "Accounting Firm with Mobility" fees are $230 application / $460 biennial renewal (sole-proprietor variant $230/$230), NOT the $275/$115 recorded. citation_url caveat: Vermont Statutes Online 74c still serves PRE-Act-119 text with no subsection (g) under a "2025 session" banner - the enrolled Act 119 is the operative source. Fetcher notes reproduced independently: sos.vermont.gov 403s a default UA, and pdftotext-style extraction of Act 119 silently drops strike markup.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: 26 V.S.A. § 74c (as amended by Act 119 Sec. 10, eff. 2026-06-08) grants privileges of licensure without a Vermont license to an individual whose principal place of business is outside Vermont who (1) holds a valid CPA license from any state AND (2) has passed the Uniform CPA exam and met one of: post-baccalaureate degree with accounting concentration + 1 year public accounting experience; 150+ semester hours including a baccalaureate and 42 accounting hours + 1 year; or a baccalaureate with accounting concentration + 2 years. Act 119 added § 74c(g) grandfathering anyone who held a valid active out-of-state CPA license and had Vermont practice privileges as of December 31, 2024. Subsections (b)-(f) were left unchanged by the act (printed as '* * *'). § 74c(f) is explicit that the individual pays no fee and gives no notice. § 74c(b) imposes automatic consent conditions (jurisdiction, discipline, cease-practice, agent for service, scope limited to home-state scope). EQUIVALENCE TEST: individual_criteria - Act 119 deleted both the Board's state-level determination and the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service route; the CPA must now individually satisfy the enumerated exam + education/experience criteria. FIRM - ATTEST: 26 V.S.A. § 74(a)(3) requires registration where the firm has no Vermont office but performs services described in § 13(1)(A)(i), (iii) or (iv) - SAS audits/engagements, SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and PCAOB-standard engagements - for a client with a home office in Vermont. § 74c(c) independently bars a mobility individual from providing those three service classes except through a firm registered under § 74. OPR implements this through the 'Non-Resident Accounting Firm by Mobility' registration (license type 192). FIRM - TAX/NON-ATTEST: § 74(b) lets an office-less firm perform § 13(1)(A)(ii) (SSARS reviews/compilations), § 13(1)(A)(v) (other SSAE examinations, reviews and AUP) and § 13(3) (compilations), and 'otherwise practice public accounting' - which by § 13(10) includes 'the preparation of tax returns or the furnishing of advice on tax matters' - without a registration, if it meets the § 74(c)/(d) ownership rules, § 75(c) as applicable, and works through a § 74c individual. Board guidance contradicts this (see flux_note item 4); conservative value recorded. PEER REVIEW: this is a condition of the FIRM REGISTRATION, and is service-triggered, not blanket. Rule 10.7(a): if no attest services were performed, no peer review is required, and the firm must so state under penalty of perjury; firms that do perform attest must attest to a peer review within the preceding three years at each renewal/reinstatement, must notify the Board within 30 days of first performing an attest service and enroll in a Board-approved program (Rule 10.7(e)), and must undergo the review within 18 months of the first attest report year-end. OPR's Non-Resident Accounting Firm by Mobility instructions apply Rule 10.7 directly to out-of-state applicants performing attest functions in Vermont, and its renewal instructions require uploading the most recent peer review results. Separately, § 74(b)(2) conditions the NO-REGISTRATION route for office-less firms on meeting § 75(c) 'as applicable', so the peer-review condition also attaches to the unregistered-firm privilege. Statutory hook is § 75(c) (Board 'may by rule require ... as a condition to renewal of firm registrations under section 74'). NOT AMENDED BY ACT 119: §§ 74 and 75 were untouched; the act's accountancy sections are Sec. 8 (§ 13 definitions - repealed 'good character', revised 'principal place of business'), Sec. 9 (§ 71a licensure pathways) and Sec. 10 (§ 74c mobility).

records.citation: Va. Code §§ 54.1-4411 (individual practice privilege), 54.1-4412.1 (firms), as amended by 2025 Acts of Assembly cc. 523 (HB 2042) and 539 (SB 1042)
records.flux_note: The 2025 rewrite (cc. 523/539) already took effect: the official LIS bill history line reads 'Approved by Governor-Chapter 523 (Effective 07/01/25)', and the chaptered act contains NO delayed-effective-date enactment clause (only clause 2, a 280-day rulemaking mandate), so the mobility rewrite of 54.1-4411 became operative 2025-07-01 under Virginia's constitutional default. Press and even VBOA headlines say 'effective Jan. 1, 2026', but every 'January 1, 2026' in the act text sits inside 54.1-4409.2's licensure-pathway provisions ('For a person seeking licensure on or after January 1, 2026...'), not the mobility sections — verified against the chaptered text with strike markup preserved; no real source conflict. Implementing regulation 18VAC5-22 (education/experience) became effective 2025-10-22. A pending proposed regulation (Va. Register Vol. 42 Iss. 12, 2026-01-26) would amend 18VAC5-22-80/-130 on firm 51% ownership — it clarifies firm-license ownership rules and does not touch mobility/practice privilege. UPDATE (verifier): 2026 Acts of Assembly cc. 234 (HB 870) + 235 (SB 605), approved 2026-04-06, effective 2026-07-01 - amend 54.1-4400/54.1-4409.1 (licensure requirements, inactive/emeritus status) and do NOT touch 54.1-4411/54.1-4412.1 (the mobility/firm sections answered here), but enactment clause 2 mandates ANOTHER Board rulemaking within 280 days, so 18VAC5-22 will be amended again. The pending proposed 18VAC5-22 regulation (Va. Register Vol. 42 Iss. 12) is broader than firm-ownership cleanup: per the agency Town Hall statement it also clarifies the principal-place-of-business definition and firm peer-review enrollment - the exact boundary conditions of firm_registration_attest and peer_review_required. rule_in_flux kept false (mobility sections themselves not amended and automatic mobility is in force since 2025-07-01) but this rulemaking is field-adjacent; re-verify on adoption.
records.data_gap_note: notice_required, fee_required, and firm_registration_tax rest on explicit statutory text; the board's website has no dedicated practice-privilege/mobility guidance page (board-side confirmation of the new individual privilege comes from VBOA's Summer 2025 newsletter PDF on boa.virginia.gov; the License Reciprocity page is silent on practice privilege). Board firm pages independently confirm the firm-licensure scope. No board-page contradiction found — absence, not staleness.
records.notes: Virginia moved to open CPA=CPA mobility on 2025-07-01: any person holding a license in good standing from any state/territory/DC who has passed the CPA exam gets practice privilege 'without notice to the Board or payment of any fees' (54.1-4411(A)) — the former NASBA-style substantial-equivalency test was stricken. equivalence_test='other' because there is no equivalency test, but 54.1-4411(E) gives the Board a guard-rail power to revoke privileges state-wide if another state licenses without minimum acceptable qualifications (such individuals can still qualify individually). FIRMS: a Virginia firm license is required only for firms whose PRINCIPAL PLACE OF BUSINESS IS IN VIRGINIA providing attest/compilation/financial-statement-preparation services (54.1-4412.1(B)); an out-of-state firm 'is not required to obtain a Virginia license' for those services if it (1) is licensed where headquartered, (2) complies with subsection D, and (3/4) staffs the engagement with Virginia licensees or privilege-compliant CPAs or supervision by same (54.1-4412.1(C)). So firm_registration_attest=false (privilege with conditions, no registration/permit/notice mechanism exists). peer_review_required=true AS A CONDITION OF THAT NO-REGISTRATION PRIVILEGE: subsection C.2 requires compliance with subsection D, whose item 6 requires enrollment in the AICPA practice-monitoring (peer review) program if the firm's services are within its scope, plus FSBA participation. Tax/non-attest: the firm licensing requirement attaches only to attest/compilation/FSP services, so no registration for tax work (firm_registration_tax=false); an out-of-state firm may even use the CPA title in Virginia on its home-state license per 54.1-4412.1(F). Chapter 539 (SB 1042) is the identical Senate companion. Passage votes: House 99-0 (2025-02-03), Senate 39-0 (2025-02-17); approved by Governor 2025-03-24. UPDATE (verifier): House passage was 98-0 first vote, reconsidered and repassed 99-0 on 2025-02-03 - 99-0 is the operative final vote as recorded.

records.citation: RCW 18.04.350 (individual practice privileges); RCW 18.04.195(1) (firm license and firm-mobility exemptions); WAC 4-30-090 (practice privileges, as amended by WSR 25-10-028 eff. 2025-05-30)
records.flux_note: Washington completed its 2025-wave mobility rewrite by BOARD RULE, not statute: WSR 25-10-028 (filed 2025-04-29, effective 2025-05-30) rewrote WAC 4-30-090 from a substantial-equivalency test to individual criteria (current good-standing license from any US jurisdiction + at time of licensure bachelor's degree, passed Uniform CPA Exam, and one year of experience). A second rulemaking, WSR 25-21-108 (effective 2025-11-20), added three licensure pathways (incl. bachelor's + 2 yrs experience) and, per the board's rulemaking page, 'guardrails for the updated practice privilege rule'. The statute, RCW 18.04.350 (last amended 2024 c 13 / HB 1920, effective 2024-06-06 per the legislature's bill page), still frames mobility as a substantial-equivalency presumption with a state-level prong (1)(a) and individual prong (1)(b); the board page likewise still says 'qualifications are substantially equivalent' without stating the new WAC criteria. This is a framing mismatch, not an operative contradiction: WAC 4-30-010 defines substantial equivalency as 'a determination by the board or its designee', and WAC 4-30-090 is that determination. No pending 2025-26 accountancy bill found (2026 HB 1920 is unrelated). Watch for a statute-conformity bill and any further WAC 4-30-090 rulemaking.
records.data_gap_note: WSR 25-21-108 adopted-order text (the Nov 2025 'guardrails' language) was not itself fetched; verified instead against the compiled WAC certified 2025-11-12 and the live WAC 4-30-090 page, which show no post-2025-05-30 amendment to the practice-privilege section.
records.notes: INDIVIDUAL: Out-of-state CPAs (principal place of business outside WA) have full practice privileges with NO notice, NO fee, NO submission (RCW 18.04.350(2); WAC 4-30-090(3)). Operative qualification test since 2025-05-30 is individual criteria under WAC 4-30-090(1): good-standing license + (at initial licensure) bachelor's degree + passed CPA exam + one year experience. Conditions: consent to board jurisdiction/discipline, compliance with chapter and rules, cease on home-license invalidity, home board as agent for service (RCW 18.04.350(3)). No NASBA/NQAS reference in statute or the practice-privilege rule (NASBA designation appears only in the separate reciprocal-LICENSE rule, WAC 4-30-092(2)). FIRM-ATTEST: default rule is a firm WITHOUT a WA office offering/rendering attest services in WA must hold a WA firm license, UNLESS it meets ALL of RCW 18.04.195(1)(a)(ii)(A)-(D): simple-majority CPA ownership per (2)(a), compliance with the board's quality assurance review (QAR) program, services performed through practice-privilege individuals, and lawful authority in the individuals' home state — i.e., WA has full CPA firm mobility for attest, so firm_registration_attest=false for qualifying firms; a firm failing any condition MUST license (board application by affidavit under RCW 18.04.195(4)). Any firm WITH an office in WA performing attest or compilations must license regardless. FIRM-TAX/NONATTEST: no firm license needed for compilation and other nonattest services (including using the CPA/CPA-firm title) if performed through practice-privilege individuals and lawful in the home state (RCW 18.04.195(1)(b)); board page confirms. PEER REVIEW: true in the sense that meeting the board's QAR program (WA's peer-review program, RCW 18.04.055(9)) is a statutory CONDITION of the no-license attest firm-mobility exemption (RCW 18.04.195(1)(a)(ii)(B)) — it conditions the privilege, not a registration; it does not apply to the nonattest-only privilege. EQUIVALENCE: coded individual_criteria per the operative WAC 4-30-090 test; statute retains a delegated substantial-equivalency framework (see flux_note). Board firm-mobility page omits the ownership condition (A) that the statute imposes — statute governs; do not advise firms off the board page alone.

records.citation: W. Va. Code § 30-9-16 (substantial equivalency practice privileges), as amended by 2026 W. Va. Acts ch. 256 (Enrolled Comm. Sub. for H.B. 4088, eff. May 24, 2026); W. Va. Code §§ 30-9-17 (issuance and renewal of firm permits), 30-9-19 (issuance and renewal of authorizations), 30-9-2(3) (definition of attest services); W. Va. C.S.R. § 1-1-10 (Board legislative rule, eff. Mar. 29, 2024)
records.flux_note: WV is a 2026-wave state. Enrolled Comm. Sub. for H.B. 4088 (2026 RS, Chapter 256, Acts 2026) amended §§30-9-2, -5, -7, -8, -10, -11, -16 and -26 and rewrote §30-9-16 in full. Official bill-history effective-date line reads 'Effective Ninety Days from Passage - (May 24, 2026)' (final passage: House Roll No. 119 on 02/18/26, Senate Roll No. 202 on 02/23/26; approved by Governor 03/02/26). No immediate-effect/two-thirds question arises: the bill carried the ordinary 90-day clause and the Legislature itself published the operative date, so no vote-count check against a supermajority threshold was needed. The change is ALREADY IN EFFECT as of the 2026-07-31 verification date; the compiled §30-9-16 on code.wvlegislature.gov matches the enrolled act word-for-word (verified line by line), so there is no act-vs-compiled-text contradiction. Flux is nevertheless TRUE for two independent reasons. (1) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON THE EQUIVALENCE TEST: the still-compiled Board legislative rule, W. Va. C.S.R. §1-1-10.1 (1CSR1, filed and effective March 29, 2024, i.e. pre-H.B. 4088), provides that 'In determining whether the certification requirements of the other state or the individual are substantially equivalent to the certification requirements of the Uniform Accountancy Act, the Board is authorized to use the NQAS' -- a UAA-benchmarked test that expressly permits reliance on NASBA's National Qualification Appraisal Service and expressly permits a STATE-level ('the other state') determination. The current statute §30-9-16(a) instead conditions the privilege on the individual's own initial license requirements having 'met the certification requirements of §30-9-8 of this code' (West Virginia's own education/exam/experience statute), i.e. an individual-criteria test benchmarked to WV law rather than to the UAA or to a NASBA state-level appraisal. §30-9-2(38) still carries BOTH prongs of the older definition. Per the conservative-value instruction, equivalence_test is recorded as 'individual_criteria' (the value demanding more of the practitioner), not 'nasba_state_level'. (2) PENDING BOARD RULEMAKING: the Board filed a Notice of Public Comment with the WV Secretary of State on 2026-05-13 proposing a legislative-rule amendment to 1CSR1 to implement H.B. 4088; the written comment period closed 2026-06-26 at 5:00 PM. Redline review of that proposal (rendered to page images to preserve strike/underline markup, since text extraction loses it) shows the amendment is confined to education/experience pathway provisions -- §1-1-10.1 is changed only from 'the Board is authorized to use the NQAS' to 'the Board may use the NQAS', leaving the UAA/NQAS framing intact and NOT conforming the rule to the new §30-9-16(a) test. As a WV legislative rule it still requires legislative authorization (W. Va. Code ch. 64) before it can take effect, so the earliest operative date is the 2027 regular session. (3) STALE BOARD WEB GUIDANCE: the Board's Mobility page (Page Updated 9/4/2020) still describes mobility as running 'from a substantially equivalent state' (state-level framing), and the Board's CPA Licensure FAQ (Page Updated 9/24/2021) still recites the '150-hour academic specifications' and a flat one-year experience requirement, both superseded by H.B. 4088's three-pathway §30-9-8. The Board's /Licensing/SubstantialEquivalency.asp and /Licensing/PracticePrivileges.asp pages are unpopulated placeholders reading 'Add your new content here...' (last updated 11/22/2016).
records.data_gap_note: No Board page affirmatively restates the post-H.B. 4088 §30-9-16(a) individual test; the two Board pages nominally dedicated to it (Licensing/SubstantialEquivalency.asp, Licensing/PracticePrivileges.asp) are empty placeholders. The equivalence_test value therefore rests on the codified statute plus the acknowledged conflict with the compiled rule, not on affirmative Board guidance. Separately, the Board-side leg for notice_required/fee_required is corroborative rather than explicit: the Mobility page states the privilege permits practice 'without obtaining a license to practice' and flags an Authorization only for attest, but does not use the words 'no notice or fee'; the explicit 'no notice, fee, or other submission is required' language comes from the statute. Also unresolved: W. Va. Code §30-9-2(3)(E) attest services (SSAE examinations, reviews and agreed-upon-procedures engagements other than prospective-financial-information examinations) are listed neither in §30-9-17(b)(3) (permit required) nor in §30-9-17(c) (permit-free with conditions), so the statute does not say whether an out-of-state firm needs a WV permit to perform a subparagraph (E) engagement for a WV-home-office client. Treat (E) engagements as unresolved, not as exempt.
records.notes:
INDIVIDUAL: W. Va. Code §30-9-16 grants practice privileges by two routes. §30-9-16(a) (forward-looking): an individual whose principal place of business is outside WV, holding a valid out-of-state certificate in good standing, whose initial license requirements met the certification requirements of §30-9-8, has all rights and privileges of a WV certificate holder without obtaining a certificate. §30-9-16(b) (grandfather): an individual whose principal place of business is outside WV and who held a valid CPA license from any state as of December 31, 2025 continues to have practice privileges regardless of the §30-9-8 comparison -- effectively CPA=CPA for the pre-2026 licensee population. §30-9-16(c) is explicit that no notice, fee, or other submission is required. Consent conditions attach automatically under §30-9-16(d)-(e): WV Board jurisdiction, appointment of the issuing state board as agent for service of process, and a duty to cease practice if the home-state certificate lapses. Note §30-9-16 is the mobility section; the starting hint pointing to §30-9-18 was wrong (§30-9-18 is notification of changes in firm ownership).

IMPORTANT INDIVIDUAL CARVE-OUT (do not read notice_required=false as covering attest): under §30-9-16(f) a mobility practitioner may perform an SAS audit, an SSAE examination of prospective financial information, or a PCAOB engagement for an entity with its home office in WV ONLY through a firm holding both a §30-9-17 permit and a §30-9-19 authorization. Under §30-9-16(g) a sole INDIVIDUAL PRACTITIONER who is also a substantial equivalency practitioner may perform those services without a firm permit but MUST obtain the §30-9-19 authorization -- which carries an application fee (§30-9-19(h)) and a peer-review condition (§30-9-19(f)(2)). So the no-notice/no-fee privilege is a non-attest privilege; an out-of-state sole practitioner doing WV attest work must register and pay.

FIRM / ATTEST: §30-9-17(b)(3) requires a permit for any firm with no WV office that performs, for a client with its home office in WV, the attest services in §30-9-2(3)(A) (SAS audits), (C) (SSAE examinations of prospective financial information) or (D) (PCAOB engagements). §30-9-19(a) separately requires an authorization to provide attest or compilation services. The Board's firm-mobility page confirms an 'Application for Firm Permit with Authorization to Perform Attestation Services' is required for exactly those three service types.

FIRM / TAX AND OTHER NON-ATTEST: §30-9-17(d) exempts an out-of-state firm with no WV office that performs no attest or compilation services for a WV-home-office client -- it may perform other professional services (tax, consulting, advisory) and use the 'CPA'/'CPA firm' title without a WV permit, but the exemption is CONDITIONAL: the services must be performed through an individual holding §30-9-16 practice privileges, and the firm must be able lawfully to perform the services in the state where those individuals have their principal place of business. This is a genuine non-attest exemption, independently confirmed on the Board's own Firm Mobility page; it was NOT inferred from the attest rule.

MIDDLE TIER (SSARS reviews and compilations): §30-9-17(c) lets an out-of-state firm with no WV office perform §30-9-2(3)(B) SSARS reviews and §30-9-2(12) compilations for a WV-home-office client, and use the CPA title, without a permit -- but only if it meets firm ownership requirements, IS UNDERGOING A CONFORMING PEER REVIEW PROGRAM, and performs the services through an individual with §30-9-16 practice privileges. §30-9-19(a) correspondingly excuses the authorization for such firms and for substantial equivalency practitioners issuing compilation reports who meet §30-9-19(f)(1)-(2).

PEER REVIEW -- WHICH KIND: it operates BOTH ways in WV, and both are recorded as true. (i) As a condition of the firm registration/authorization: §30-9-19(d)(3) requires, for issuance of an authorization to a permit holder, that 'The permit holder is undergoing a peer review program that conforms with applicable rules'; §30-9-19(f)(2) imposes the same on an individual practitioner's authorization. (ii) As a condition of the NO-REGISTRATION privilege: §30-9-17(c) conditions the permit-free SSARS-review/compilation route for out-of-state firms on the firm 'undergoing a peer review program that conforms with applicable rules.' Program acceptability is governed by W. Va. C.S.R. §1-1-8; the Board accepts the AICPA program administered by the WV Society of CPAs or a program it deems comparable.

EQUIVALENCE TEST: recorded as individual_criteria on the strength of §30-9-16(a)'s reference to §30-9-8, over the contrary UAA/NQAS framing surviving in the unamended W. Va. C.S.R. §1-1-10.1 -- see flux_note. §30-9-8 as amended by H.B. 4088 now offers three pathways (post-baccalaureate degree, or baccalaureate + 30 semester hours, each with 1 year of experience; or baccalaureate alone with 2 years of experience), the standard 2025-26-wave bachelor's+2yr pairing.

RECIPROCAL CERTIFICATE TRIGGER (mobility ends here): per the Board's Mobility page, a CPA from another jurisdiction who intends to perform accounting services in WV and who is a WV resident, has established a business in WV, or is an employee of a WV firm or business entity, must first apply for a reciprocal certificate. This tracks the 'principal place of business is not in this state' precondition in §30-9-16(a)-(b).

OTHER 2026 BILL: S.B. 532 (2026 RS) was a similar accountancy vehicle that passed the Senate (Roll No. 44) but died in House Finance on 02/05/26; H.B. 4088 is the enacted vehicle. §§30-9-17 and 30-9-19 were not touched by either bill and have not been amended since 2008 (Enrolled C.S. for H.B. 4494).

records.citation: Wis. Stat. § 442.025(4) (individual practice privilege, as amended by 2025 Wis. Act 166); Wis. Stat. § 442.08(2) and Wis. Admin. Code §§ Accy 5.101-5.102 (firm licensure); Wis. Stat. § 442.087 and Wis. Admin. Code § Accy 6.101 (peer review)
records.flux_note: Wisconsin completed its mobility rewrite in the 2025-26 wave: 2025 Wis. Act 166 (2025 AB 696; Assembly passed 2026-02-10, Senate concurred 2026-02-11, approved 2026-04-02, published 2026-04-03) took effect 2026-04-04 under its own clause 'Notwithstanding s. 227.265, this act takes effect on the day after publication' (no supermajority condition; Wisconsin uses publication-based effectiveness, and the LRB-inserted grandfather date of April 3, 2026 = day before effective date confirms 2026-04-04). It replaced the former NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test in s. 442.025(4)(a)2., 2023 stats., with an individual-criteria test ('has met requirements similar to those under s. 442.04(5)(b)' - education/exam/experience, now including a bachelor's+2yr pathway) plus a grandfather clause preserving privileges held as of 2026-04-03. Act 166 also amended Wis. Admin. Code ch. Accy 2 directly (Register April 2026 No. 844, eff. 4-4-26), so statute and compiled admin code are aligned; no pending mobility rulemaking found. Firm-licensure and peer-review provisions (442.08, 442.087, Accy 5, Accy 6) were NOT changed by Act 166.
records.data_gap_note: DSPS/board web pages contain NO guidance on out-of-state practice privilege or Act 166 mobility (searched profession page, board page, rules page) - individual-privilege fields therefore rest on the codified statute alone (single_source); firm-registration and peer-review fields are effectively dual-sourced (Accy 5/442.08 plus DSPS Form #125). notice_required/fee_required=false are absence findings: s. 442.025 grants a complete exemption ('does not require a certificate or license') with deemed-consent conditions in (4)(b) and no notice/registration/fee mechanism anywhere in ch. 442 for privilege holders. firm_registration_tax=true is the CONSERVATIVE reading: Accy 5.101's trigger ('if any member of the firm practices as a certified public accountant in Wisconsin') and DSPS Form #125 ('practicing accounting in Wisconsin') are service-agnostic, but no provision expressly addresses an out-of-state firm with no WI office whose members practice only under the s. 442.025(4) privilege in non-attest capacities; Accy 5.302 says such firms 'may be licensed' via a designated WI-licensed compliance CPA.
records.notes: Scheme: s. 442.025(4) exempts from licensure a person whose principal place of business or residence is not in Wisconsin who holds a valid CPA certificate/license from another state and 'has met requirements similar to those under s. 442.04(5)(b)' (individual criteria), with a grandfather for anyone who had WI practice privileges under the 2023 stats as of 2026-04-03; conditions are deemed consents (board jurisdiction/discipline, compliance with ch. 442, home-state board as agent for service) - no notice filing, no fee. Firms: Wisconsin is NOT a UAA sec. 7 no-notice firm-mobility state. Accy 5.101 requires firm licensure if any member practices as a CPA in Wisconsin and provides that a CPA 'may only provide attest services ... in a CPA firm that has a firm license'; Accy 5.302 provides the licensure route for firms without a WI office (designated WI-licensed compliance CPA); firm license fee $43 (DSPS Form #125, via LicensE portal). Peer review is a condition of the firm license: initial application must demonstrate satisfaction of s. 442.087/ch. Accy 6 (Accy 5.102(3)(d)); renewal requires a peer review within the preceding 3 years for firms providing or offering attest services (s. 442.087(2), Accy 6.101(1)); firms that do not offer or perform attest services are exempt but must claim the exemption at renewal (Accy 6.101(2)-(3)). So peer review conditions the firm registration (attest-performing firms), not the individual privilege. Individual privilege quotes 'all the privileges of licensees,' which via Accy 5.101 means attest may only be provided through a licensed firm. UPDATE (verifier): 2025-26 rulemaking completeness - CR 24-071 (Accy 2 exam credit window 18->30 months, eff. 2025-05-01) also ran; affects no recorded field.

records.citation: W.S. 33-3-116 (certified public accountant; holders of certificates in sister states / practice privileges); W.S. 33-3-118(b)(xiii)-(xvi) (certified public accountant firms; permit requirement and out-of-state firm exemptions); W.S. 33-3-132 (practice monitoring program); Wyoming Administrative Rules, Board of Certified Public Accountants ch. 10 (Practice Privileges, eff. 10/28/2019), ch. 4 (Permits, eff. 10/28/2019), ch. 9 (Peer Review, eff. 04/07/2022)
records.data_gap_note: Board-page coverage of the ATTEST permit carve-out is thin. The board's mobility page states flatly that out-of-state firms and individuals may serve Wyoming clients 'without obtaining or maintaining a Wyoming certificate or permit,' and only obliquely acknowledges the carve-out ('If the firm provides services which requires licensure, each firm is required to designate a certificate holder of some state to be responsible for the proper registration of the firm'). The affirmative permit requirement for audits / SSAE prospective-financial-information examinations / PCAOB engagements rests on the codified statute (W.S. 33-3-116(a)(iv)) and Board Rule ch. 4 s.2(a), plus the board's Initial Firm Registration page requiring a peer review acceptance letter when the scope of practice includes Audits/Attest, SSAE, PCAOB, Reviews or Compilations. Treated as incomplete board guidance rather than a source contradiction, because the board page expressly incorporates 'W.S. 33-3-116 and Chapter 10 of Board rules and regulations' by reference. Practitioners relying on the board page alone would be misled; a CPA compliance product should surface the statutory carve-out, not the board summary.
records.notes: STRUCTURE (classic pre-2025 UAA, unchanged): (1) INDIVIDUAL - W.S. 33-3-116(a)(i) grants automatic practice privilege to a CPA whose principal place of business is outside Wyoming and who is licensed in a state the board or its designee (NASBA) has determined substantially equivalent, with express statutory language that 'no notice, fee or other submission shall be required.' W.S. 33-3-116(a)(ii) supplies an alternate route for licensees of non-equivalent states who individually obtain verification of substantial equivalency from the board or its designee. Board Rule ch. 10 s.2-s.3 implements this via NASBA's National Qualification Service and says such persons 'may practice in Wyoming without obtaining a Wyoming certificate or paying a fee.' equivalence_test recorded as nasba_state_level because the operative default is NASBA/NQAS state-level equivalency; the statutory individual-verification alternative in 33-3-116(a)(ii) exists but is secondary, and Board Rule ch. 10 s.4 describes only a narrow individual route (pre-1/1/2012 exam passers). Consent conditions attach automatically (33-3-116(a)(iii)): jurisdiction/disciplinary authority of the board, compliance with the act and rules, cease practice if the home license lapses, and appointment of the home board as agent for service of process. (2) FIRM - ATTEST: recorded TRUE, but the requirement is a SUBSET, not blanket. W.S. 33-3-116(a)(iv) requires an individual with practice privileges to provide services only through a firm HOLDING A WYOMING PERMIT when performing, for an entity with its home office in Wyoming: (A) any financial statement audit or other SAS engagement, (B) any SSAE examination of prospective financial information, or (C) any PCAOB-standards engagement. W.S. 33-3-118(b)(xiv) lets an out-of-state firm with no Wyoming office perform other attest services (including SSARS reviews and other SSAE engagements) and compilations for a Wyoming home-office client WITHOUT a permit, provided it meets the majority-CPA-ownership test of (b)(xvi), complies with W.S. 33-3-132 (practice monitoring/peer review), and performs through an individual with practice privileges. Board Rule ch. 4 s.2(a) adds that an out-of-state firm performing compilations for a Wyoming home-office client that is NOT subject to AICPA or some state's peer review requirements MUST register and obtain a permit. (3) FIRM - TAX/NON-ATTEST: recorded FALSE. W.S. 33-3-118(b)(xv) permits a firm not caught by (xiii) or (xiv) to perform other professional services under the CPA/CPA-firm title without a permit if it works through an individual with practice privileges and could lawfully perform those services in that individual's principal-place-of-business state. (4) PEER REVIEW: recorded TRUE and it operates BOTH ways in Wyoming - it is a condition of the permit (Board Rule ch. 9 s.3(a); the board's Initial Firm Registration page requires the most recent peer review acceptance letter and reviewer's report when the scope includes Audits/Attest, SSAE, PCAOB, Reviews or Compilations) AND a condition of the no-permit out-of-state attest/compilation privilege (W.S. 33-3-118(b)(xiv)(A) conditions the exemption on compliance with W.S. 33-3-132, and Board Rule ch. 9 s.3(a)(i) expressly reaches 'CPA firms who perform accounting and auditing engagements ... for clients with a home office in Wyoming'). Firms whose only SSARS service is preparation of financial statements are exempt from enrollment (ch. 9 s.3(a)(ii)). Nevada Society of CPAs is Wyoming's peer review administering entity. (5) NO 2025-26 CHANGE. Contrary to the starting hint, Wyoming did NOT enact a 2025 pathway/mobility bill. Verified three ways: (a) the officially compiled Title 33 PDF on wyoleg.gov, HTTP Last-Modified Fri, 08 May 2026 22:33:19 GMT (i.e. compiled AFTER the 2026 Budget Session adjourned 2026-03-11), carries no session-law amendment note later than 'Laws 2019, ch. 2' anywhere in chapter 3 (Accountants), while showing 'Laws 2025, ch. 81' amendments elsewhere in Title 33 - so the compilation is current and chapter 3 is untouched; (b) the LSO Subject Cross Index for the 2025 General Session (dated 2/6/2025) and for the 2026 Budget Session (dated 3/30/2026) contain no 'Accountants' subheading under Professions and Occupations and no occurrence of the string 'accountan' at all; (c) the board's own Statute & Rules page still lists chapter effective dates of 10/28/19 (ch. 1, 3, 4, 8, 10), 8/8/24 (ch. 2, Examination - the newest), 7/15/20 (ch. 5), 3/4/13 (ch. 6, 11), 10/31/11 (ch. 7), 4/7/22 (ch. 9) - no 2025-26 rulemaking in the mobility, firm-permit or peer-review chapters. Wyoming's next general session convenes January 2027; the Joint Labor, Health & Social Services interim committee's 2026 topics do not include accountancy. FORWARD RISK (not flux, but monitor): Wyoming's substantial-equivalency yardstick in W.S. 33-3-116(c)(i)(A) still hard-codes 150 semester hours. As other states license under bachelor's+2-years pathways, whether those licensees qualify in Wyoming turns entirely on NASBA/NQAS determinations under 33-3-116(a)(i) or on individual verification under 33-3-116(a)(ii) - Wyoming has not amended its own text to accommodate the new pathways.
